title: 429 retry-after capped at 10s — quota exhaustion retried instead of surfaced
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Other

### 💻 Operating System

Other

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Other

### 📌 Version

latest (static analysis — not version-specific)

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome, Other

### 🐛 What happened?

executeWithRetry in packages/model-runtime/src/providers/githubCopilot/index.ts reads retry-after correctly but caps it at 10 seconds:

Math.min(retryAfter, 10_000)

A retry-after of 3 hours (quota exhaustion) gets truncated to 10 seconds and retried 3 times instead of surfacing
immediately as unrecoverable.


### 📷 How to reproduce it?

Static analysis finding in src/providers/githubCopilot/index.ts

Trigger a quota exhaustion 429 with retry-after > 300s.

Observe that executeWithRetry caps the delay at 10s and retries MAX_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES times instead of surfacing.


### 🚦 What it should be?

retry-after above a threshold should surface immediately as quota exhaustion, not consume retry attempts.

Suggested fix:
const STOP_THRESHOLD_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000
if (retryAfter && retryAfter > STOP_THRESHOLD_MS) {
    throw this.mapError(error)
}


### 📝 Additional Information

Documented across production systems:
[github.com/SirBrenton/pitstop-truth](https://github.com/SirBrenton/pitstop-truth)

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

**Affects:** LobeHub v2.1.47 (and likely earlier versions)                                        
**Model:** Any agent backed by `gemini-3-flash-preview` (and other Gemini 3+ models)              
**Endpoint:** `POST /api/v1/responses` (streaming and non-streaming)   

### 🚦 What it should be?

 There are two layers involved:

  Layer 1 — already fixed in #10470:                                                                
  packages/model-runtime/src/core/streams/google/index.ts forces Gemini 3 models into multimodal
  processing mode, which emits content_part SSE events (with partType: 'text') instead of the       
  standard text events:                        
                                                                                                    
  // google/index.ts                           
  const isGemini3Model = modelVersion.includes('gemini-3') ||
  modelVersion.includes('image-preview');                                                           
  const shouldUseMultimodalProcessing = (...isGemini3Model) && ...;
                                                                                                    
  Layer 2 — not yet fixed:                     
  src/server/modules/AgentRuntime/RuntimeExecutors.ts sets up the ChatStreamCallbacks object passed 
  to the model runtime. The interface already defines onContentPart, but the callback is never      
  registered:                                  
                                                                                                    
  // RuntimeExecutors.ts — current code        
  callback: {                                  
    onGrounding: async (e) => { ... },
    onText: async (text) => { textBuffer += text; ... },                                            
    onThinking: async (reasoning) => { ... },                                                       
    onError: async (e) => { ... },                                                                  
    // ← onContentPart is missing here                                                              
  }                                                                                                 
                                               
  When content_part events arrive from the Google stream, protocol.ts calls                         
  callbacks.onContentPart?.(data) — but since it was never registered, the call is a no-op. Text
  content goes into the void, textBuffer stays empty, and stream_chunk events are never published. 

### 📝 Additional Information

Register onContentPart in createRuntimeExecutors, before onText:
                                                                                                    
  onContentPart: async (data) => {                                                                  
    // Handle multimodal content_part events emitted by Gemini 3+ models.
    // These carry the same text payload as onText but via a different callback.                    
    if (data.partType === 'text' && data.content) {                                                 
      content += data.content;                                                                      
      textBuffer += data.content;                                                                   
      if (!textBufferTimer) {                                                                       
        textBufferTimer = setTimeout(async () => {
          await flushTextBuffer();                                                                  
          textBufferTimer = null;                                                                   
        }, BUFFER_INTERVAL);                   
      }                                                                                             
    }                                          
  },                                           
                                                                                                    
  This mirrors the existing onText accumulation logic exactly.

### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?

None

title: verifyQStashSignature returns false instead of true when signing keys   are not configured, silently breaking all self-hosted bot (Feishu/WeChat)        replies
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Web (Desktop Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

Ubuntu

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Other

### 📌 Version

2.1.47

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

In self-hosted Docker deployments without Upstash QStash configured, Feishu  
  and WeChat bot channels receive messages but the bot never replies. No errors 
  appear in Docker logs — messages are silently dropped.    
                                                                                
  After analyzing the source code, the root cause is a one-line bug in          
  src/libs/qstash/index.ts line 43.                                            
                                                                                
  verifyQStashSignature has a comment that says:                                
  ▎ Returns true if signing keys are not configured (verification skipped) or  
  signature is valid.                                                           
                                                            
  But the actual code returns false:                                            
                                                                                
  if (!currentSigningKey || !nextSigningKey) {                                 
    log('QStash signature verification disabled (no signing keys configured)'); 
    return false; // ← should be true                                           
  }                                                                             
                                                                                
  This causes /api/agent/webhooks/bot-callback to always return 401 for         
  self-hosted deployments, silently dropping all bot replies.  

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

                                                                           
  1. Deploy LobeHub via Docker without setting QSTASH_TOKEN,
  QSTASH_CURRENT_SIGNING_KEY, or QSTASH_NEXT_SIGNING_KEY                        
  2. Bind a Feishu or WeChat channel to an Agent            
  3. Send a message from Feishu/WeChat                                          
  4. Bot never replies; no errors in Docker logs                                
                                                  

### 🚦 What it should be?

                                                                       
  The bot should reply normally. In local mode (no QStash),                    
  verifyQStashSignature should return true to skip signature verification,      
  allowing the internal bot-callback to complete.           
                                                                                
  The full broken flow:                                                         
  1. Feishu sends message → LarkAdapter.handleWebhook() ✅                     
  2. chat.processMessage() triggers ✅                                          
  3. LocalQueueServiceImpl executes agent step ✅           
  4. AgentRuntimeService calls /api/agent/webhooks/bot-callback internally ✅   
  5. verifyQStashSignature() returns false → 401 ❌ → reply dropped             
                                                                                
  Fix: Change return false to return true on line 43 of                         
  src/libs/qstash/index.ts.                                                     
                                                                                
  Note: Setting the signing keys does not work around this — the bot-callback is
   an internal call with no Upstash signature header, so verification will still
   fail.                                                                        
                       

### 📝 Additional Information

_No response_

No, but I am happy to help test the fix

title: Desktop: execTask child session gets stuck / fails before output, but works after manual "Regenerate"
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Desktop App (Electron)

### 💻 Operating System

macOS

_No response_

### 📌 Version

2.1.47;2.1.48

Other

### 🐛 What happened?

## Description

On macOS desktop (Apple Silicon, ARM dmg app), `execTask` creates a child session/thread but the child session often gets stuck with no output, or fails before producing any visible LobeHub response.

However, if I open that child session and click **Regenerate**, the same session can then respond normally.

This makes it look like the model itself is available and usable, but the **automatic async task execution path** is failing while the **manual foreground regenerate path** works.

---

## Environment

- Platform: macOS
- Hardware: Apple Silicon (ARM)
- App install method: downloaded and launched from the ARM `.dmg`
- Launch method: normal app launch by clicking, not via terminal
- PATH / shell env manually configured: No
- Model provider setup: custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint
- Model name: `gpt-5.4`
- Base URL: custom/self-hosted URL
- App version: _(please fill in exact version from About page)_

---

## Reproduction Steps

1. Open the desktop app.
2. Configure and use a custom OpenAI-compatible model endpoint with model name `gpt-5.4`.
3. Confirm that normal chat works.
4. Trigger an async task via `execTask` (even a minimal task can reproduce this).
   - Example instruction:
     - `Output exactly one line: OK`
5. Observe that a child task session/thread is created.
6. In many cases, the child session:
   - stays stuck without output, or
   - fails before showing any visible response.
7. Open that child session manually and click **Regenerate**.
8. Observe that the child session can then produce normal output.

---

## Expected Behavior

`execTask` should automatically execute the child session and produce output without requiring any manual interaction.

---

## Actual Behavior

The child task session is created, but automatic execution does not complete correctly.
Manual **Regenerate** inside that child session often makes it work.

---

## Frequency

Reproducible multiple times.

---

## Additional Observations

- Normal chat works with the same model configuration.
- Manual regenerate inside the child session also works.
- The issue seems specific to the **automatic `execTask` execution path**.
- In some cases, the UI shows an error similar to:

Task failed: [object Object]

title: [Security] LobeHub lacks permission controls to prevent LLMs from damaging the system!!!
body: ### 📱 Client Type Desktop App (Electron) ### 💻 Operating System macOS ### 📦 Deployment Platform Self hosting Docker ### 📌 Version v2.1.48 ### 🌐 Browser Safari ### 🐛 What happened? LobeHub allows models to freely activate any tool, including destructive ones. 1. Silently fall back from Cloud Sandbox to the local system *(LobeHub should stop the model here — this is the simplest safeguard without relying on third-party command checks)* 2. Bypass safety warnings (e.g., PEP 668 restriction) 3. Force-install Python packages into the global environment, which could lead to installing malicious packages. ### 📷 How to reproduce it? 1. **Launch LobeHub Desktop** (self-hosted version is required, as LobeHub will automatically attempt Cloud Sandbox before falling back to local system) 2. **Issue a command that requires filesystem access** *Example: Ask the model to "create lobe.docx to introduce yourself"* ### 🚦 What it should be? LobeHub attempts to use Cloud Sandbox first, then silently falls back to the local system — without requesting user permission. If blocked by safeguards like PEP 668, it will bypass these warnings and force-install Python packages into the global environment, which could lead to installing malicious packages. ### 📝 Additional Information Any Tool activation **requires** user confirmation. ### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR? title: [Bug] Turbopack bundles chat module into two separate chunks, causing chat-sdk to initialize twice (duplicate QQ bot replies)
body:
### 💻 Operating System

Other Linux

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 🔧 Deployment Mode

server db (lobehub/lobehub image)

### 📌 Version

canary (Next.js 16.2.3) — also reproducible on latest stable

### 🌐 Browser

N/A (QQ Bot feature)

### 🐛 Bug Description

When using the built-in QQ Bot (chat-sdk) feature with Docker deployment, the bot sends **every reply twice** with identical content but different response times (e.g., 5s and 8s).

Root cause: Turbopack compiles the `@lobehub/chat` module into **two independent chunks** with separate module-level state. The module's singleton pattern (`var iM = null`) fails because each chunk maintains its own copy of `iM`.

**Chunk A** (`0-1h_chat_dist_index_0stqjes.js`):
- Loaded by `instrumentation.js` → `src_0t6_v1o._.js`

**Chunk B** (`0-1h_chat_dist_index_0sviq1g.js`):
- Loaded by `/api/agent/gateway/start/route.js` (triggered by `startServer.js`)

Both chunks execute `new Chat(...)` independently → two WebSocket connections to QQ → duplicate message handling.

### 📷 Reproduction Steps

1. Deploy `lobehub/lobehub` (canary or stable) with Docker
2. Configure a QQ Bot in the web UI
3. Restart the container and observe logs:

```
[chat-sdk] Initializing chat instance...    ← simultaneous!
[chat-sdk] Initializing chat instance...    ← 
[chat-sdk:qq] Initialized QQ adapter (botUserId=xxx)
[chat-sdk] Chat instance initialized { adapters: [ 'qq' ] }
[chat-sdk:qq] Gateway URL: wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket (shards: 1)
[chat-sdk:qq] WebSocket connected (resume=false)
[chat-sdk:qq] Ready: session_id=xxx user=xxx
[chat-sdk:qq] Initialized QQ adapter (botUserId=xxx)
[chat-sdk] Chat instance initialized { adapters: [ 'qq' ] }
[chat-sdk:qq] Gateway URL: wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket (shards: 1)
[chat-sdk:qq] WebSocket connected (resume=false)
[chat-sdk:qq] Invalid session (canResume=false)
[chat-sdk:qq] WebSocket closed: code=4903 reason=create session error
```

4. Send a message to the bot → receives two identical replies

### Evidence

**Process inspection** — only one container, one Node process + one next-server worker:
```
PID   USER     TIME  COMMAND
  1   nextjs   0:00  {MainThread} /bin/node /app/startServer.js
 28   nextjs   1:05  next-server (v16.2.3)
```

**Two independent chunks confirmed:**
```bash
# Chunk loaded by instrumentation
grep -rl "0stqjes" /app/.next/server/
# → src_0t6_v1o._.js (instrumentation chunk)
# → [root-of-the-server]__0-dwdb8._.js

# Chunk loaded by API routes
grep -rl "0sviq1g" /app/.next/server/app/
# → gateway/start/route.js, gateway/route.js, and many other routes
```

**Creative content proves single LLM call:** When asking the bot to write a poem, both replies contain the exact same poem (word-for-word), proving the LLM was called once but the result was sent twice.

### 🚦 Expected Behavior

`chat-sdk` should only be initialized once. The singleton pattern should work across chunk boundaries.

### Suggested Fix

Replace the module-level singleton with a `globalThis`-based singleton to survive Turbopack chunk duplication:

```javascript
// Current (broken across chunks):
var iM = null;

// Fix:
var iM = globalThis.__lobechat_chat_singleton || null;
// ... and in registerSingleton():
globalThis.__lobechat_chat_singleton = this;
```

Alternatively, configure Turbopack to treat the chat module as a shared/singleton chunk that is never duplicated.

### 📝 Additional Information

- The second instance's WebSocket connection is rejected by QQ server with `code=4903 reason=create session error`, but both instances still register message handlers
- The `startServer.js` entrypoint calls `POST /api/agent/gateway/start` (without await) to trigger initialization, while `instrumentation.js` independently loads the chat module at server startup — these two paths load different chunk copies

title: [Deploy] OOM and OOM again
body: Hello everyone, I’ve recently been unable to complete the build correctly in Vercel. title: [Bug] readLocalFile `loc` parameter is displayed in UI but ignored in actual content — always returns from line 0
body:
## 🐛 Bug Description

The `readLocalFile` tool accepts a `loc: [startLine, endLine]` parameter to read a specific
line range from a local file. The UI correctly displays the specified range next to the file
path (e.g., "L191–"), but the **actual returned content always starts from line 0**,
regardless of what `loc` value is passed. As a result, files longer than 200 lines **cannot
be read beyond the first 200 lines** through any workaround.

---

## ✅ Validations

- [x] Checked for existing duplicate issues
- [x] This is a LobeHub Desktop issue, not a third-party provider issue
- [x] This is a reproducible bug

---

## 📱 Client Type

- [x] Desktop (Electron)

## 💻 Operating System

- Windows 11

## 📌 Version

v2.1.49 (confirmed still present)

---

## 🔁 Reproduction Steps

1. Enable the Local System built-in tool on any agent.
2. Ask the agent to read a local `.md` file with **more than 200 lines**.
3. Call `readLocalFile(path)` with no `loc` → returns content from line 0 ✓ (expected default).
4. Call `readLocalFile(path, loc=[190, 220])` → UI header shows **"lines 190–220"**, but content **still starts from line 0** ✗.
5. Call `readLocalFile(path, loc=[200, 400])` → same result, content still starts from line 0 ✗.
6. All three calls return **identical content**, making it impossible to read anything past line 200.

---

## 🚦 Expected vs Actual

| Call | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `readLocalFile(path)` | Lines 0–200 | Lines 0–200 ✅ |
| `readLocalFile(path, loc=[200, 400])` | Lines 200–400 | Lines 0–200 ❌ |
| `readLocalFile(path, loc=[190, 220])` | Lines 190–220 | Lines 0–200 ❌ |

---

## 🔍 Root Cause Analysis

Two related PRs help explain this bug:

- **PR #11485** (Jan 14, 2026) — `style: update readFile content`
  Modified only the **frontend UI** (`ReadLocalFile/index.tsx`) to display the `loc` range
  in the Inspector. **No changes were made to the backend file reading logic.**
  This created a disconnect: the UI shows the correct range, but the backend ignores it.

- **PR #12022** (Feb 1, 2026) — `style: improve local-system tool implement`
  Included commits: `improve local system ability`, `refactor the LocalFileCtr.ts result`.
  A significant refactor of the file reading implementation, after which users report
  the `loc` parameter stopped working.

The suspected root cause: in `LocalFileCtr.ts`, the `loc` parameter is **passed to
metadata/logger** but **not applied to slice the actual file content** before returning.

---

## 🛠 Suggested Fix

Ensure `loc` is applied to slice the content in the backend handler.

```typescript
// In LocalFileCtr.ts — readLocalFile handler
const rawContent = await loadFile(filePath);
const allLines = rawContent.split('\n');
const totalLineCount = allLines.length;

const [startLine = 0, endLine = 200] = loc ?? [0, 200];
const slicedContent = allLines.slice(startLine, endLine).join('\n');

return {
  content: slicedContent,   // ← Currently missing
  totalLineCount,
  loc: [startLine, endLine],
};
```

---

body:
### 📱 Client Type

Desktop App (Electron)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

Zeabur

### 📌 Version

 v2.1.49

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

## Bug Description

The built-in `readLocalFile` tool's `loc` parameter does not respect the **start line**.
No matter what start line is specified, the tool always returns content beginning from **line 1** of the file.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a conversation with a Local System tool enabled agent
2. Ask the agent to read a file with a specific line range, e.g. `loc: [180, 210]`
3. Observe that the returned content starts from line 1 instead of line 180

## Expected Behavior

When calling `readLocalFile` with `loc: [180, 210]`, the tool should return **only lines 180 to 210** of the file.

## Actual Behavior

The tool ignores the start line and always returns content **starting from line 1**, regardless of the specified range.
The end line also appears to be ignored — the tool returns a fixed default chunk from the beginning of the file.

## Reproduction Example

- File: `D:\AI-Scientist-v2-AD8\launch_scientist_bfts.py` (364 lines total)
- Called with: `loc: [180, 210]`
- Expected: lines 180–210
- Actual: lines 1–~200 (always from the beginning)

## Additional Context

- Tried multiple different start values: `[180, 210]`, `[200, 99999]` — all returned content from line 1
- This makes it impossible to read large files in segments
- Workaround: currently none available within the tool; user must paste file content manually

## Environment

- LobeHub Desktop Version: v2.1.49
- OS: Windows
- File type tested: `.py` (Python source file)

title: Bug Report: Volcengine (Doubao) Provider Fails to Process Videos with InvalidParameter Error
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Web (Desktop Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📌 Version

1.143.3

### 🌐 Browser

Edge

### 🐛 What happened?

📝 Summary
When using the Volcengine (Doubao) provider with a vision model (e.g., doubao-seed-1-6-flash-250828) in LobeChat, attempting to analyze a video file results in an InvalidParameter error. The same operation works perfectly for images, and direct API calls to Volcengine using the same video file succeed.

🌍 Environment
LobeChat Version: Docker latest (running Next.js 15.3.8)

Deployment: Docker Desktop on Windows

Provider: Volcengine (Doubao)

Model Used: doubao-seed-1-6-flash-250828 (multimodal vision model)

File Storage: Local file system (default Docker setup)

❌ Current Behavior
The request fails immediately. The LobeChat UI may show a generic error message. The Docker logs reveal the following error from the Volcengine API:

text
Route: [volcengine] ProviderBizError: {
  code: 'InvalidParameter',
  message: 'Error while connecting: http://127.0.0.1:9000/lobe-chat/files/.../video.mp4, error: Get "...": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:9000: connect: connection refused',
  param: 'video_url',
  type: 'BadRequest'
}
Key observation: The error includes the parameter video_url pointing to a local, non-routable address (127.0.0.1:9000). This indicates LobeChat is sending a URL to the Volcengine API instead of using the required file upload + File ID workflow.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

🔍 Steps to Reproduce
Set up LobeChat with Volcengine provider and a valid API key.

Select a vision-capable Doubao model (e.g., doubao-seed-1-6-flash-250828).

Upload a video file (MP4, size <20MB) via the chat interface.

Send a message asking the model to describe the video content.

### 🚦 What it should be?

✅ Expected Behavior
LobeChat should:

Upload the video file to Volcengine using the /api/v3/files endpoint.

Receive a file_id in response (e.g., file-20260416163311-dw46x).

Construct a chat completion request using the input_video type with the obtained file_id, not a video_url parameter.

### 📝 Additional Information

🔬 Additional Context
Image uploads work correctly: The same model can analyze images without any issue, suggesting the problem is specific to how video files are handled.

Direct API test passes: Using curl or PowerShell to manually upload the video and call the Volcengine API returns a successful, detailed description of the video content. This confirms the video file itself and API key are valid.

Relevant Documentation: Volcengine's [Vision Understanding API](https://www.volcengine.com/docs/82379/1616176) requires files to be uploaded first, then referenced by file_id with type input_video.

📎 Logs (sanitized)
text
🌐 DNS Server: [ '127.0.0.11' ]
[Database] Start to migration...
✅ database migration pass.
▲ Next.js 15.3.8
- Local: http://localhost:3210
- Network: http://0.0.0.0:3210
✓ Starting...
✓ Ready in 444ms
Route: [volcengine] ProviderBizError: {
  code: 'InvalidParameter',
  message: 'Error while connecting: http://127.0.0.1:9000/lobe-chat/files/.../video.mp4, error: Get "...": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:9000: connect: connection refused',
  param: 'video_url',
  type: 'BadRequest'
}
💡 Possible Cause
The Volcengine provider adapter in LobeChat may be incorrectly mapping video input to the video_url field instead of implementing the required two-step upload process (as documented for models like doubao-seed-1-6-flash). The same issue might not appear for images if the provider uses a different code path (e.g., base64 encoding or image_url with local file serving).

🙏 Suggested Fix
Update the Volcengine provider logic for video files to match the official API workflow:

Use POST /api/v3/files to upload the video.

Extract file_id from the response.

Build the request payload with type: "input_video" and file_id.

Ensure the video_url parameter is not used for local files, as Volcengine's API does not support it.

title: [Request] Add Linksee Memory to the LobeHub MCP marketplace
body:
## Feature Description

Request to add **Linksee Memory** to the LobeHub MCP marketplace.

## What it is

Linksee Memory is a local-first agent memory MCP server that gives any AI agent (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT Desktop) a structured cross-agent brain.

Where existing agent-memory tools (Mem0, Letta, Zep) save flat fact lists, Linksee Memory keeps the **WHY** behind every memory using a 6-layer structure:

- `goal` — what the user wanted (WHY)
- `context` — why this, why now (WHY THIS NOW)
- `emotion` — user tone / temperature
- `implementation` — what was tried (success / failure)
- `caveat` — pain lessons (auto-protected from forgetting)
- `learning` — growth log

It also ships a **token-saving file diff cache** (`read_smart`) that returns only changed chunks on re-reads — measured 86% token savings on typical TS file edits, 99% on unchanged re-reads.

## Why it is useful

1. **Cross-agent portability** — single SQLite file at `~/.linksee-memory/memory.db`. Same brain readable from Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT.
2. **Local-first / private** — no cloud, no signup. All memory stays on user's machine.
3. **Token cost reduction** — `read_smart` cuts re-read costs dramatically on long sessions.
4. **WHY-layer recall** — `recall_file("server.ts")` returns not "edited 30 times" but the 30 actual user instructions that drove each edit, organized by phase.
5. **Auto-capture (optional)** — Stop hook for Claude Code records every session into the structured brain with no manual prompting.
6. **Active forgetting** — Ebbinghaus-curve based decay keeps the memory store small; caveat-layer lessons are protected.

## Links

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/linksee-memory
- GitHub: https://github.com/michielinksee/linksee-memory
- MCP Official Registry: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=linksee-memory
- Author: Synapse Arrows PTE. LTD.

## Install / usage

- **Package**: `linksee-memory` (npm, MIT license)
- **Run with**: `npx linksee-memory` (or `claude mcp add -s user linksee -- npx -y linksee-memory`)
- **Transport**: stdio
- **Required env vars**: none. (Optional: `LINKSEE_TELEMETRY=basic` for opt-in anonymous usage stats; `LINKSEE_MEMORY_DIR` to override default `~/.linksee-memory/`.)

## Suggested listing summary

> Local-first agent memory MCP. Cross-agent brain (Claude / Cursor / ChatGPT) with 6-layer structured memory and a token-saving file diff cache.

## Suggested category

- `memory` (primary)
- `productivity` / `developer-tools` (secondary)

## Tools exposed (6)

- `remember` — store memory in 1 of 6 layers for an entity
- `recall` — FTS5 + heat-score + momentum composite ranking, JP/EN trigram search
- `recall_file` — complete edit history of a file across sessions, with per-edit user-intent context
- `read_smart` — diff-only file read; 86% / 99% measured token savings
- `forget` — explicit delete or forgettingRisk-based auto-sweep
- `consolidate` — sleep-mode compression (cluster cold memories → protected learning summary)

Thanks for considering. Happy to provide additional metadata or a Validated badge if helpful.

title: Several Questions About Cloud Sandbox for Self-Hosted Docker LobeHub
body:
When self-hosting LobeHub via Docker, there is an option to enable the cloud sandbox in the chat box, which is a great feature. However, there are many questions I couldn't find answers to after searching the community for a long time, so I'm filing this issue.

1. There is no documentation for the cloud sandbox in self-hosted LobeHub. I could only find sandbox documentation for the official LobeHub deployment.
2. Enabling the cloud sandbox requires creating a LobeHub community creator account. I don't understand what this is for — why does the cloud sandbox need to be bound to a LobeHub creator account?
3. After binding the LobeHub community account, there is no way to unbind it — I cannot find any logout mechanism. Can the unbinding be done directly in the backend database of the self-hosted LobeHub? How would that work? I don't want to be logged into a community account.
4. Where is the cloud sandbox for self-hosted Docker LobeHub? Is it on the self-hosted server or on the official LobeHub server (app.lobehub.com)? There are no environment configuration options related to the cloud sandbox during self-hosting, which suggests it is not running on the self-hosted server. For privacy reasons, users need to know where the cloud sandbox is actually hosted.
5. If the sandbox is on the official server, I think this design doesn't make logical sense for self-hosted LobeHub users. First, since the user has already self-hosted LobeHub, they must have their own cloud server — the sandbox should run on that server, keeping data and code within their own infrastructure. Second, maintaining so many sandboxes on the official side must be costly — wouldn't it be more cost-effective to run the sandbox on users' own servers?

The cloud sandbox is a great feature, but I hope the developers can clarify these questions. Thank you.

title: Desktop heterogeneous-agent attachment cache should sanitize path-like image ids
body:
## 📱 Client Type
- Desktop App (Electron)

## 💻 Operating System
- macOS
- Windows (path semantics also affected in code review)

## 📌 Version
- Reproduced on current `canary` head on 2026-04-18
- Feature is present in `v2.1.52-canary.6`
- Latest stable `v2.1.51` does **not** contain `HeterogeneousAgentCtr` yet

## 🐛 What happened?
The desktop heterogeneous-agent attachment cache uses the raw `image.id` as a filesystem path segment in `HeterogeneousAgentCtr.resolveImage()`:

```ts
const metaPath = join(cacheDir, `${image.id}.meta`);
const dataPath = join(cacheDir, image.id);
```

Because `image.id` is not normalized or converted into a safe cache key, traversal-looking ids (for example `../../escaped-payload`) are treated as real path components.

In local validation, the current controller code:
- wrote cache payload and metadata files outside `heteroAgent/files`
- allowed a longer traversal (`../../../outside-storage`) to escape beyond the `appStoragePath` root
- treated pre-seeded out-of-root traversal targets as cache hits on later reads

This looks like the same class of bug that was fixed earlier in `TempFileManager.writeTempFile()`.

## 📷 How to reproduce it?
1. Open the current desktop heterogeneous-agent controller implementation:
   - `apps/desktop/src/main/controllers/HeterogeneousAgentCtr.ts`
2. Call `resolveImage()` with an attachment id such as `../../escaped-payload`
3. Observe that the resulting `dataPath` / `metaPath` no longer stay inside `.../heteroAgent/files`
4. Call it with `../../../outside-storage` and the resolved path escapes beyond the `appStoragePath` root
5. Pre-create matching traversal target files, then call `resolveImage()` again with the same traversal id and observe that the existing out-of-root files are reused as cache hits

Shared input acceptance is also easy to confirm:
- `UpdateMessageParamsSchema` currently accepts `imageList[].id = '../../escaped-payload'`

## 🚦 What it should be?
Attachment cache files should always stay inside the dedicated desktop cache directory regardless of user-controlled `image.id` values.

A path-like id should be treated as opaque data, not as a path segment.

## 📝 Additional Information
A narrow fix is to derive a stable filesystem-safe cache key from `image.id` (for example `sha256(image.id)`) before constructing payload/meta paths.

That keeps deterministic cache hits while removing traversal semantics from the filename.

I also prepared a small PR with:
- a controller-only fix using a stable hash cache key
- regression tests covering:
  - out-of-root write prevention
  - ignoring pre-seeded traversal cache files

## 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?
- Yes, I am willing to submit a PR

title: [Bug] lobe-user-memory tool schema rejected by Gemini ($ref/allOf not normalized)
body:
### 📦 Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📦 Deployment mode

server db (`lobehub/lobehub:latest`, digest `sha256:c6ac036…`)

### 📌 Version

Observed on **2.1.48**. No related schema-normalization fix appears in the 2.1.49 → 2.1.52-canary.15 CHANGELOG, so I expect this to still reproduce on current `latest`, but I have not tested 2.1.51/2.1.52 directly.

### 💻 Operating System

Other Linux (CachyOS, rootless Docker 29.3.1)

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 Bug Description

When an agent with the built-in **User Memory** plugin is used against a Gemini-family model, Google returns a 400 on the very first request:

```
[400]: * GenerateContentRequest.tools[0].function_declarations[22].parameters.properties[timeIntent].properties: only allowed for OBJECT type
* GenerateContentRequest.tools[0].function_declarations[22].parameters.properties[timeIntent].required: only allowed for OBJECT type
```

The offending tool is `lobe-user-memory____searchUserMemory____builtin`. Its schema uses JSON Schema features that the Gemini `GenerateContentRequest.Tool.Schema` subset does not accept: `$ref` / `definitions`, `allOf`, `oneOf`. With `$ref` left unresolved, the effective node at `timeIntent` has `properties` and `required` but no explicit `type: "object"` — exactly what Google rejects.

Captured excerpt from the failing request — only the minimum needed to reproduce (other fields elided for brevity, but all JSON below is valid as-is):

```json
{
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "definitions": {
      "searchMemoryTimeIntent": {
        "type": "object",
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "properties": {
          "selector": {
            "type": "string",
            "enum": ["today", "yesterday", "currentWeek", "day", "range"]
          },
          "date":  { "type": "string", "format": "date-time" },
          "start": { "type": "string", "format": "date-time" },
          "end":   { "type": "string", "format": "date-time" }
        },
        "required": ["selector"]
      }
    },
    "properties": {
      "timeIntent": {
        "description": "Optional calendar-friendly time selector…",
        "allOf": [
          { "$ref": "#/definitions/searchMemoryTimeIntent" }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Gemini's Schema validator does **not** dereference `$ref` or collapse `allOf` — the merged effective node ends up carrying `properties`/`required` without `type: "object"` and is rejected. The earlier fix tracked in #8085 covered `any_of` on the MCP-tools path; it does not cover `$ref` / `allOf` / `oneOf` emitted by built-in plugin manifests.

Note: the per-payload index `[22]` in the error above is not stable — the offending tool is matched by name `lobe-user-memory____searchUserMemory____builtin`.

### 📷 Recurrence Steps

1. Self-host `lobehub/lobehub:latest` (≥ v2.1.48).
2. Configure any Gemini model (I reproduced with `gemini-2.5-pro` and `gemini-2.5-flash`; the failing payload is emitted client-side by LobeHub so it should fail wherever Google validates the request).
3. Enable the built-in **User Memory** plugin on the agent.
4. Send any user message → 400 with "only allowed for OBJECT type".

Does **not** reproduce against OpenAI-compatible providers (GPT-4o-mini, Claude through an OpenAI-style endpoint) — their schema validators are more permissive and tolerate `$ref`/`allOf` without normalization.

### 🚦 Expected Behavior

Tool schemas emitted toward Gemini-compatible backends should be normalized to fit Google's Schema subset: dereference `$ref`, collapse `allOf`, rewrite or drop `oneOf`/`anyOf`, and guarantee every object node carries `type: "object"`. Doing this in the Gemini context-builder keeps the fix future-proof for every plugin, not just user-memory.

Possible touch points:
- `packages/builtin-tool-memory/src/manifest.ts` — source of the `$ref`+`allOf` schema.
- `packages/model-runtime/src/core/contextBuilders/google.ts` — where tool declarations are prepared for Google. A JSON-Schema-to-Gemini-Schema normalization step here would cover this and future built-in/MCP plugins.

### 📝 Additional Information

- Related, closed: #8085 — same family of errors on `any_of` via MCP tools; fixed for that path only.
- Workarounds while investigating:
  - Disable the built-in **User Memory** plugin on agents that talk to Gemini models.
  - Or use a provider whose validator tolerates full JSON Schema composition (Claude, OpenAI GPT-4o) — not a "non-Gemini route through Gemini", to be clear.
- Full captured request body (with tokens and keys stripped) available on request.

title: 🐛 [Bug] Tool/Skill activation fails due to case-sensitive identifier matching
body:
### Describe the bug

The `lobe-activator` tool uses strict equality (`===`) when matching tool and skill identifiers. When an LLM generates identifiers with different casing (e.g., `lobehub` instead of `LobeHub`, or `Lobe-Web-Browsing` instead of `lobe-web-browsing`), the activation silently fails with "Not found".

### To Reproduce

1. In a conversation, have the agent try to activate a builtin tool or skill using a differently-cased identifier
2. For example, activating the skill `LobeHub` with identifier `lobehub` returns "Not found: lobehub"

### Expected behavior

Identifier matching should be case-insensitive so that `lobehub`, `LobeHub`, and `LOBEHUB` all resolve to the same tool/skill.

### Affected files

- `packages/builtin-tool-activator/src/ExecutionRuntime/index.ts` — `alreadyActive.includes(id)` and `foundIdentifiers.has(id)`
- `packages/builtin-tool-skills/src/ExecutionRuntime/index.ts` — `builtinSkills.find(s => s.name === id/name)`
- `src/store/tool/slices/builtin/executors/lobe-activator.ts` — `discoverable.has(id)`, `.find(t => t.identifier === id)`
- `src/server/services/toolExecution/serverRuntimes/activator.ts` — `context.toolManifestMap[id]`

### Fix

Branch `fix/activator-case-insensitive` normalizes all identifier comparisons to lowercase.

title: [MCP] Add Suprsonic: Unified agent API with dozens of capabilities
body:
## Feature Description
Please include Suprsonic MCP in the LobeHub MCP marketplace.

## What it is
Suprsonic is a unified agent API that gives AI agents dozens of capabilities through a single API key: search, scrape, profile enrichment, email finding, image generation, TTS, STT, messaging, document extraction, and more. Zero provider auth required.

## Why it is useful
- One API key replaces dozens of provider signups, dashboards, and invoices
- Multi-provider waterfall with automatic failover
- Unified response format across all capabilities
- Credits deducted only on success (failed requests are free)
- Works with Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, ChatGPT

## Links
- Website: https://suprsonic.ai
- Docs: https://suprsonic.ai/docs/api
- Capability list: https://suprsonic.ai/apis
- GitHub: https://github.com/O-mega-Enterprise/suprsonic-mcp
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/suprsonic-mcp
- OpenAPI: https://suprsonic.ai/v1/openapi.json

## Install
- Package: suprsonic-mcp
- Run: npx suprsonic-mcp
- Env: SUPRSONIC_API_KEY

## Suggested category
Developer Tools / Search / Communication

title: [Bug] Auto Context Compression not triggering for Alibaba Cloud Bailian GLM-5, causing 400 Input Length Error
body:
### 📱 Client Type Web (Official Cloud: [app.lobehub.com]()) ### 💻 Operating System Browser (Cross-platform) ### 📦 Deployment Platform Official Cloud ([app.lobehub.com]()) ### 📌 Version Latest (Current as of 2026-04-24) ### 🐛 What happened? Auto Context Compression appears to fail for **Alibaba Cloud Bailian GLM-5** (via Coding Plan provider).
The conversation history grew to **201,525 tokens** without being compressed, causing the API request to fail with a `400` error due to exceeding the provider's input length limit. **Error Details:** ```json { "error": { "code": "invalid_parameter_error", "type": "invalid_request_error", "message": "<400> InternalError.Algo.InvalidParameter: Range of input length should be [1, 202745]" }, "endpoint": "https://coding.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1", "provider": "bailiancodingplan" } ``` **Observation:** * Total Input: 201,525 tokens (Un-cached input: 201,081). * The error indicates the provider's limit is \~202,745. * Despite "Auto Context Compression" being enabled, the system did not trigger a summary/compression before hitting the hard limit. ### 📷 How to reproduce it? 1. Open LobeHub Web ([app.lobehub.com]()). 2. Create a session with **Alibaba Cloud Bailian** provider, using the **GLM-5** model (Coding Plan endpoint). 3. Ensure "Auto Context Compression" is enabled. 4. Engage in a long conversation or upload large context until the total tokens approach the model's limit (approx 200k). 5. Observe that the context is not compressed and the API returns a 400 error when the threshold is breached. ### 🚦 What it should be? The system should trigger context compression (summarization of older messages) when the input length approaches the threshold (e.g., 80-90% of the limit), preventing the request from hitting the provider's hard limit. ### 📝 Additional Information * This issue is similar to [LOBE-5789](https://linear.app/lobehub/issue/LOBE-5789/enable-auto-context-compression-not-working) (reported for Opus 4.6), suggesting a potential platform-wide issue with context compression triggers for specific high-context models. * Model GLM-5 typically supports 1M+ context, but the Bailian Coding Plan endpoint seems to return a limit of \~200k here. Even so, compression should have triggered to keep usage below this limit. * **Privacy Note:** I am not uploading screenshots of the error due to sensitive session information, but the JSON error message is included above. ### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR? No (Cloud environment issue).

title: [MCP] Mandatory progress feedback for long-running tool calls — heartbeat, live timer, and abort button
body:
## The Problem

When an LLM makes 3+ sequential MCP tool calls in a batch (e.g., search → scrape → analyze), the user sees **zero textual response** for 30-90+ seconds. Just a static spinner with a tool name. You cannot tell:
- Is the model still working?
- Is the MCP server alive or silently crashed?
- Should I wait 5 more seconds or 5 more minutes?
This creates **deep uncertainty anxiety** in users.
## Proposal: 3-Layer Progress Assurance

### Layer 1: MCP Heartbeat Protocol (Mandatory)
MCP servers **MUST** send `notifications/progress` every 5s during execution:
```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "notifications/progress",
  "params": {
    "progressToken": "<tool_call_id>",
    "progress": 45,
    "total": 100,
    "message": "Fetching page 45/100..."
  }
}
Escalation rules (no heartbeat received):
10s silence → Yellow warning: "No response for 10s..."
30s silence → Red warning: "Tool may have crashed" + Abort button
MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT → Force terminate

Layer 2: Live Per-Tool Status Card
Each tool call displays in the chat thread:
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 🔍 Desktop Commander     ⏱ 23s          │
│ ► Searching B站 "AI Agent" videos...      │
│ ████████████░░░░░░░░░ 45%               │
│ [⏹ Abort]                               │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
Required: live timer (0.1s precision), status message, progress bar, abort button.

Layer 3: Multi-Tool Batch View
When 3+ tools run in sequence with no text output:
Show a collapsed summary of all queued/running tools
Each shows: icon, name, status (⏳/🔄/✅/❌), elapsed time
Expand any card for full progress details
On completion, collapse to: "🔧 3 tools completed in 42s [+]"
Fallback for MCP Servers Without Progress Support
If a server doesn't send progress notifications:
Frontend injects a 5s polling heartbeat check
Auto-escalates warnings at 10s / 30s
Shows abort button after 15s


Why This Matters
Without this, users have no way to distinguish between "model is working hard" and "something is broken." This is the #1 UX gap in MCP-based agent applications today.


Environment
LobeHub Desktop v2.1.52
Self-hosted backend
Model: DeepSeek
MCP: Desktop Commander, Playwright, Fetcher, Tavily

title: [High Priority] Mobile regression in 2.1.53-canary.27: selecting any historical topic immediately redirects to home
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Web (Mobile Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

iOS

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📌 Version

2.1.53-canary.27

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

A severe mobile regression appears in LobeChat `2.1.53-canary.27` under a Docker Compose self-hosted deployment.

On iPhone 15 Pro with iOS `26.3.1`, when opening LobeChat on mobile and entering any assistant, tapping the topic selector at the top and selecting any historical topic does not work. The selected topic flashes briefly, then the interface immediately switches back to the home/default page. As a result, historical conversations cannot be opened or viewed on mobile at all.

This issue is reproducible in all tested mobile access modes:

- Safari on iOS
- Chrome on iOS
- PWA / Add to Home Screen mode

The issue affects:

- All assistants
- All historical topics
- All attempts to enter historical topics on mobile

Desktop access works normally on the same deployment. Historical topics can be opened correctly on desktop browsers.

This behavior did not occur in `2.1.53-canary.23`. It started occurring after upgrading to `2.1.53-canary.27`.

No configuration changes were made except upgrading from `2.1.53-canary.23` to `2.1.53-canary.27`.

Impact:

- Mobile users cannot access any historical topic.
- Historical conversation records are effectively inaccessible on mobile.
- The problem affects every assistant and every historical topic.
- PWA mode is also affected.
- This is a core functionality regression and makes mobile history access unusable.

Given the severity and the fact that this completely blocks mobile users from opening historical conversations, I believe this should be treated as a high-priority regression.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

Steps to reproduce:

1. Deploy LobeChat using Docker Compose.
2. Use version `2.1.53-canary.27`.
3. Open the self-hosted LobeChat site on an iPhone 15 Pro running iOS `26.3.1`.
4. Reproduce using any of the following:
   - Safari on iOS
   - Chrome on iOS
   - PWA / Add to Home Screen mode
5. Enter any assistant.
6. Tap the topic selector at the top of the assistant page.
7. Select any existing historical topic.
8. Observe the result.

Actual result:

- The selected historical topic flashes briefly.
- The interface immediately switches back to the home/default page.
- The historical topic cannot be opened.
- Repeating the operation always produces the same result.

Scope of reproduction:

- All assistants are affected.
- All historical topics are affected.
- Browser mode and PWA mode are both affected.
- Desktop browsers on the same deployment work normally.

Regression information:

- Last known working version: `2.1.53-canary.23`
- Affected version: `2.1.53-canary.27`
- No configuration changes were made except upgrading from `2.1.53-canary.23` to `2.1.53-canary.27`.

### 🚦 What it should be?

After selecting a historical topic from the top topic selector on mobile, LobeChat should stay inside the selected topic and display the corresponding historical conversation.

Expected behavior:

- The selected historical topic should open normally.
- The user should be able to view the historical conversation records.
- The page should not redirect back to the home/default page.
- Mobile web and PWA behavior should be consistent with desktop behavior.
- The behavior should remain consistent with the previously working version `2.1.53-canary.23`.

### 📝 Additional Information

Environment:

- Deployment platform: Docker Compose self-hosted deployment
- Device: iPhone 15 Pro
- OS: iOS `26.3.1`
- Affected version: `2.1.53-canary.27`
- Last known working version: `2.1.53-canary.23`
- Browsers / modes tested:
  - Safari on iOS
  - Chrome on iOS
  - PWA / Add to Home Screen
- Desktop access: Works normally
- Mobile access: Broken
- Scope:
  - All assistants are affected
  - All historical topics are affected
  - All attempts to open historical topics on mobile redirect back to the home/default page

Upgrade information:

No configuration changes were made except upgrading from `2.1.53-canary.23` to `2.1.53-canary.27`.

This strongly suggests a regression introduced between `2.1.53-canary.23` and `2.1.53-canary.27`.

The issue is highly severe because it completely prevents mobile users from accessing historical conversations. The selected topic appears only for a brief moment before the UI jumps back to the home/default page.

Please consider prioritizing this issue, as topic history access is a core feature and is currently unusable on mobile in the affected version.

No, but I am happy to help test the fix

title: Bug: Context Compression fails in Group Chat — No conversation history provided to compress
body:
## Bug: Context Compression fails in Group Chat — "No conversation history provided to compress"

### Description

In Group Chat, both auto and manual context compression fail with the LLM responding:

> No conversation history provided to compress. The chat history is empty.

However, the chat history clearly exists and is visible in the conversation.

### Related Issues

* [LOBE-5730](https://linear.app/lobehub/issue/LOBE-5730/context-compression-not-detecting-chat-history-in-agent-group-chat) reports the same symptom but has no root cause analysis
* [#12986](<https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/issues/12986>) addresses a different issue (empty compression summary overwriting history) and does not fix this bug

### Root Cause Analysis

After investigation, I found that the `compress_context` executor on the server side is **never reached** in group chat. The problem occurs upstream on the client side:

1. The client retrieves messages via `dbMessagesMap[messageKey]` before creating the compression instruction
2. The `messageMapKey` function generates different keys for group chats (format: `group_{groupId}_{topicId}`)
3. When compression is triggered in a group chat context, the `messageKey` used to look up messages does not correctly include the `groupId`, resulting in an empty messages array
4. The empty messages array is then sent to the LLM, which responds with "No conversation history provided to compress"

Additionally, the server-side `compress_context` executor queries messages without passing `groupId`:

```javascript
// Current code in compress_context executor
t.messageModel.query({agentId:s.metadata?.agentId, threadId:s.metadata?.threadId, topicId:h})
```

Even if the client-side issue were fixed, `s.metadata` does not contain `groupId`, so the server would also fail to query the correct messages for group chats.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Group Chat with multiple agents
2. Ensure "Enable Auto Context Compression" is enabled for the agent
3. Send enough messages to trigger auto compression (or manually trigger compression)
4. Observe the compression output: "No conversation history provided to compress. The chat history is empty."
5. Subsequent messages in the same topic are treated as an empty conversation

### Expected Behavior

Compression should correctly detect chat history in group chats and generate a proper summary.

### Environment

* LobeChat version: v2.1.53
* Deployment: Docker self-hosted
* Feature: Group Chat + Context Compression

### Workaround

Disable "Enable Auto Context Compression" in the agent settings and create a new topic. Existing topics where compression has already failed will continue to behave as empty conversations.

title: [Bug] lobe-web-onboarding injects <next_actions> after completion, triggers false finishOnboarding signals (v2.1.55-canary.11)
body:
## Summary

After completing onboarding, the `lobe-web-onboarding` plugin continues to inject `<next_actions>` blocks into every turn, even when:
- Onboarding is **complete** (confirmed via `getOnboardingState` — returns "Onboarding is complete")
- The user has NOT sent a new message (the block arrives alone, with no user text)
- The conversation is on an unrelated technical task

This creates two serious problems:

1. **False completion signals**: The block contains text like "If the user says Done/Thanks/好了, you MUST call finishOnboarding" — but the user has not said any of those things. A less defensive agent would prematurely terminate onboarding or call persistence tools on non-existent user input.

2. **Phantom turns**: The agent receives multiple turns in a row containing ONLY the `<next_actions>` block with no user content.

## Reproduction

1. Complete onboarding normally
2. Start a technical conversation (e.g., debugging a local tool)
3. Observe: every 1–2 turns the system injects a `<next_actions>` block, sometimes as the entire message content with no accompanying user text

## Environment

- **Platform**: LobeHub Desktop (Windows)
- **Version**: v2.1.55-canary.11
- **Agent model**: global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 (Bedrock)
- **Plugin involved**: lobe-web-onboarding

## Suspected root cause

Likely regression from one of these canary.11 PRs:
- #14290 — refactor(agent-signal): simplify structure of agent-signal
- #14297 — fix: include all properties in task_topic_handoff response_format required

The `<next_actions>` injection appears to fire on every turn regardless of onboarding state (complete flag) and regardless of whether the user actually sent a message.

## Expected behavior

- When onboarding state is complete, no `<next_actions>` block should be injected
- When a turn contains no user content, onboarding directives should not be evaluated
- Completion-detection rules should ONLY fire when the user has actually sent text

## Impact

Forces every agent using lobe-web-onboarding to implement defensive logic (explicitly declaring 'I will NOT call finishOnboarding because you didn't say it' in every turn) which pollutes the conversation and wastes tokens. Non-defensive agents may incorrectly call finishOnboarding or writeDocument on phantom messages.

## Additional notes

Discovered during a debugging session where the user was asking for MCP server code analysis. Across ~6 consecutive turns the system injected the `<next_actions>` block alone, disrupting the technical task.

---

title: [Request]  Add "Open in Portal" action to topic / thread list item menu
body: ## 🚩 Feature Description Currently, when I click the "⋯" menu on a topic / sub-topic (thread) in the left sidebar, the only available actions are **Rename** and **Delete**. There is no way to open that topic/thread in the right-side Portal panel from the sidebar. The only way to get the split (parent topic + sub-topic side-by-side) layout is to click the "branch" icon on a message at the moment the sub-topic is first created. Once the page is reloaded or reopened from the sidebar (URL without `?portalThread=`), the split layout is lost and there is no UI way to bring it back. i want reopen in two col page, like ## 🧩 Proposal Add a new menu item `Open in Portal` (在侧栏打开) to the "⋯" dropdown of every topic/thread in the left sidebar, alongside Rename / Delete. Clicking it should call the existing action: ```ts useChatStore.getState().pushPortalView({ threadId: item.id, type: PortalViewType.Thread, }); ``` Because `ThreadHydration.tsx` already binds `portalThreadId` to the `?portalThread=` URL query via `useQueryState`, the side-by-side layout will then be restorable by simply reloading or bookmarking that URL. ## ✅ Why this is low-cost - All underlying infrastructure already exists: - `pushPortalView` action (`src/store/chat/slices/portal/action.ts`) - URL ↔ store sync (`src/routes/(main)/agent/features/Conversation/ThreadHydration.tsx`) - Portal rendering of `PortalViewType.Thread` - Estimated change: ~20 LOC (one menu item + i18n keys) - Zero breaking change, purely additive ## 💡 Use Case Power users often keep several parallel threads open next to the main conversation (e.g. reference thread + active thread). Today, once the tab is closed or reloaded from the sidebar, there is no way to bring a specific thread back into the Portal without creating a brand-new branch from a message. Adding this menu item closes that gap and makes the already-supported `?portalThread=` URL feature discoverable from the UI.

title: [Bug] Creating a sub-topic from inside a sub-topic inherits only the parent Topic's context, losing the current sub-topic's context
body: ### 📦 Deployment Environment Server mode (`lobe-chat-database` image, self-hosted with PostgreSQL) ### 📌 Software Version v2.1.56 ### 💻 System Environment macOS / Chrome ### 🐛 Bug Description LobeChat allows creating a new sub-topic (Thread) from inside an existing sub-topic — the UI button works and a new Thread row is created. **However, the new sub-topic receives the wrong context:** > **When branching a new sub-topic `B` from a message inside sub-topic `A`, `B` only inherits the parent Topic's linear history and completely drops everything that happened inside `A`.** This is the opposite of what a user expects. Standing inside `A` and branching off implies: *"continue to dig deeper along the current discussion thread"*, not *"throw away `A` and fall back to the parent Topic"*. ### 📷 Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a Topic `P` and have a few messages in it: `P1, P2, P3, ...` 2. On message `Pk`, create sub-topic `A`; continue the conversation inside `A`, producing `A1, A2, A3, ...` 3. On message `Am` inside `A`, click "create sub-topic" again — this creates a new sub-topic `B` 4. In `B`, ask the model something like "summarize everything you can see in the current context" **Actual**: `B`'s reply clearly only covers messages from `P` (up to `Pk`); nothing from `A1 ~ Am` is visible to the model. **Expected**: `B`'s context should be `P1 ~ Pk` + `A1 ~ Am` — i.e. the full visible history walking from the Topic root down the `A` branch to the fork point. ### 📷 Screenshots (real repro) > I'll attach screenshots once I re-open the window. Brief description below. **Screenshot 1** — the new sub-topic `B` created from inside sub-topic `A` (`学习计划` / "Study Plan"): The model in `B` is discussing Qwen3_5 internals (`RMSNorm`, `RoPE`, `gate_proj` / `up_proj` / `down_proj`, etc.) — all of which come from a parent-Topic message titled "千问 35 模型结构解释" ("Qwen 3.5 model architecture explanation"), **not** from sub-topic `A`. **Screenshot 2** — the parent Topic `LLM 大模型学习` ("LLM Study") sidebar: `千问 35 模型结构解释` is a Topic-level message node. Sub-topic `A` (`学习计划`) contains meaningful content like `🚀 给你的落地行动建议表` ("Actionable roadmap"). None of this content appears in `B`'s context, confirming that `B` skipped `A` entirely and pulled from the parent Topic instead. ### 🚦 Expected Behavior - When sub-topic `B` is branched from message `M` inside sub-topic `A`, `B`'s context should be the **full visible history along the current Thread chain**, i.e.: - parent Topic messages up to `A`'s fork point, **plus** - messages inside `A` from the beginning up to `M` - Equivalently: a sub-topic's context should be computed from **the chain of ancestor Threads walking up via `parentThreadId`**, not just from the root Topic's linear history. - This is the only behavior that matches the natural semantics of "keep drilling deeper into the current branch". ### 📌 Likely Source Code Areas - `packages/database/src/schemas/topic.ts` — the `threads.parentThreadId` column is a self-reference, so **the data model already supports arbitrary nesting**. No schema change needed. - `src/store/chat/slices/thread/action.ts` — `createThread` accepts `parentThreadId`, but the context-window computation for a nested sub-topic likely filters only by `topicId + sourceMessageId` and does not walk up the `parentThreadId` chain to include ancestor Threads' messages. - The chat-history assembly logic (message query / `chatHistory` builder) appears to miss the union with ancestor Threads' visible messages. **Suggested fix (algorithm sketch)**: ``` ancestors = [] t = B.parentThread while t is not null: ancestors.prepend(t) # walk up parentThreadId to the Topic root t = t.parentThread context = [] # Start from the root Topic up to where the topmost ancestor Thread forked off context += messages of root Topic up to ancestors[0].sourceMessageId # Then for each ancestor Thread, include its messages up to where the next child forked off for i, thread in enumerate(ancestors): next_fork = ancestors[i+1].sourceMessageId if i+1 < len(ancestors) else B.sourceMessageId context += messages inside `thread` up to next_fork ``` Implementation style is up to the team — the key point is to **include messages from ancestor Threads**, not just the root Topic. ### 🔗 Related Issues - #8327 — describes context bleeding between **sibling** sub-topics and the parent Topic. This issue focuses on the **nested** sub-topic case, where the current Thread's own context is dropped. Both appear to be different symptoms of the same class of bug in sub-topic context slicing. ### 📝 Additional Notes - The database layer already supports nested Threads via `threads.parentThreadId` self-reference. This is a logic bug in how context is collected, not a schema limitation.

title: Vercel deployment failure is fixed by #14200 but still awaiting approval
body:
## Summary

PR #14200 fixes a reproducible Vercel deployment failure for `lobehub`, but it has not been approved/merged yet.

- PR: https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/pull/14200
- PR title: `🐛 fix: stabilize Vercel deploy and sitemap generation`
- PR opened: April 26, 2026
- Checked on: May 3, 2026
- Current PR state observed: open, non-draft, mergeable

This issue affects Vercel deployments generally, not just a single preview environment. Any Vercel deployment that installs the affected dependency graph can hit the same `@lobehub/editor` postinstall Lexical patch mismatch during dependency installation. Even when installation succeeds, the uncached sitemap metadata generation can still make the later build stage unstable or appear stuck while rendering routes and sitemap chunks.

The deployments referenced below were reproduced and verified on my own Vercel account/project. They are included as before/after evidence for the same LobeHub code path, not as a claim that only that specific Vercel project is affected.

## Why this matters

Current `canary` can fail during Vercel dependency installation before the application build even starts. The failing point is `@lobehub/editor` postinstall patching Lexical:

```text
[lobe-editor] Failed to patch Lexical automatically: Patch context mismatch in Lexical.dev.js
ELIFECYCLE Command failed with exit code 1.
Error: Command "npx pnpm@10.26.2 install" exited with 1
```

PR #14200 fixes this by pinning the editor dependency and aligning the package manager version used by Vercel, preventing dependency drift during install. It also caches sitemap identifiers so sitemap generation does not repeatedly refetch the same data during the build.

Leaving this PR unmerged keeps Vercel deployments broken or unstable for users deploying LobeHub from the affected branch, including self-hosted Vercel deployments and preview deployments created from forks.

## Sitemap generation fix

PR #14200 also fixes a separate Vercel build-stage stability problem in sitemap generation. The install failure evidence above focuses on `@lobehub/editor` / Lexical patching, but the PR also changes `src/server/sitemap.ts` so sitemap metadata identifiers are cached during the build instead of being fetched repeatedly for every generated sitemap path.

This matters because Vercel prerenders many sitemap routes, including `/sitemap/pages.xml`, `/sitemap/providers.xml`, `/sitemap/plugins-1.xml`, and more than 150 additional metadata paths. Without caching, the build can repeatedly call the same expensive metadata fetching logic during route output generation, which can make the deployment appear stuck around route generation / rendering chunks / sitemap generation even after dependency installation succeeds.

With the cache in place, sitemap generation becomes deterministic and cheaper during the same build process, so #14200 addresses both the install-stage failure and the later build-stage instability.

### 🥰 Feature Description

We'd like to list **Parse** on LobeHub's MCP marketplace (https://lobehub.com/mcp). The site's "Submit" modal returned `Failed to submit MCP plugin` (POST `/api/workflows/add-mcp-plugin` → 500), so filing here as the documented fallback (mirrors #14133).

### 🧐 Proposed Solution

Index our GitHub repository:

- **Repo**: https://github.com/Parsegl/parse-mcp
- **Name**: Parse
- **Publisher**: Parse (https://parse.gl) — official
- **License**: MIT
- **Suggested category**: `Analytics` (or `Marketing` / `SEO` if Analytics is not a marketplace category)

**What it does**

Look up how any brand surfaces in ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews. Parse's public AI visibility index, queryable from any MCP-capable client. **577,000+ brands tracked** across millions of organic AI prompts, with 47M+ citation observations. Read-only, no auth required, structured for sales prospecting, due diligence, editorial research, and competitor scans.

**Transport & Auth**

- Transport: `streamable-http`
- Endpoint: `https://mcp.parse.gl/mcp`
- MCP-Protocol-Version: `2025-06-18`
- Auth: none (public read-only)

**Quick start (Claude Desktop / Cursor / hosted)**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "parse": {
      "transport": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.parse.gl/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

For Claude Code:

```
claude mcp add --transport http parse https://mcp.parse.gl/mcp
```

For stdio-only Claude Desktop builds, use the `mcp-remote` shim:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "parse": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.parse.gl/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

**Tools exposed** (verified live):

- `parse_search` — query across brands / prompts / niches / sources
- `parse_get_brand` — public brand brief (Parse score, strengths, weak spots, top prompts, citation sources)
- `parse_get_prompt` — one organic AI-search prompt by slug
- `parse_get_stats` — dataset scale and freshness
- `search` and `fetch` — compatibility aliases

title: Local QStash dev server fails to process Workflow callbacks for memory extraction
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Web (Desktop Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows, Ubuntu

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📌 Version

2.1.56

### 🌐 Browser

Edge

### 🐛 What happened?

Attempting to use the built-in memory extraction feature
with a self-hosted QStash dev server results in a timeout after 5–10 minutes:
  "User memory extraction timed out after N minutes for M topics"
Investigation reveals that while QStash dev server (both v2.36.5 and v2.37.18) 
correctly handles simple messages published via POST /v2/publish (events appear 
in GET /v2/logs and callbacks are delivered), workflow messages published by 
@upstash/workflow SDK's client.trigger() never appear in /v2/logs. QStash 
returns a valid workflowRunId, yet the workflow is never processed.
No network connectivity issues — both containers share the same Docker bridge 
network, and manual /v2/publish tests confirm QStash can reach lobehub 
successfully. MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL is correctly set.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Deploy LobeHub via Docker Compose (lobehub/lobehub:latest, v2.1.56)
2. Add a local QStash dev server to docker-compose.yml:
     image: public.ecr.aws/upstash/qstash:latest
     command: qstash dev
3. Set in .env:
     QSTASH_TOKEN=<token from dev server>
     QSTASH_URL=http://qstash:8080
     MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_GATEKEEPER_PROVIDER=deepseek (or any non-openai provider)
     MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_GATEKEEPER_MODEL=<valid model>
     MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL=http://lobehub:3210
     (repeat for LAYER_EXTRACTOR, PERSONA_WRITER, EMBEDDING)
4. Start all containers: docker compose up -d
5. Create a conversation and click "Request Memory Analysis"
6. Observe:
   - async_tasks table: workflowRunId is stored (publish succeeded)
   - GET /v2/logs on QStash: no workflow events appear
   - lobehub logs: no POST to /api/workflows/memory-user-memory/... received
   - Manual publish via curl to the same workflow URL proves network works

### 🚦 What it should be?

QStash dev server should fully support the workflow protocol used by 
@upstash/workflow SDK's client.trigger(). Workflow callbacks should be 
delivered to the registered endpoint, and their lifecycle events 
(CREATED → ACTIVE → DELIVERED/ERROR) should be visible in GET /v2/logs, 
mirroring the behavior of simple messages published via /v2/publish.

### 📝 Additional Information

- LobeHub version: 2.1.56 (Docker image built 2026-05-01)
- Next.js: 16.2.4
- QStash dev server: tested v2.36.5 and v2.37.18, same behavior
- Deployment: Docker Compose on Windows (WSL2), all services on same bridge network
- AI Provider: DeepSeek BYOK (issue is not model-related)
- Memory extraction configs are set to non-openai providers — model config is not the root cause
- Manual /v2/publish tests prove QStash ↔ lobehub connectivity works

### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?

None

### ✅ Validations

- [x] Read the [docs](https://lobehub.com/zh/docs).
- [x] Check that there isn't [already an issue](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues) that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate.
- [x] Make sure this is a LobeChat issue and not a third-party library or provider issue.
- [x] Check that this is a concrete bug. For Q&A, please use [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions) or join our [Discord Server](https://discord.gg/rGHwKq4R).

title: [Request] Add Inferventis to the LobeHub MCP marketplace
body:
## Feature Description

Please include **Inferventis** in the LobeHub MCP marketplace. Inferventis is a remote-hosted MCP server providing 20 financial tools — covering real-time stock quotes, cryptocurrency prices, multi-currency FX conversion, financial calculations, bank account data (Open Banking/PSD2), Stripe payment records, web news headlines, and URL reading — all accessible to AI agents via a single zero-install Streamable HTTP endpoint.

## Canonical Metadata

- **Title:** Inferventis MCP
- **Identifier:** \`io.github.bankee-ai/inferventis-tools\`
- **Repository:** https://github.com/Bankee-ai/inferventis-tools
- **Remote endpoint:** https://mcp-server-295985738387.europe-west1.run.app/mcp (Streamable HTTP)
- **License:** MIT
- **Maintainer:** @Bankee-ai
- **Website:** https://inferventis.ai

## Tools

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| \`platform_tool_finder\` | Discovers the most relevant tools available on this MCP server for a given task |
| \`stock_quote\` | Real-time stock price quotes and company information for any publicly listed ticker |
| \`stock_price_lite\` | Current trading price for a publicly listed stock by ticker symbol |
| \`crypto_price\` | Real-time price data for any cryptocurrency listed on CoinGecko |
| \`crypto_price_lite\` | Spot price and 24-hour change for any cryptocurrency |
| \`crypto_fx_rates\` | Converts amounts between any cryptocurrency and fiat currency pair |
| \`currency_convert\` | Converts a monetary amount between currencies using live exchange rates |
| \`currency_convert_lite\` | Converts between any two fiat currencies using live exchange rates |
| \`currency_fx_lite\` | FX conversion between two fiat currencies |
| \`currency_rates\` | Live and historical fiat currency exchange rates from Frankfurter API |
| \`currency_convert_open\` | Fiat currency conversion using open exchange rate data |
| \`financial_calculator\` | Precise financial calculations across six calculation types (no external API) |
| \`financial_calculator_lite\` | Common financial calculations locally with no external API dependency |
| \`bank_accounts\` | Bank account details and recent transaction history via connected banking |
| \`open_banking_transactions\` | Bank account balances and transaction history via PSD2 Open Banking (TrueLayer) |
| \`stripe_payments\` | Live payment data from a Stripe account via the Stripe API |
| \`stripe_payment_records\` | Payment and charge records from a Stripe merchant account |
| \`web_news_headlines\` | Latest real-time news headlines and article summaries from BBC News |
| \`web_url_reader\` | Fetches any public web page and returns clean, readable plain text |

## Remote (zero-install) Configuration

**Claude Code:**
\`\`\`bash
claude mcp add inferventis --transport http https://mcp-server-295985738387.europe-west1.run.app/mcp
\`\`\`

**Any MCP client:**
\`\`\`json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "inferventis": {
      "type": "streamableHttp",
      "url": "https://mcp-server-295985738387.europe-west1.run.app/mcp"
    }
  }
}
\`\`\`

## Why include this

Inferventis is one of the few fully remote, zero-install MCP servers focused entirely on financial data. Agents can access live markets, FX, crypto, banking, and payments with a single URL — no API keys required for the core tools, no local setup. It runs on Google Cloud Run (Europe West 1) with structured logging, telemetry, and 99.9%+ uptime.

### 📱 Client Type Web (Desktop Browser) ### 💻 Operating System Windows ### 📦 Deployment Platform Self hosting Docker ### 📌 Version v2.1.57-canary.12 ### 🌐 Browser Chrome ### 🐛 What happened? When using Azure OpenAI provider with image generation models (e.g., `gpt-image-2`), the image generation flow sends the raw model ID (`gpt-image-2`) to Azure's `/images/generations` endpoint instead of the configured deployment name. This causes a `400 Unknown model: gpt-image-2` error, displayed as **Generation Failed ServerError** in the UI. The model list fetch works correctly — the deployment name mapping is visible in the UI provider settings. Chat completion also works correctly because the frontend resolves the deployment name via `findDeploymentName()` and passes it in the payload. However, the image generation async router does not resolve the deployment name before calling the provider. ### 📷 How to reproduce it? 1. Configure Azure OpenAI provider with `AZURE_MODEL_LIST` containing a deployment name mapping, e.g.: ``` -all,+gpt-image-2->your-deployment-name ``` 2. "code": "unknown_model" }, "code": "unknown_model" } [async-image] Full error: { "endpoint": "https://***.openai.azure.com/openai/v1", "error": { "error": {} }, "errorType": "ProviderBizError", "provider": "azure" } ```

A direct curl call to the same Azure endpoint with the correct deployment name works fine: ```bash curl -X POST $AZURE_ENDPOINT/openai/v1/images/generations \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZURE_API_KEY" \ -d '{"prompt":"a pixel cat","model":""}' ``` ### 🚦 What it should be? For Azure provider, the image generation request should use the deployment name (from `AZURE_MODEL_LIST` env var or web UI configuration) instead of the raw model ID when calling `client.images.generate()`, just like how the chat completion flow handles it. ### 📝 Additional Information **(Analyzed with claude code)** The deployment name mapping for Azure models works differently in chat vs image generation: - **Chat flow**: The frontend resolves deployment name via `findDeploymentName()` ([`src/services/chat/helper.ts`](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/7bf923d762f916a1ffb2e1860f5b52ec5df13939/src/services/chat/helper.ts#L28-L41)) and passes it in the payload as `deploymentName`. The backend Azure runtime uses `deploymentName ?? model` in the chat handler. - **Image generation flow**: The frontend sends `{ model, params }` to the lambda router, which triggers the async router. The async router ([`src/server/routers/async/image.ts`](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/7bf923d762f916a1ffb2e1860f5b52ec5df13939/src/server/routers/async/image.ts#L271-L274)) calls `resolveBusinessModelMapping()` from `@lobechat/business-model-runtime` ([`packages/business/model-runtime/src/model-mapping.ts`](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/7bf923d762f916a1ffb2e1860f5b52ec5df13939/packages/business/model-runtime/src/model-mapping.ts#L28-L35)), but currently this function is a no-op stub that returns the model ID as-is: ```typescript export const resolveBusinessModelMapping = async ( _provider: string, model: string, ): Promise => { return { resolvedModelId: model, // no-op }; }; ``` As a result, the Azure `createImage()` method receives the raw model ID `gpt-image-2` instead of the deployment name, causing `400 Unknown model`. **Temporary workaround:** Manually parsing `process.env.AZURE_MODEL_LIST` in `src/server/routers/async/image.ts` before the `createImage` call resolves the deployment name correctly. However a proper fix should be implemented in `resolveBusinessModelMapping()`. ### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?
