title: [Request] Add Lawbster MCP Server to the MCP marketplace
body:
## MCP server submission The web form at [https://lobehub.com/de/mcp]() returns
`POST /api/workflows/add-mcp-plugin → 500 Internal Server Error`
(`{"error":"Human verification is required"}` after Cloudflare challenge).
Filing here as the documented fallback path, in line with lobehub/lobehub#14133. ### Repository [https://github.com/PLANIT-TECH/lawbster-mcp]() ### About Lawbster Verified, citable German & EU law for any MCP-capable AI assistant.
Daily updates from official sources, hosted in Germany. \~11 000 statutes,
the full EU legal corpus, and German federal court decisions
(BGH, BVerfG, BAG, BSG, BPatG, BFH, EuGH). * Website: [https://lawbster.planitprima.com]() * Operator: PLANIT // TECH GmbH (Germany) * Service: commercial managed SaaS; 14-day free trial, €19/seat/month after. * Repo license: MIT — covers documentation, client snippets/rules/skills/prompts,
and the npm wrapper package source (`packages/lawbster-mcp/`).
The hosted Lawbster server itself is **not open source** and is not covered
by the repo LICENSE — it's a managed SaaS. See LICENSE for the exact scope. ### Quality checklist - [X] Has README - [X] Provides ≥1 installation method (npx, manual JSON, OAuth web flow) - [X] Has ≥1 Skill (8 MCP tools) - [X] Has LICENSE (MIT) - [X] Offers friendly installation (`npx -y @planit-lawbster/lawbster-mcp setup --client claude|cursor|vscode|windsurf`) - [X] Includes Prompts (3 MCP prompts: `legal_research`, `citation_resolve`, `compare_de_eu`) - [X] Includes Resources (6 MCP resources: `legal://rechtsrahmen`, `legal://filter_values`, `legal://eu_celex_registry`, plus three URI templates) ### Transport & authentication * Streamable HTTP at `https://lawbster.planitprima.com/mcp` * OAuth 2.1 (recommended for browser clients) **and** Bearer API key (`sk-legal-…`) ### Configuration example ```json { "mcpServers": { "lawbster": { "type": "http", "url": "https://lawbster.planitprima.com/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer sk-legal-..." } } } } ``` ### Logo / assets * 1254×1254 icon: [https://github.com/PLANIT-TECH/lawbster-mcp/blob/main/public/icon.png]() * Brand SVG: [https://github.com/PLANIT-TECH/lawbster-mcp/blob/main/public/lawbster-logo.svg]() ### Tools (8) | Tool | Purpose | | -- | -- | | | \`legal_search | | Hybrid search across DE federal law, EU law, federal court decision | | | \`legal_lookup | | Full text by exact citation (`§ 823 BGB`, `Art. 6 GDPR`, `C-311/18`, `BGH VI ZR 175/22` | | | \`legal_lookup_batch | | Up to 20 lookups in one cal | | | \`legal_get_context | | Surrounding norms before/after a citatio | | | \`legal_find_citing_decisions | | DE federal courts citing a specific nor | | | \`legal_list_laws | | Discovery — what's in the inde | | | \`legal_get_toc | | Table of contents of a la | | | \`legal_get_stats | | Index statistics + last update timestam | ### NPM package `@planit-lawbster/lawbster-mcp` — Sigstore provenance signed.
[https://www.npmjs.com/package/@planit-lawbster/lawbster-mcp]() Thanks!

title: [Feature] Add `searchFCModel` and `reasoning` flags to `lh agent edit`
body:
## Description

The CLI command `lh agent edit` currently does not support modifying `chatConfig.searchFCModel`, `chatConfig.enableReasoning`, or `chatConfig.reasoningBudgetToken`. These fields are visible via `lh agent view --json` and configurable via the web UI, but the CLI has no flags to update them.

This blocks programmatic/bulk agent optimization workflows (e.g., switching all agents to a budget FC model via script).

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
$ lh agent view <agentId> --json
# Shows: chatConfig.searchFCModel: {"model": "deepseek-v4-pro", "provider": "lobehub"}

$ lh agent edit <agentId> --fc-model "qwen/qwen3.5-flash" --fc-provider "openrouter"
error: unknown option '--fc-model'
```

## Expected Behavior

New flags for `lh agent edit`:

| Flag | Field | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `--fc-model <model>` | `chatConfig.searchFCModel.model` | Model for function calling / search |
| `--fc-provider <provider>` | `chatConfig.searchFCModel.provider` | Provider for FC model |
| `--enable-reasoning` | `chatConfig.enableReasoning = true` | Enable reasoning (chain-of-thought) |
| `--no-reasoning` | `chatConfig.enableReasoning = false` | Disable reasoning |
| `--reasoning-budget <n>` | `chatConfig.reasoningBudgetToken` | Max reasoning tokens |
| `--search-mode <mode>` | `chatConfig.searchMode` | Search mode (auto/manual/off) |

## Impact

This enables bulk agent optimization, cost reduction workflows (switching FC models to budget options), and parity between web UI and CLI capabilities.

## Additional Context

Currently all agents default to `deepseek-v4-pro` for `searchFCModel`, even agents whose primary model is `qwen3.5-flash` (100x cheaper). Bulk-switching FC models via CLI would immediately cut 60-80% of function-calling token costs.

title: [Bug] Cloudflare Turnstile rejects all /api/workflows/add-mcp-plugin requests (submit + claim + rescan)
body:
### 📦 Platform

LobeHub web ([lobehub.com](<http://lobehub.com>))

### 📌 Version

Current production (reproduced 2026-05-08)

### 💻 Operating System

macOS

### 🌐 Browser

Reproduced in two browsers (Chrome + Safari) on macOS, including incognito/private mode, both on home WiFi and cellular tether.

### 🐛 Bug Description

The Cloudflare Turnstile validator on `POST /api/workflows/add-mcp-plugin` consistently rejects every submitted token, returning HTTP 400 with the structured error:

```json
{
  "code": "workflows.add_mcp_plugin.turnstile_failed",
  "detail": "Cloudflare Turnstile rejected the supplied token.",
  "error": "Human verification failed",
  "status": 400,
  "title": "Bad Request",
  "instance": "/api/workflows/add-mcp-plugin"
}
```

This affects **three distinct user workflows that share the endpoint:**

1. **Submit a new MCP server** (web modal at [https://lobehub.com/mcp](<https://lobehub.com/mcp>) → "Submit MCP")
2. **Claim ownership** of an existing auto-scraped listing
3. **Rescan** an existing listing for updated metadata

All three return the same `turnstile_failed` error, suggesting the issue is server-side in the Turnstile validator config (site-key/secret mismatch, expired key, or risk-score threshold set too aggressively) rather than user-environment specific.

### 📷 Recurrence Steps

1. Sign in to [https://lobehub.com](<https://lobehub.com>) via GitHub OAuth.
2. Navigate to [https://lobehub.com/mcp](<https://lobehub.com/mcp>).
3. Click "Submit MCP" (or, on an existing listing page, "Claim" or "Rescan").
4. Fill in the GitHub repository URL.
5. Wait for the Turnstile widget to issue a token.
6. Click Submit.
7. Observe HTTP 400 with `workflows.add_mcp_plugin.turnstile_failed` in the network panel.

Reproduced across:

* ✗ Chrome (latest, with extensions)
* ✗ Chrome incognito (no extensions)
* ✗ Safari (default config)
* ✗ Two networks: home WiFi (residential ISP) and cellular tether (different ASN)
* ✗ Submit-within-60-seconds-of-page-load (rules out token expiry)
* ✗ Single-click only (rules out double-redemption)

### 🚦 Expected Behavior

Turnstile validates the token and the request proceeds: the new listing is created, ownership is claimed, or the existing listing is rescanned.

### 📝 Additional Information

This is a **widespread issue affecting many submitters**. Issues lobehub/lobehub#14133 (Longbridge, 2026-04-24), lobehub/lobehub#14396 (Parse, 2026-05-03), lobehub/lobehub#14467 (Lawbster, 2026-05-06), and lobehub/lobehub#14481 (Great Question, 2026-05-07) all explicitly cite the same Turnstile failure as the reason for filing a `[Request] Add X` issue as a fallback. The fact that submitters have organically adopted GitHub issues as the documented fallback suggests this has been broken for \~2+ weeks.

I've also filed a `[Request]` issue for my own server (lobehub/lobehub#14528) to get into the queue, but the underlying Turnstile bug deserves a separate fix because it's blocking everyone in the backlog and the maintainer cost of batch-processing the `[Request]` issues scales linearly with the bug duration.

**Suggested investigation priority:**

1. Check the Turnstile site-key currently embedded in the [lobehub.com](<http://lobehub.com>) web client matches the secret-key the `/api/workflows/add-mcp-plugin` validator is using server-side. Most common cause of universal `turnstile_failed` is a key-rotation desync.
2. Check the Turnstile dashboard for the validator's recent reject reasons (Cloudflare logs each rejection with a code: `expired-token`, `invalid-input-secret`, `bad-request`, `internal-error`, etc.). The specific code will pinpoint the cause.
3. If the validator is using `Cf-Connecting-IP` or similar to feed risk scoring, check whether residential IPs (especially APAC/Australia) are being mass-rejected.

Happy to provide additional diagnostic info (HAR file, full network trace) if useful.

title: [Bug] Visual understanding tool breaks Claude (Bedrock) with anyOf schema — Error 471
body:
## Bug Report

### Summary
The visual understanding tool introduced in **v2.1.57-canary.2** ([#14378](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/pull/14378)) causes a complete skill failure when using **Claude models via Bedrock** provider. The tool schema uses `anyOf` in its parameter definition, which is not supported by the Bedrock runtime for Claude and results in an **Error 471**.

### Affected versions
- **Broken**: v2.1.57-canary.2 through v2.1.57-canary.9 (latest at time of report)
- **Working**: v2.1.56 stable (visual understanding tool not present)

### Provider / Model
- **Provider**: Bedrock
- **Model**: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (`global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`)
- Not tested on Anthropic direct (may behave differently)

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install v2.1.57-canary.2 or later
2. Use any agent with Claude via Bedrock provider
3. Enable or activate the visual understanding tool / skill
4. Send any message (even without an image)
5. Observe Error 471 — the tool schema fails validation on the Bedrock side

### Expected behavior
Claude via Bedrock should be able to use the visual understanding tool without errors. The tool parameters should be formatted in a way compatible with Bedrock's schema validation.

### Actual behavior
Error 471 is thrown. The `anyOf` construct in the tool schema is not accepted by the Bedrock runtime for Claude. This makes the entire skill system non-functional when the visual understanding tool is loaded.

### Root cause analysis
The tool schema for `visual_understanding` uses `anyOf` in its parameter definition. Bedrock's Claude runtime does **not** support `anyOf` in tool schemas — it requires a flat, explicit type definition.

The canary.9 commits ([#14428](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/pull/14428) `agentDispatcher.selectRuntimeType` and [#14425](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/pull/14425) `extract producer pipeline`) appear to lay the **infrastructure** for a fix by allowing provider-specific schema formatting. However, if the manifest of `visual_understanding` still hardcodes `anyOf`, the dispatcher improvement alone may not be sufficient.

### Workaround
Downgrade to **v2.1.56 stable**. The visual understanding tool is not present in that release.

### Additional context
- PR that introduced the tool: [#14378](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/pull/14378)
- Potentially related infrastructure fix: [#14428](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/pull/14428), [#14425](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/pull/14425)
- Bedrock does not support `anyOf` in tool/function calling schemas — this is a known AWS Bedrock limitation
- Anthropic direct API may handle `anyOf` differently and may not be affected

### Suggested fix
In the `visual_understanding` tool manifest, replace `anyOf` with explicit, flat type definitions compatible with Bedrock's schema validation requirements. Alternatively, use the new `selectRuntimeType` infrastructure (canary.9) to serve a Bedrock-compatible schema variant when the Bedrock runtime is detected.

title: [Bug] MCP stdio pre-check timeout (5s) too short for npx/bunx first-time download
body:
## Problem

When adding a custom MCP server with an `npx` or `bunx` command, the connection pre-check fires a hardcoded **5-second timeout**. On first run, npx/bunx must download the package before the server can start — this takes 15-60+ seconds depending on package size and network speed.

**Result**: LobeHub always reports `INITIALIZATION_TIMEOUT` for any npx/bunx MCP server that hasn't been pre-cached. The server actually works fine; the problem is the timeout fires before the download completes.

## Workaround

Manually run the npx/bunx command in a terminal once to cache the package, then retry adding the MCP server in LobeHub.

## Expected behaviour

The pre-check timeout should be long enough for first-run downloads (60s+), or configurable via an environment variable (e.g. `MCP_STARTUP_TIMEOUT`).

## Code location

`src/libs/mcp/client.ts` — `preCheckStdioCommand()`, the `setTimeout(..., 5000)` block.

## Context

- The existing `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` constant (line ~27) already uses the correct configurable pattern — this bug is that the pre-check timeout didn't follow the same pattern.
- Affects all npx/bunx MCP servers on first run (before local cache exists).
- Affected versions: all versions including current canary.
- Platform: Windows 11 Desktop (likely affects all platforms).

## Labels

`bug`, `area:mcp`

title: OpenAI prompt_cache_key is too broad for group chat workflows
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Web (Desktop Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📌 Version

canary

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

After PR #14349, LobeChat automatically adds `prompt_cache_key` for OpenAI-compatible requests.

The generated key appears to be scoped as:

```text
lobe:${user}:${model}
```

This is too broad for multi-agent/group chat workflows.

When a supervisor agent delegates work to other agents, multiple parallel requests can come from the same user using the same model. Those requests receive the same `prompt_cache_key`, even though they belong to different delegated agent runs.

This can cause separate agent streams/runs to share the same cache/session identity, which may lead to streaming responses failing, ending early, or behaving unpredictably during group chat delegation.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Use a canary build that includes PR #14349.
2. Configure an OpenAI-compatible provider with a GPT/o-series model.
3. Start a group chat / multi-agent workflow where a supervisor delegates work to one or more agents.
4. Make sure multiple delegated agents can run in parallel with the same user and model.
5. Observe that the generated `prompt_cache_key` is the same for those parallel requests because it only includes `user` and `model`.
6. Some streaming responses may fail or end early when these parallel delegated requests overlap.

### 🚦 What it should be?

`prompt_cache_key` should not collide between parallel delegated agent runs.

For normal single-agent chats, `lobe:${user}:${model}` may be fine. But for group chat / supervisor delegation, the key should include narrower workflow context, for example:

```text
lobe:${user}:${agentId}:${sessionId}:${model}
```

or at least:

```text
lobe:${user}:${agentId}:${model}
```

If LobeChat cannot safely scope the key for delegated/parallel agent calls, it should avoid adding `prompt_cache_key` automatically for those calls.

### 📝 Additional Information

This seems related to PR #14349:

https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/pull/14349

The implementation added automatic `prompt_cache_key` generation in `packages/model-runtime/src/core/openaiCompatibleFactory/index.ts`.

The current comment says:

```ts
// Keep the default key at {userId}:{model}; {agentId} can be added later if a narrower cache bucket is needed.
```

I think group chat / supervisor delegation is exactly the case where a narrower cache bucket is needed.

Suggested fix:
- Preserve custom user-provided `prompt_cache_key` values.
- Keep simple single-agent behavior if desired.
- For delegated/group chat agent calls, include agent/session/run context in the generated cache key.
- Add tests ensuring two delegated agents from the same user using the same model do not receive the same automatic `prompt_cache_key`.

### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?

Yes, I am willing to submit a PR

title: [Bug] Windows 客户端本地命令执行时中文输出乱码 (cmd.exe encoding issue)
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Desktop App (Electron)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Other

### 📌 Version

v2.1.57

### 🌐 Browser

Other

### 🐛 What happened?

在 Windows 环境下使用 LobeHub 桌面客户端时，调用“本地系统 (Local System)”插件/工具的 `runCommand` 执行命令（例如 `echo 测试` 或读取带有中文的返回值），输出的中文字符会变成乱码 ``。

这是因为客户端底层在执行命令或相应的插件在调用 Node.js 的 `child_process.exec` 时，默认使用 `UTF-8` 编码来解析命令行的标准流输出。但 Windows 中文版的 `cmd.exe` 及其控制台环境默认代码页通常是 `cp936` (即 GBK)。Node.js 无法自动识别这个区别，直接将 GBK 的二进制流强行按照 UTF-8 去解析，导致了中文内容发生不可逆的乱码。

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. 在 Windows 电脑上运行 LobeHub 桌面版客户端。
2. 配置好环境并在对话框触发 AI，让其使用 Local System (或类似功能的) 插件执行命令。
3. 执行一条带有中文输出的命令（如：`ipconfig`、`ping` 或仅仅执行 `echo 中文测试`）。
4. 观察插件抓取并返回给 AI 的 Output 内容，会发现中文字符变成了乱码标识符（）。

### 🚦 What it should be?

命令行的输出应该能正确解析中文字符并不出现乱码。

应当判断所在的操作系统及语言环境，在 Windows 中执行本地命令时可以覆盖默认的 UTF-8 解析行为，例如通过将执行输出设为二进制 Buffer。然后引入 `iconv-lite` 等转码库，手动通过 `cp936` 进行解码。

或者设置选择调用CMD还是Powershell等系统工具

### 📝 Additional Information

代码逻辑修复参考：
```javascript
const { exec } = require('child_process');
const iconv = require('iconv-lite');

// 关键1：设定 encoding 为 buffer，阻止 Node.js 的默认处理
exec('ipconfig', { encoding: 'buffer' }, (error, stdout) => {
    if (error) {
        console.error(error);
        return;
    }
    // 关键2：将获取到的 Buffer 按照操作系统的真实代码页（Windows 中文下为 cp936）进行解码
    const result = iconv.decode(stdout, 'cp936');
    console.log(result);
});
```
建议 LobeHub 开发者可在插件/命令执行的引擎侧增加检测，自动针对 Windows 环境屏蔽乱码。

*(本 Issue 由用户与 LobeHub AI 助手共同排查并提交)*

title: bug: rustfs-init fails with minio/mc probe-bsign incompatibility (Connection closed by foreign host)
body:
## Bug Description

The official docker-compose deployment script uses `minio/mc` to initialize the RustFS S3 bucket. However, when `mc alias set` is executed, it sends a probe request to a dynamic path like `/probe-bsign-xxx/?location=` to verify connectivity. RustFS closes the TCP connection on this path instead of returning a proper HTTP response, causing `mc` to fail with:

```
mc: <ERROR> Unable to initialize new alias from the provided credentials.
Get "http://rustfs:9000/probe-bsign-nzevtk9o6yebuolxtmpa3pbhl921pj/?location=": Connection closed by foreign host http://rustfs:9000/probe-bsign-nzevtk9o6yebuolxtmpa3pbhl921pj/?location=. Retry again.
```

This causes `lobe-rustfs-init` to exit with code 1 every time, which blocks the main `lobehub` container from starting (since it depends on `rustfs-init: service_completed_successfully`).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy using the official docker-compose
2. Run `docker compose up -d`
3. `lobe-rustfs-init` fails immediately after rustfs becomes healthy

## Environment

- minio/mc: `RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z`
- rustfs/rustfs: `latest`
- Platform: arm64 (Apple Silicon)

## Root Cause

`minio/mc` uses a probe-bsign mechanism to validate server credentials before executing any command. RustFS does not implement this probe path and closes the connection instead of returning an error response, which `mc` interprets as a fatal connection failure.

Note: RustFS's `/health` endpoint works fine (which is why the healthcheck passes), but the S3 API probe path is not handled.

## Suggested Fix

Replace `minio/mc` with `amazon/aws-cli` in the `rustfs-init` service, which uses standard S3 API calls without the probe mechanism:

```yaml
rustfs-init:
  image: amazon/aws-cli:latest
  environment:
    AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
    AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
    AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: us-east-1
    NO_PROXY: '*'
    no_proxy: '*'
  entrypoint: /bin/sh
  command: >
    -c '
      set -eux;
      aws --endpoint-url http://rustfs:9000 s3 mb s3://lobe --region us-east-1 || true;
      aws --endpoint-url http://rustfs:9000 s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket lobe --policy file:///bucket.config.json;
    '
```

Alternatively, this issue could be fixed on the RustFS side by returning a proper HTTP 403/404 response for unknown paths instead of closing the TCP connection.

## References

- Related RustFS issue: https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/issues/522
- minio/mc probe behavior: https://github.com/minio/mc/issues/5238

https://github.com/EmblemCompany/Agent-skills

EmblemAI is a hosted Model Context Protocol server that gives AI agents a full-featured crypto wallet plus 200+ tools for trading, DeFi, NFTs, and on-chain analytics across 7 blockchains — Bitcoin, Solana, Ethereum, Base, BSC, Polygon, and Hedera.

* Website: https://emblemvault.ai

* Repo license: MIT (covers stdio bridge + documentation; hosted MCP itself is managed SaaS)
* Glama listing: https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/EmblemCompany/Agent-skills

- [x] Has README
- [x] Provides ≥1 installation method (hosted HTTP via `claude mcp add`, stdio bridge via `npx -y @emblemvault/mcp`)
- [x] Has ≥1 Skill (200+ MCP tools across 7 chains)
- [x] Has LICENSE (MIT)
- [x] Offers friendly installation (one-liner for hosted; npx for stdio)
- [ ] Includes Prompts

* Streamable HTTP at `https://emblemvault.ai/api/mcp` (canonical)
* Stdio bridge: `@emblemvault/mcp` (npm)

{

}

title: feat(task): snapshot current agent model into task config at execution time
body:
## Background

When a task is triggered, it currently inherits the executing agent's model at runtime without persisting that choice. This means if the user later changes the agent's default model (e.g. from a task-appropriate model to `gpt-5.4 pro` for regular chat), all existing/pending tasks will silently start using the new model on their next run — potentially incurring unexpected high costs or producing incorrect results.

**Root cause observed in production:**  
A team member set their LobeAI agent default to `gpt-5.4 pro` for chat. A previously-created cron task then picked up that model on its next scheduled run, bypassing any intent about which model should be used for task execution.

## Expected Behavior

When a task starts executing, the runtime should **snapshot the agent's current model configuration into the task config** (e.g. a `modelConfig` or `executionModel` field). Subsequent runs should use this persisted model unless the user explicitly overrides it.

## Proposed Solution

- On task creation / first execution, write the current agent model (and relevant params like ,  if applicable) into the task's config record.
- Expose a UI affordance so users can see / override which model the task runs with, independently of the agent's default chat model.
- Add a pre-check / warning if the task's persisted model differs significantly from the agent's current default (e.g. cost tier mismatch).

## Impact

- **Cost control**: prevents accidental use of premium chat models for background/scheduled tasks.
- **Predictability**: task behavior is reproducible regardless of what the user sets as their chat model later.
- **Auditability**: task run logs can clearly show which model was used.

## Related

- Discussion triggered by: team member's task running `gpt-5.4 pro` due to agent default model change, causing abnormal token spend.

body:
**MCP listing:** https://lobehub.com/mcp/promptibus-mcp

## Background

- **npm:** `@promptibus/mcp` v0.9.0 (public, MIT licensed)
- **GitHub:** https://github.com/promptibus/mcp (public, with SLSA provenance + auto-publish workflow)
- **MCP Registry:** published under DNS-verified `com.promptibus` namespace
- **Smithery:** https://smithery.ai/server/@promptibus/mcp (validated)

## Issue

Unable to claim/validate ownership via the LobeHub UI. every attempt to call `/api/workflows/add-mcp-plugin` is rejected by Cloudflare Turnstile with `HTTP 400 workflows.add_mcp_plugin.turnstile_failed`. This is the same problem documented in #14529 (open, ~2 weeks).

## Request

Could you (@canisminor1990?) manually flag the `promptibus-mcp` listing as validated, since the self-service path is currently broken?

Happy to verify ownership via any out-of-band channel:
- DNS TXT record on `promptibus.com`
- GitHub repo control proof
- MCP Registry DNS verification public key (already on promptibus.com)

Thanks!

title: 🐛 fix: LaTeX formula not rendered in document view (only works in preview)
body:
## Bug Description

LaTeX/math formulas in documents are not rendered in the main document view, but they render correctly in the preview interface.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a document with LaTeX math formulas (e.g., `$\sinh t$`, `$`)
2. View the document in the normal document view
3. Formulas appear as raw LaTeX source text instead of rendered math

## Expected Behavior

Math formulas should be rendered (as shown in the preview interface).

## Actual Behavior

Formulas display as raw LaTeX strings like `$\sinh t$`, `$` etc.

## Screenshots

- **Document view (broken)**: formulas show as raw LaTeX
- **Preview interface (working)**: formulas render correctly with proper math notation

## Environment

Reported via Discord community feedback.

## Additional Context

The preview interface renders formulas correctly, suggesting the math rendering library is available but not being applied in the document view renderer.

title: [Request] Add Medical Terminologies MCP Server to the MCP marketplace
body:
## MCP server submission

The web form at https://lobehub.com/mcp returns HTTP 500 (the badge endpoint
`/badge/mcp/sidneybissoli-medical-terminologies-mcp` is also 500). Filing here
as the documented fallback path, in line with #14133 (Longbridge) and #14467
(Lawbster).

### Repository

https://github.com/SidneyBissoli/medical-terminologies-mcp

### About Medical Terminologies MCP

Unified MCP server providing programmatic access to **7 major medical
terminologies** from a single endpoint:

- **ICD-11** — WHO international classification of diseases (current revision)
- **SNOMED CT** — Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine (opt-in; requires self-hosted Snowstorm + IHTSDO license)
- **LOINC** — Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes
- **RxNorm** — Normalized names for clinical drugs (NIH)
- **MeSH** — Medical Subject Headings (NLM; PubMed's indexing vocabulary)
- **ATC** — Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification, via NLM RxClass
- **CID-10** — Brazilian Portuguese translation of ICD-10 (DataSUS V2008, bundled)

Audience: biomedical researchers, public-health analysts (incl. Brazil/SUS),
clinical-informatics developers, educators. Explicitly **not** a clinical
decision-support tool — clinicians have specialized assistants for that.

* Operator: independent maintainer (Sidney Bissoli)
* License: **MIT** (the server code; bundled terminology data follows each
  source's license — WHO CC BY-ND 3.0 IGO, LOINC license, etc.)
* Hosted endpoint: `https://medical-terminologies-mcp.sidneybissoli.workers.dev/mcp`
  (Cloudflare Workers; WHO credentials configured server-side — all 31 default
  tools work without setup on the client side)

### Quality checklist

- [x] Has README
- [x] Provides ≥1 installation method (`npx -y medical-terminologies-mcp`, manual JSON, Docker, hosted URL)
- [x] Has LICENSE (MIT)
- [x] Includes **3 Prompts** (`find-medical-code`, `drug-info`, `cid10-portuguese-lookup`)
- [x] Includes **4 Resources** (`info://server`, `info://cid10/chapters`, `info://licenses`, `info://stats`)
- [x] Registered in the official MCP Registry as `io.github.SidneyBissoli/medical-terminologies-mcp` (10 versions, latest `1.5.0`)
- [x] Public usage stats counter — `/stats` and `info://stats` resource (Cloudflare Durable Object)
- [x] Daily integration-test CI against live upstream APIs (surfaces drift)

### Transport & authentication

* **stdio** — for Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.
* **Streamable HTTP** at `https://medical-terminologies-mcp.sidneybissoli.workers.dev/mcp`
* No auth required for the hosted endpoint. ICD-11 tools (5 of 37) need WHO
  credentials when self-hosting — set `WHO_CLIENT_ID` / `WHO_CLIENT_SECRET`
  (free registration at https://icd.who.int/icdapi). Other terminologies work
  unauthenticated.

### Configuration example

**Hosted (no install):**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "medical-terminologies": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://medical-terminologies-mcp.sidneybissoli.workers.dev/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

**Local (npx, stdio):**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "medical-terminologies": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "medical-terminologies-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "WHO_CLIENT_ID": "your-id",
        "WHO_CLIENT_SECRET": "your-secret"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

title: Feature Request: Allow AI Assistant to Perceive Current Conversation Token Usage Context
body:
## Problem Description

Users can see the current conversation's token consumption details in the LobeHub UI, but the AI assistant itself is completely unaware of this. This prevents the AI from judging how token-intensive its own behavior is.

## Proposed Solution

Before each response, the platform injects a token usage data entry into the context, formatted as:
`[Context Usage: profile=30K, skills=29.8K, messages=1.2K, used=31K, max=1M]`

This way, the AI can perceive the consumption and avoid unnecessary waste.

## Alternative Solution

Similar to SillyTavern's "regex replacement" feature - allowing users to automatically transform content before sending messages, automatically appending the UI's token data to the end of messages while keeping it hidden from the user's view.

## Expected Platform
LobeHub v1.x+

---
> This issue was translated by Claude.

<details>
<summary>Original Content</summary>

## 问题描述

用户可以在 LobeHub UI 中看到当前对话的 token 消耗详情，但 AI 助手本身对此一无所知。导致 AI 无法判断自己的行为有多耗 token。

## 建议方案

在每次回复前，由平台在上下文中注入一条 token 用量数据，格式如：
[Context Usage: profile=30K, skills=29.8K, messages=1.2K, used=31K, max=1M]

这样 AI 就能感知到消耗，避免无谓的浪费。

## 备选方案

类似 SillyTavern 的"正则替换"功能——允许用户在发送消息前自动转换内容，把 UI 的 token 数据自动附加到消息末尾，同时对自己隐藏。

## 期望平台
LobeHub v1.x+
</details>

title: Memory persona workflow may ignore configured provider and route to DeepSeek Anthropic endpoint
body:
### Summary

In the self-hosted memory user-memory workflow, the `persona/update-writing` pipeline can ignore or bypass the memory-specific provider/baseURL/API key configuration and route to another enabled provider.

This caused `persona/update-writing` to route to DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic`) even when I intended to use an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`https://api.deepseek.com/v1`). The workflow then failed with the Anthropic SDK non-streaming long request guard.

### Environment

- Project: self-hosted LobeHub / LobeChat
- Image: `lobehub/lobehub:canary`
- Image ID: `sha256:1cc367e4c0400000f4f05531b9c240f34f5b1352098d300bbf7db1ef6ded4676`
- Image created: `2026-05-14T19:13:36.095959966Z`
- Deployment: Docker Compose
- Memory workflow callback URL example:
  - `/api/workflows/memory-user-memory/pipelines/persona/update-writing`

### Failure 1: built-in `deepseek` provider routes persona writer to Anthropic endpoint and fails

With memory persona writer configured to use the built-in `deepseek` provider, the workflow failed:

```env
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_PERSONA_WRITER_PROVIDER=deepseek
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_PERSONA_WRITER_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash
```

The workflow endpoint returned HTTP 500:

```text
POST /api/workflows/memory-user-memory/pipelines/persona/update-writing -> 500
```

The server log / response body contained:

```text
endpoint: https://api.de****ek.com/anthropic
provider: deepseek
errorType: ProviderBizError
message: Streaming is required for operations that may take longer than 10 minutes. See https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript#long-requests for more details
```

Relevant stack trace excerpt:

```text
Error: Streaming is required for operations that may take longer than 10 minutes.
    at rs.calculateNonstreamingTimeout (...)
    at t9.create (...)
    at async Object.generateObject (...)
    at async Object.runWithFallback (...)
    at async nN.generateObject (...)
    at async i.toolCall (...)
    at async Object.composeWriting (...)
```

### Expected behavior for failure 1

If the memory workflow uses structured/tool-call generation in a non-streaming path, the built-in DeepSeek provider should not route this path in a way that triggers Anthropic SDK's non-streaming long-request guard. Possible fixes might include using DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible endpoint for this workflow path, using streaming where required, or avoiding the long non-streaming Anthropic SDK configuration.

### Failure 2: `MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_PERSONA_WRITER_PROVIDER=openai` can still fall back to another enabled provider

I then attempted to force DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible API by configuring the memory LLM stages as OpenAI-compatible:

```env
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_GATEKEEPER_PROVIDER=openai
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_GATEKEEPER_MODEL=deepseek-chat
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_GATEKEEPER_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/v1
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_GATEKEEPER_API_KEY=<set>

MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_LAYER_EXTRACTOR_PROVIDER=openai
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_LAYER_EXTRACTOR_MODEL=deepseek-chat
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_LAYER_EXTRACTOR_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/v1
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_LAYER_EXTRACTOR_API_KEY=<set>

MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_PERSONA_WRITER_PROVIDER=openai
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_PERSONA_WRITER_MODEL=deepseek-chat
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_PERSONA_WRITER_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/v1
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_PERSONA_WRITER_API_KEY=<set>
```

`deepseek-chat` on `https://api.deepseek.com/v1/chat/completions` supports tool calls in a direct smoke test:

```text
model=deepseek-chat -> HTTP 200, finish_reason=tool_calls
```

However, the memory workflow still failed and the logs showed:

```text
[ai-infra] no enabled provider found for persona writer "deepseek-chat" (preferred openai), falling back to server-configured provider "openai".
[memory-extraction] skipping provider openai due to missing API key in user vault
endpoint: https://api.de****ek.com/anthropic
provider: deepseek
message: Streaming is required for operations that may take longer than 10 minutes.
```

In this self-hosted setup:

- The user-level `openai` provider row was disabled and had no user key vault.
- The user-level `deepseek` provider was enabled and had a key vault.
- The memory-specific env vars above had a system API key and baseURL for the configured `openai` provider.

So the runtime skipped the configured preferred provider because there was no user-vault key, then continued to another enabled provider (`deepseek`) and eventually routed to `/anthropic`.

### Expected behavior for failure 2

When memory-specific env vars provide an explicit provider, API key, and baseURL, the memory workflow should use those system-level values even if the user-level provider key vault is empty.

In other words, this should be honored:

```env
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_PERSONA_WRITER_PROVIDER=openai
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_PERSONA_WRITER_MODEL=deepseek-chat
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_PERSONA_WRITER_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/v1
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_PERSONA_WRITER_API_KEY=<set>
```

The runtime should not continue to a different enabled provider after skipping `openai` due to a missing user-vault key.

### Suspected causes

From inspecting the compiled runtime, there appear to be two related issues:

1. `UserPersonaService.composeWriting` / persona writer provider matching does not pass a preferred provider constraint equivalent to gatekeeper/layer extraction. This allows persona writer matching to select another enabled provider with a matching model.
2. The memory runtime provider resolver checks user-vault credentials first. If the preferred/configured provider has no user-vault API key, it logs a skip and continues to other providers, instead of using the memory-specific system fallback API key/baseURL.

### Workaround that fixed the issue locally

I applied runtime hotfixes locally:

1. Force persona writer provider matching to include the configured provider as a preferred provider.
2. If the preferred provider has no user-vault key but matches the configured memory agent provider and `MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_*_API_KEY` is set, use the system fallback API key/baseURL instead of continuing to another provider.

After these hotfixes and this config:

```env
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_GATEKEEPER_PROVIDER=openai
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_GATEKEEPER_MODEL=deepseek-chat
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_GATEKEEPER_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/v1

MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_LAYER_EXTRACTOR_PROVIDER=openai
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_LAYER_EXTRACTOR_MODEL=deepseek-chat
MEMORY_USER_MEMORY_LAYER_EXTRACTOR_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/v1

title: Settings / custom model form: label accessibility (for vs focusable id), extend-params dropdown width, modal label truncation
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Web (Desktop Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Other

### 📌 Version

2.1.57

### 🌐 Browser

Firefox

### 🐛 What happened?

  #### 1. Incorrect `<label for="…">` (accessibility / Lighthouse)
  On the custom model form (and similar provider UI), DevTools / Lighthouse report:
  > Incorrect use of `<label for="FORM_ELEMENT">` — the label’s `for` attribute doesn’t match any element id.
  Concrete examples from the DOM:
  - Label text related to **max context window** → `for="contextWindowTokens"` but no matching `id="contextWindowTokens"` on the actual 
  focusable control (Ant Design `InputNumber` / wrapper chain).
  - Label **extended parameters** → `for="settings_extendParams"` but the visible combobox input uses an auto-generated id instead.
  **Impact:** click-to-focus from label, some assistive tech behaviors, and noisy a11y audits.
  **Expected:** `Form.Item`-generated labels should reference the real focusable node (`id` propagated through custom wrappers).
  ---
  #### 2. “Extended parameters” dropdown far too wide / overflows viewport

  The multi-select dropdown for extended parameters can become extremely wide (long option hints). With placement such as `bottomRight`, the  panel grows leftward and **overflows off-screen**.
  **Expected:** dropdown width constrained to the trigger / viewport; long option text should wrap instead of forcing huge horizontal size.

  ---
  #### 3. Custom model configuration modal — labels truncated / cramped layout
  In the **custom model** modal, long translated labels (e.g. FR) are **truncated** or hard to read because:
  - horizontal form layout uses a **very narrow** label column;
  - default Ant Design form label styling uses **single-line / hidden overflow** unless `labelWrap` / wider columns / vertical layout on small
   screens are used.
  **Expected:** labels readable in common locales without ellipsis/clipping; optional vertical layout on narrow widths.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

  1. Go to **Settings → Provider** (e.g. vLLM).
  2. Open **custom model configuration** (create or edit).
  3. Open **extended parameters** multi-select and inspect layout + Lighthouse a11y on the form fields above.

### 🚦 What it should be?

_No response_

### 📝 Additional Information

  ### Possible direction for fixes 
  - Forward `id` from `Form.Item` through wrappers (`MaxTokenSlider` → `InputNumber`, `ExtendParamsSelect` → `Select`).
  - Tame select dropdown width (`popupMatchSelectWidth`, `maxWidth`, wrapping option content).
  - Adjust modal form layout: `labelWrap`, responsive `labelCol` / `wrapperCol`, `layout="vertical"` on small screens, scrollable modal body 
  if needed.

### 🥰 Feature Description

We'd like to list **agent-payment-mcp** on LobeHub's MCP marketplace ([https://lobehub.com/mcp](<https://lobehub.com/mcp>)). The site's "Submit" modal failed with Cloudflare Turnstile error, so filing here as fallback per issue lobehub/lobehub#14529.

### 🧐 Proposed Solution

Please index our repository:

* **Repo**: [https://github.com/evidai/agent-payment-mcp](<https://github.com/evidai/agent-payment-mcp>)
* **npm**: [https://www.npmjs.com/package/agent-payment-mcp](<https://www.npmjs.com/package/agent-payment-mcp>) (v0.6.1)
* **Name**: agent-payment-mcp (LemonCake)
* **Publisher**: EvidAI / LemonCake ([https://lemoncake.xyz](<https://lemoncake.xyz>))
* **License**: MIT
* **Official MCP Registry**: `io.github.evidai/agent-payment` — [https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io](<https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io>)

**What it does**

Give your AI agent a USDC wallet with pay-per-call billing for any HTTP API. No human approval per call. Kill switch + spend caps included. Demo Mode requires zero credentials.

**Tools:** `setup`, `list_services`, `call_service`, `check_balance`, `check_tax`, `get_service_stats`

**Available APIs via call_service:** Serper (Google Search), [Hunter.io](<http://Hunter.io>), Jina Reader, Firecrawl, Slack, IPinfo, Open Exchange Rates, TRUSTDOCK eKYC, and more.

**Transport:** stdio (npx)

**Config:**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pay-per-call": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "agent-payment-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "LEMON_CAKE_BUYER_JWT": "eyJhbGci..."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Leave `LEMON_CAKE_BUYER_JWT` unset → **Demo Mode** (no charges, real APIs, no signup required).

title: Browserless crawler times out on modern frontend pages due to networkidle2 and short upstream timeout
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Other, Web (Desktop Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

Ubuntu

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📌 Version

latest Docker image, self-hosted with lobehub/lobehub

### 🌐 Browser

Firefox

### 🐛 What happened?

When using the self-hosted version of LobeHub with Browserless enabled, the web crawler frequently times out when reading modern frontend pages such as Next.js / SPA pages.

Configuration:
```
BROWSERLESS_URL=http://browserless:3000
BROWSERLESS_TOKEN=***
CRAWLER_IMPLS=browserless
```

Example URL: https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose
When asking the AI to read this page, it fails with a timeout, for example:
```
TimeoutError: Request timeout after 10000ms
```

Browserless logs show that LobeHub does call Browserless successfully:
```
POST /content?blockAds=false&launch=...
Content API invoked with body: {
  gotoOptions: { waitUntil: 'networkidle2' },
  url: 'https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose'
}
200: https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose
```

But Browserless later reports:
```
Error: Request closed prior to writing results
```

This suggests that LobeHub closes the upstream Browserless request before Browserless finishes returning the result.

I verified that this is not a Docker networking, DNS, token, or Browserless availability issue:

- browserless container can access the target URL directly.
- lobehub container can access Browserless /pressure.
- lobehub container can manually call Browserless /content successfully.
- Browserless receives requests from LobeHub when the frontend triggers page reading.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Deploy LobeHub via Docker Compose on Ubuntu.
2. Configure Browserless: 
```
browserless:
  image: ghcr.io/browserless/chromium:v2.49.0
  container_name: browserless
  restart: unless-stopped
  environment:
    - 'TOKEN=${BROWSERLESS_TOKEN}'
    - 'CONCURRENT=10'
    - 'QUEUED=20'
    - 'TIMEOUT=300000'
  shm_size: "2gb"
  networks:
    - lobe-network
  ```

3. Configure LobeHub:
```
BROWSERLESS_URL=http://browserless:3000
BROWSERLESS_TOKEN=***
CRAWLER_IMPLS=browserless
```

4. In the chat UI, ask the AI to read:
```
https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose
```
5. The AI reports that fetching the page timed out.
6. Check Browserless logs. The request is received, but ends with:
```
Error: Request closed prior to writing results
```

I also tested the same Browserless /content request manually from inside the lobehub container.

With LobeHub's current payload using networkidle2:
```
docker exec -it lobehub sh
time wget -S -O /tmp/lobehub.html \
  --header='Content-Type: application/json' \
  --post-data='{"gotoOptions":{"waitUntil":"networkidle2"},"url":"https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose"}' \
  "http://browserless:3000/content?blockAds=false&launch=%7B%22stealth%22%3Afalse%7D&token=$BROWSERLESS_TOKEN"
```

Result:
```
real    0m 18.66s
```

Using load:
```
time wget -S -O /tmp/page-load.html \
  --header='Content-Type: application/json' \
  --post-data='{"gotoOptions":{"waitUntil":"load"},"url":"https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose"}' \
  "http://browserless:3000/content?blockAds=false&launch=%7B%22stealth%22%3Afalse%7D&token=$BROWSERLESS_TOKEN"
```

```
real    0m 4.41s
```

Using domcontentloaded:
```
time wget -S -O /tmp/page-domcontentloaded.html \
  --header='Content-Type: application/json' \
  --post-data='{"gotoOptions":{"waitUntil":"domcontentloaded"},"url":"https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/platform/docker-compose"}' \
  "http://browserless:3000/content?blockAds=false&launch=%7B%22stealth%22%3Afalse%7D&token=$BROWSERLESS_TOKEN"
```

```
real    0m 4.86s
```

For comparison, a lighter page works fine even with networkidle2:
```
time wget -S -O /tmp/microsoft.html \
  --header='Content-Type: application/json' \
  --post-data='{"gotoOptions":{"waitUntil":"networkidle2"},"url":"https://www.microsoft.com"}' \
  "http://browserless:3000/content?blockAds=false&launch=%7B%22stealth%22%3Afalse%7D&token=$BROWSERLESS_TOKEN"
```

```
real    0m 1.54s
```

### 🚦 What it should be?

LobeHub should be able to crawl modern frontend pages reliably when Browserless is configured.

The Browserless crawler should not fail simply because a modern frontend page takes longer to reach networkidle2.

Ideally, self-hosted users should be able to configure Browserless crawler behavior, especially:

- Browserless gotoOptions.waitUntil;
- upstream crawler request timeout;
- optionally, request blocking behavior.

For example, expose environment variables such as:
```
BROWSERLESS_WAIT_UNTIL=load
```
or
```
BROWSERLESS_WAIT_UNTIL=domcontentloaded
```
and:
```
CRAWLER_TIMEOUT=30000
```
The exact names are only suggestions.

Alternatively, consider changing the default Browserless waitUntil from networkidle2 to load or domcontentloaded, since LLM web-reading usually needs text extraction rather than waiting for a fully network-idle page.


### 📝 Additional Information

Root cause appears to be the combination of:
1. Browserless crawler sends:
```
{
  "gotoOptions": {
    "waitUntil": "networkidle2"
  }
}
```
2. Modern Next.js / SPA pages may load many JS chunks, Cloudflare scripts, analytics scripts, external badges, and other resources, causing networkidle2 to take much longer.
3. LobeHub appears to have an upstream request timeout of around 10 seconds.
4. Browserless needs around 18.66 seconds to finish the networkidle2 crawl for the LobeHub docs page, so LobeHub closes the request before Browserless returns the result.

This matches Browserless logs:
```
Request closed prior to writing results
```


I also checked recent commits:
#14817 fix(agent-runtime): honor per-tool timeout end-to-end for client tool dispatch

This seems to affect client-dispatched tools via Agent Gateway / BLPOP / renderer execution.

It does not appear to affect the server-side Browserless crawler path or Browserless /content payload.
#14660 fix(web-crawler): cap response body size to prevent serverless OOM

This affects the naive crawler by capping response body size to 1MB.

It may affect fallback behavior or large-page extraction, but it does not appear to change Browserless gotoOptions.waitUntil or Browserless crawler timeout behavior.


Current workaround

My current workaround is to deploy a lightweight proxy between LobeHub and Browserless:
```
LobeHub -> browserless-proxy -> Browserless
```
The proxy intercepts /content requests and changes:
```
{
  "gotoOptions": {
    "waitUntil": "networkidle2"
  }
}
```
to:
```
{
  "gotoOptions": {
    "waitUntil": "load"
  }
}
```

This reduces the crawl time for the LobeHub docs page from about 18.66s to under 5s, avoiding the timeout.



### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?

None

title: Bug: lobe-local-system treats .tex LaTeX files as binary
body: Description: lobe-local-system readFile function incorrectly treats .tex LaTeX files as binary files and refuses to read them. .tex files are plain text UTF-8/ASCII and should be readable. title: lobe-local-system commands containing double quotes will fail to execute on Windows
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Desktop App (Electron)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Official Cloud

### 📌 Version

2.2.0

### 🌐 Browser

Other, Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

On Windows, the runCommand tool fails to execute any command that contains double-quoted arguments (") .  When agent tries to run such command it will return "Tool execution failed". The agent then tried to use powershell: 
`powershell -Command "test command"`
and the tool returns everything inside the quotes ("test command", in my case a command to create a folder with spaces in C:\, I tested D:\ and still no luck so it shouldn't be a Windows privilege problem) instead of actually executing the command. However commands without double quotes are correctly executed.
I don't know if its a issue caused by something on my end since I can't find a similar issue. But I reproduced this issue on a PC from a friend of mine so I guess it should not be just me?

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

Tell an agent (in my case Lobe AI) to run a command that will contain double quotes such as create a folder with spaces in its name.

The tool will fail to execute, showing Tool execution failed.

### 🚦 What it should be?

The command should run fine and do what it should do (in my test case create a folder under C:\ )

### 📝 Additional Information

I tested Deepseek v4, and Claude models and they all didn't work so I believe it shouldn't be a issue related to models.
The debug view (bug icon) of the tool shows 
Arguments:
```
{
  "description": "",
  "command": "mkdir \"C:\\Test Folder With Spaces\""
}
```
Response:
`Tool execution failed`
Function Call:
```
{
  "apiName": "runCommand",
  "arguments": "{\"description\":\"测试双引号创建含空格的文件夹\",\"command\":\"mkdir \\\"C:\\\\Test Folder With Spaces\\\"\"}",
  "id": "call_00_byeWT6kfSXefxUz6o2Br9585",
  "identifier": "lobe-local-system",
  "type": "builtin"
}
```
Skill state:
```
{
  "success": false,
  "isBackground": false
}
```
Skill intervention:

{

}

title: CLI detection misses tools added through shell PATH setup
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Desktop App (Electron)

### 💻 Operating System

macOS

### 📦 Deployment Platform

_No response_

### 📌 Version

v2.2.1-canary.5

### 🌐 Browser

Other

### 🐛 What happened?

LobeHub Desktop fails to detect some CLI tools installed via `mise` or Homebrew when they are only exposed through shell-initialized `PATH` setup.

This is a LobeChat Desktop issue, not a third-party CLI or provider issue. The CLI tools themselves work correctly in an interactive terminal, but LobeHub Desktop reports them as not detected when launched outside the shell environment.

The current detector appears to rely on the Electron main process `PATH` and then runs commands like `which gemini` / `which qwen`, followed by `--version` validation. It does not appear to hydrate the login shell environment or account for tools added to `PATH` by shell startup files such as `~/.zshrc` or `~/.zprofile`.

As a result, tools installed via:

  - `mise`
  - Homebrew shell setup (`eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"`)

may be visible in Terminal but not visible to LobeHub Desktop when launched from Finder or Launchpad.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

```
(base) ➜  lobe-chat git:(canary) which gemini
/Users/pleasure1234/.local/share/mise/installs/node/latest/bin/gemini
(base) ➜  lobe-chat git:(canary) which qwen  
/Users/pleasure1234/.local/share/mise/installs/node/latest/bin/qwen
```

### 🚦 What it should be?

_No response_

### 📝 Additional Information

The third-party CLIs work correctly in the terminal. The issue is that LobeHub Desktop detects CLI tools using the Electron process environment, which may not include shell-managed paths from mise.

Relevant code appears to be:

- apps/desktop/src/main/modules/toolDetectors/cliAgentDetectors.ts
- resolveCommandPath()
- detectValidatedCommand()

### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?

None

title: [Request] Add linksee-memory to the MCP marketplace
body:
## Feature Description

Request to add **Linksee Memory** to the LobeHub MCP marketplace.

Linksee Memory is a local-first agent memory MCP server that gives any AI agent (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT Desktop) a structured cross-agent brain. Unlike flat-fact memory tools (Mem0, Letta, Zep), it preserves the **WHY** behind every memory using a 6-layer structure and ships a **token-saving file diff cache** with measured 86% savings.

## Proposed Solution

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Name** | Linksee Memory |
| **GitHub** | https://github.com/michielinksee/linksee-memory |
| **npm** | https://www.npmjs.com/package/linksee-memory |
| **Publisher** | Synapse Arrows PTE. LTD. |
| **License** | MIT |
| **MCP Official Registry** | https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io (registered) |
| **Glama** | https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/@michielinksee/linksee-memory |
| **Version** | 0.3.0 |

## Transport

`stdio`

## Authentication

None required. Fully local — no API keys, no cloud, no signup.

Optional env vars:
- `LINKSEE_MEMORY_DIR` — override default `~/.linksee-memory/`
- `LINKSEE_TELEMETRY=basic` — opt-in anonymous usage stats

## Tool Count

**8 tools** exposed:

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `remember` | Store memory in 1 of 6 layers (goal/context/emotion/implementation/caveat/learning) for an entity |
| `recall` | FTS5 + heat-score + momentum composite ranking search, JP/EN trigram support |
| `recall_file` | Complete edit history of a file across sessions, with per-edit user-intent context |
| `update_memory` | Update existing memory entries with new information |
| `list_entities` | List all known entities in memory with summary stats |
| `read_smart` | Diff-only file read — returns only changed chunks on re-reads (86%/99% measured token savings) |
| `forget` | Explicit delete or Ebbinghaus-curve-based auto-sweep |
| `consolidate` | Sleep-mode compression — cluster cold memories into protected learning summaries |

Additionally: 7 Resources, 5 Prompts, Sampling, Roots, and Elicitation support (MCP Five Blocks compliant).

## Config Example

**Claude Code (one-line install):**
```bash
claude mcp add -s user linksee -- npx -y linksee-memory
```

**Claude Desktop / LobeChat `mcpServers` config:**
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "linksee": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "linksee-memory"]
    }
  }
}
```

**Global install (recommended for daily use):**
```bash
npm install -g linksee-memory
```
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "linksee": {
      "command": "linksee-memory"
    }
  }
}
```

## Quality Checklist

| Check | Status |
|-------|--------|
| Has README | Yes (detailed, 500+ lines with architecture diagrams) |
| Provides at least 1 installation method | Yes (npx, npm global, Claude Code one-liner) |
| Has at least 1 Skill/Tool | Yes (8 tools + 7 resources + 5 prompts) |
| Has LICENSE file | Yes (MIT) |
| Offers friendly installation (one-line config) | Yes (`claude mcp add -s user linksee -- npx -y linksee-memory`) |
| Includes Prompts | Yes (5 prompts) |
| Includes Resources | Yes (7 resources with subscribe/listChanged) |

## Additional Info

**Key differentiators:**
1. **6-layer WHY structure** — not flat facts, but goal/context/emotion/implementation/caveat/learning
2. **Cross-agent portability** — single SQLite file at `~/.linksee-memory/memory.db`, readable from Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT
3. **Token savings** — `read_smart` returns only file diffs (86% savings on typical edits, 99% on unchanged re-reads)
4. **Ebbinghaus forgetting curve** — automatic memory decay keeps the store small; caveat-layer lessons are protected
5. **JP/EN bilingual** — trigram search supports both Japanese and English queries
6. **MCP Five Blocks compliant** — Tools + Resources + Prompts + Sampling + Roots + Elicitation

**Community traction:**
- 4 featured articles on Zenn (Japanese dev platform): 73+ likes, 165+ Hatena Bookmark
- Listed on Glama.ai awesome-mcp-servers
- Registered on MCP Official Registry

**Note:** Previous submission (#13912) was closed. Resubmitting with complete structured format per marketplace guidelines. Web form submission is currently unavailable due to Turnstile validation issue (#14529).

title: bug: multi-agent broadcast with document write causes PostgreSQL insert failure and session freeze
body:
## Bug Description

When issuing a broadcast command to all agents in a group to review previous conversation context and write to a document, the session becomes completely unresponsive. The backend logs show a **PostgreSQL insert failure** on the `messages` table.

## Actual Behavior

- Database query fails: `insert into "messages" ... returning "id"...`
- Error message in UI: "Sending encountered a problem: Failed query..."
- The entire conversation session becomes unusable (frozen)
- All subsequent operations in that session fail

## Error Detail

The PostgreSQL insert error appears to be related to message serialization when multiple agents write concurrently. The failed SQL includes a large batch insert with multiple rows (`values (, , ...), (3, 4, 5...)`), suggesting the system is attempting to write multiple agent response messages in a single transaction and failing.

## Environment

- **Platform**: LobeHub (likely LobeChat)
- **Feature**: Multi-agent group chat with `broadcast` function
- **Trigger**: Calling all agents simultaneously to review context and perform document write operations

## Expected Behavior

Multi-agent broadcast with document write operations should complete gracefully without database failures. If concurrent writes are problematic, the system should handle them sequentially or provide a clear error without freezing the entire session.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a multi-agent group with multiple participant agents
2. Issue a request that triggers all agents to respond simultaneously (broadcast)
3. Include a document write/save operation in the request
4. Observe the session freeze and database error

## Possible Causes

- Race condition in batch message insert when multiple agents complete near-simultaneously
- Parameter serialization mismatch in the batch insert query
- Missing transaction error handling that causes session state corruption rather than graceful recovery

---

title: [Bug] Upstream Sync workflow fails for all forks due to actions-cool/issues-helper being disabled by GitHub
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Other

### 💻 Operating System

Other

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Other

### 📌 Version

v2.2.1-canary.15

### 🌐 Browser

Other

### 🐛 What happened?

The scheduled "Upstream Sync" workflow at `.github/workflows/sync.yml` has been failing for ALL fork repositories since May 19, 2026.

**Error**: `Repository access blocked` at the "Getting action download info" phase.

**Root Cause**: The workflow references `actions-cool/issues-helper@e361abf` (used for opening/closing sync failure issues). On May 19, 2026, this action was compromised in a supply chain attack — attackers moved all tags to point to malicious commits that exfiltrate CI/CD credentials. GitHub has since permanently disabled the repository:
https://github.com/actions-cool/issues-helper

Because the repo is disabled, GitHub Actions cannot download the action, causing ALL fork sync workflows to fail immediately.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Fork the `lobehub/lobehub` repository (or any existing fork)
2. Wait for the scheduled "Upstream Sync" workflow to trigger (every 2 hours)
3. Or manually trigger via `workflow_dispatch` on the Actions tab
4. Observe: workflow fails at initialization with `##[error]Repository access blocked`

### 🚦 What it should be?

Replace `actions-cool/issues-helper` with GitHub CLI commands or a maintained alternative.

**Suggested fix** — replace the issue-helper steps with `gh` CLI:

```yaml
- name: Clean issue notice
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  run: |
    gh issue list --label "🚨 Sync Fail" --state open --json number -q '.[].number' |
    while read num; do gh issue close "$num"; done

- name: Sync check
  if: failure()
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  run: |
    gh issue create \
      --title "🚨 同步失败 | Sync Fail" \
      --label "🚨 Sync Fail" \
      --body "..."
```

**References**:
- Attack report: https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html
- StepSecurity analysis: https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised

### 📝 Additional Information

**Important note**: Because the workflow uses a SHA-pinned reference (`e361abf...`), no malicious code would have executed. However, since GitHub entirely disabled the repo, the action cannot be downloaded at all — hence the "Repository access blocked" error.

The `actions-cool/maintain-one-comment` action was also compromised in the same attack. Please check if it's used elsewhere in this repo.

This issue affects EVERY fork of lobehub/lobehub. The upstream sync workflow is the primary way forks stay updated, so this is a high-priority fix.

title: [Request] Add SaturnZap to the MCP marketplace
body:
### 🥰 Feature Description

We'd like to list **SaturnZap** on LobeHub's MCP marketplace (https://lobehub.com/mcp). Filing here as the documented fallback path per the precedent set by #14133 — happy to also retry the web Submit modal if preferred.

### 🧐 Proposed Solution

Index our GitHub repository:

- **Repo**: https://github.com/lqwdtech/SaturnZap
- **Name**: SaturnZap
- **Publisher**: LQWD Technologies Corp. (https://lqwdclaw.bot) — official
- **License**: MIT
- **Official MCP Registry entry**: `io.github.lqwdtech/saturnzap` — https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=saturnzap (v1.3.1 latest, `isLatest: true`, published 2026-04-23)
- **PyPI**: `saturnzap` v1.3.1

**What it does**

SaturnZap is a non-custodial Bitcoin Lightning Network wallet built specifically for autonomous AI agents. Each agent installs SaturnZap to run its **own** LDK Lightning node, open channels, and autonomously pay L402-gated APIs / paywalls from the CLI or via a built-in MCP server. The agent IS the Lightning node — keys never leave the agent's machine.

**Transport & Auth**

- Transport: `stdio` (local MCP server)
- Auth: Local-only — uses `SZ_PASSPHRASE` env var to decrypt the local wallet seed
- Optional: `SZ_MCP_MAX_SPEND_SATS` for per-request spend caps on L402 operations

**Install**

One-line installer (handles uv + the vendored ldk-node wheel):
```bash
curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lqwdtech/SaturnZap/main/install.sh | sh
```

Or directly via `uv`:
```bash
uv tool install saturnzap \
  --find-links https://github.com/lqwdtech/SaturnZap/releases/expanded_assets/v1.3.1
```

(The `--find-links` flag is required because `ldk-node==0.7.0` is not yet on PyPI; the SaturnZap GitHub Release ships the vendored wheel.)

**Quick start (MCP server)**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "saturnzap": {
      "command": "sz-mcp",
      "env": {
        "SZ_PASSPHRASE": "<your-passphrase>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 📝 Additional Information

Quality checklist (from LobeHub's submit modal):

| Check | Status |
|-------|--------|
| Has README | ✅ https://github.com/lqwdtech/SaturnZap/blob/main/README.md |
| Provides ≥1 installation method | ✅ one-line installer + `uv tool install` + manual `uv sync` from clone |
| Has ≥1 Skill (Tool) | ✅ MCP tools exposed via stdio |
| Has LICENSE | ✅ MIT |
| Offers friendly installation | ✅ one-line installer documented |
| Includes Prompts | ❌ Tools-only server |
| Includes Resources | ❌ Tools-only |

Already live on:

- Official MCP Registry — https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=saturnzap
- PyPI — https://pypi.org/project/saturnzap/

Currently submitting in parallel to:
- Glama
- Smithery
- PulseMCP
- punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers (PR #6684 just opened)
- Fewsats/awesome-L402 (PR #15 open)

Logo (in repo, SVG): https://github.com/lqwdtech/SaturnZap/blob/main/logos/SaturnZap%20Main%20Logo%20Transparent%20bg.svg — happy to provide a 400×400 PNG export if needed.

Thanks!

title: [Request] Skill override Update
body:
### 🥰 Feature Description

Add skills to override uploads 

Currently, to apply an update, you must first delete the existing version and then upload the new one. However, doing so will change the ID of the skill, and any agents that use this skill will need to be reconfigured.

### 🧐 Proposed Solution

Add a confirm-before-overwrite path for ZIP skill uploads. When a user uploads a ZIP whose `SKILL.md` manifest has the same skill name as one of their own existing Agent Skills, the app should ask for confirmation before replacing that existing skill. If the user confirms, update the existing skill record instead of creating a duplicate or requiring manual uninstall/reinstall.

The overwrite should preserve the existing skill identity and ownership metadata, including the skill record id, identifier. It should replace the uploaded skill content and package-derived metadata, including manifest, description, resources, and ZIP hash.



### 📝 Additional Information

_No response_

## MCP Marketplace Submission

- **Repo URL**: https://github.com/Marsmanleo/MarsNMe
- **npm package**: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@marsnme/mcp-gateway
- **Server name**: MarsNMe
- **Publisher**: Marsmanleo
- **License**: MIT
- **Description**: Agent-agnostic AI memory backend. Turn your AI into a true companion that never forgets you across sessions. Supports dual-profile memory (semantic + episodic), session boot/close lifecycle, and works with any MCP-compatible AI client (Claude, Cursor, Perplexity, etc.).

## Why it's useful

Most AI tools lose context between sessions. MarsNMe gives AI a persistent memory layer — it recalls past decisions, preferences, and context automatically on session start, without the user repeating themselves.

## Key features

- Semantic + episodic dual-layer memory
- Session boot/close lifecycle management
- Self-hostable via `docker compose up` (one command)
- Works with Claude Desktop, Cursor, Perplexity, and any MCP client
- Free JINA API key for embeddings

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Marsmanleo/MarsNMe
cd MarsNMe
cp .env.example .env  # fill JINA_API_KEY
docker compose up
# MarsNMe gateway live at http://127.0.0.1:18790/mcp
```

Or via npm:
```bash
MCP_PROFILE=my-profile SUPABASE_BASE_URL=... npx @marsnme/mcp-gateway
```

title: Gateway Mode 下思考参数似乎未透传，导致GPT模型以不思考模式请求，Gemini返回空结果
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Web (Desktop Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📌 Version

2.2.0

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

### 问题现象

我这边在自部署环境中启用了 Gateway Mode，基础功能本身是正常的：

- 对话发出后，即使中途关闭浏览器窗口，等任务完成后重新打开页面，消息已经是完成状态
- 说明 Gateway 的“代接收 / 断开后继续收流”能力本身工作正常

但是我遇到了两个看起来相关的问题：

1. OpenAI / 推理类模型的思考强度参数，开启 Gateway Mode 后似乎失效了
2. Gemini 这类带 thinking 的模型，在 Gateway Mode 下有时会直接返回空结果

### 具体表现

#### 1. 思考强度疑似被忽略

我给了一个明显需要长时间思考的复杂问题，并把思考强度拉到最高，比如 `xhigh`。

按平时经验，这类请求一般会先思考几分钟，然后再开始输出正文。

但是只要开启 Gateway Mode，就会变成几乎立即开始输出正文，体感上像是思考参数被丢弃了，行为更接近 `none` 。

关闭 Gateway Mode 后，立刻恢复正常。

#### 2. Gemini Pro 模型在 Gateway Mode 下可能直接空结果

我测试了 Gemini 这类本身无法彻底关闭 thinking、最低也会带thinkingLevel=Low 的模型。

结果是在 Gateway Mode 下，有时最终直接返回空结果，像是“请求成功了，但正文没有被正确接收”。

同样地，关闭 Gateway Mode 后，现象会立刻消失。

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

部署`lobehub-gateway`，打开lobehub的gateway模式，使用GPT模型开启思考发送消息/Gemini Pro模型发送消息

### 🚦 What it should be?

### 期望行为

- 开启 Gateway Mode 后，当前聊天面板里设置的思考强度、thinking budget、thinking level 等参数，应该与普通聊天模式保持一致
- Gemini 等 thinking 模型在 Gateway Mode 下，不应出现“请求成功但正文为空”的情况
- Gateway Mode 的输出行为应尽量与非 Gateway Mode 保持一致，只是把接收位置从浏览器端转移到服务端 / gateway

### 📝 Additional Information

我实际使用 Codex 辅助排查了一下 `2.2.0` 源码，但自己能力有限，未必完全判断正确。

烦请开发者验证，下面这些线索也许能作为排查参考。

### Codex 辅助排查得到的线索

#### 一、Gateway Mode 和普通聊天走的不是同一条参数链路

普通聊天路径里，当前聊天面板的 `chatConfig` 会被解析成模型扩展参数，例如：

- `reasoning_effort`
- `thinkingBudget`
- `thinkingLevel`

相关位置大致在：

- `src/services/chat/index.ts`
- `src/services/chat/mecha/modelParamsResolver.ts`

也就是说，普通聊天路径是有专门的“把当前会话里的思考参数转成模型调用参数”的逻辑的。

#### 二、Gateway Mode 发起 `execAgentTask` 时，没有看到这些思考参数被带上

Gateway Mode 前端调用大致在：

- `src/store/chat/slices/aiChat/actions/gateway.ts`

这里调用 `execAgentTask(...)` 时，能看到传了：

- `agentId`
- `appContext`
- `clientRuntime`
- `fileIds`
- `parentMessageId`
- `prompt`
- `resumeApproval`
- `trigger`

但没有明显看到类似这些字段：

- `reasoningEffort`
- `thinkingBudget`
- `thinkingLevel`
- 当前 chatConfig 的临时覆盖参数

#### 三、服务端 `ExecAgentSchema` 入口也没有接这些字段

服务端入口大致在：

- `src/server/routers/lambda/aiAgent.ts`

`ExecAgentSchema` 里能看到的字段主要也是：

- `agentId`
- `appContext`
- `clientRuntime`
- `fileIds`
- `parentMessageId`
- `prompt`
- `resumeApproval`
- `trigger`

没有看到思考强度相关字段。

这让我怀疑：Gateway Mode 进入服务端执行后，当前聊天里临时调整的思考参数，根本没有透传进去。

#### 四、服务端最终创建 operation 时，似乎只保留了 `model/provider`

相关逻辑大致在：

- `src/server/services/aiAgent/index.ts`

这里创建 operation 时，看到的 `modelRuntimeConfig` 主要像是：

- `{ model, provider }`

没有看到把当前聊天里的 reasoning / thinking 扩展参数一起塞进去。

进一步看服务端执行器：

- `src/server/modules/AgentRuntime/RuntimeExecutors.ts`

这里构造给模型层的 `chatPayload` 时，主要是：

- `messages`
- `model`
- `stream`
- `tools`

也没有明显看到把 `reasoning_effort / thinkingBudget / thinkingLevel` 一起带入。

所以第一个现象我比较怀疑是：

**Gateway Mode 服务端执行链路目前只拿到了 model/provider，但没有拿到当前聊天会话里临时设置的思考参数。**

#### 五、Gemini 空结果像是第二个问题：新流格式没有被 Gateway 这条链完整消费

Google / Gemini 的流处理大致在：

- `packages/model-runtime/src/core/streams/google/index.ts`

这里对于 Gemini 新格式，能看到会产出：

- `content_part`
- `reasoning_part`

而 `model-runtime` 的协议桥接层大致在：

- `packages/model-runtime/src/core/streams/protocol.ts`

这里会：

- `text` -> `onText`
- `reasoning` -> `onThinking`
- `content_part` -> `onContentPart`
- `reasoning_part` -> `onReasoningPart`

但是 Gateway 服务端执行器这边，我看到的回调主要只接了：

- `onText`
- `onThinking`
- `onToolsCalling`

位置大致在：

- `src/server/modules/AgentRuntime/RuntimeExecutors.ts`

没有看到对：

- `onContentPart`
- `onReasoningPart`

的处理。

与此同时，普通前端聊天那条链路里是有专门处理 `content_part / reasoning_part` 的：

- `src/store/chat/agents/StreamingHandler.ts`

但 Gateway Mode 前端事件处理这边，我看到主要还是只处理：

- `text`
- `reasoning`
- `tools_calling`

位置大致在：

- `src/store/chat/slices/aiChat/actions/gatewayEventHandler.ts`

所以第二个现象我怀疑是：

**Gemini 在 Gateway Mode 下走到了 `content_part / reasoning_part` 这套新流格式，但服务端 AgentRuntime / Gateway 事件桥接这条链没有完整消费，导致最终正文可能为空。**

### 我的猜测

目前看起来，这可能不是 `lobehub-gateway` 本身的代接收能力问题，而更像是：

- LobeHub 主体在 Gateway Mode 下切换到了另一条服务端执行路径
- 这条路径对“当前聊天里的思考参数透传”支持还不完整
- 同时对 Gemini 新流格式的兼容也可能还不完整

也就是说，这两个现象可能都出在 **LobeHub 本体的 Gateway Mode 执行链**，而不是单纯出在 gateway transport 层。



### 环境说明

- 自部署
- LobeHub `2.2.0`
- 已启用 Gateway Mode
- 现象稳定可复现
- 关闭 Gateway Mode 后问题立即消失


### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?

None

title: [Bug] Server DB Mode: Critical UI/State sync bugs on Mobile Web view and the new Native App (Released around April 2026)
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Mobile App (React Native), Web (Mobile Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

Android

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📌 Version

2.2

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

Bug 1 (Mobile Web View): Custom agents created on the desktop client or desktop web interface are completely invisible when logging into the same account via a mobile browser using the default narrow-screen layout.

Bug 2 (New Native App): The messaging engine for custom agents completely freezes and stops responding after the App is resumed from the background. Tap into the newly created custom agent, type a message, and click the send button yields no response.

Bug 3 (New Native App): Modifying the metadata (e.g., name or avatar) of an agent inside the Native App yields no immediate visual feedback on the screen. The UI remains unchanged, continuously displaying the old name and avatar snapshot.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

For Bug 1:

Create a custom agent on the Desktop Web interface.

Log into the same account using a mobile browser (e.g., Chrome on Android) without enabling desktop mode. Observe that the custom agent list is empty.

Toggle the mobile browser setting to "Request Desktop Site" (Desktop View). The page re-renders, and the custom agent list instantly appears and functions normally.

For Bug 2:

Open the new Native App, create a new custom agent, select a model, and send a message. The chat functions normally, and the message histories instantly sync to the PostgreSQL backend and appear on the Desktop Web interface.

Force-close the App or send it to the background, then reopen it.

Tap into the newly created custom agent, type a message, and click the send button. The button is completely unresponsive; no network request is sent, and no records are updated in the backend database or visible on other clients. (Note: System-default agents or empty conversations are unaffected by this bug).

For Bug 3:

While the App is running, open an agent's settings and change its name or avatar, then tap save.

The UI remains unchanged, continuously displaying the old name and avatar snapshot.

Force-close the App and reopen it. The name and avatar are now successfully updated in the UI. Checking the Desktop Web or Windows client confirms the changes were successfully pushed to the PostgreSQL database during step 1.

### 🚦 What it should be?

For Bug 1: The mobile viewport layout should trigger the same initialization hooks to fetch and render the full cloud custom agent array (api/agent/list) as the desktop layout does, ensuring multi-device data parity.

For Bug 2: When the App enters the onResume or wake-up lifecycle state, it should successfully re-bind and re-activate the cloud session_id/UUID within the Chat Store runtime state so that the chat message handler can route outbound messages properly.

For Bug 3: Upon receiving a successful asynchronous response (200 OK) from the metadata mutation API (PATCH /api/agent/update), the App should instantly trigger a state invalidation or UI re-render signal to update the view on the screen.

### 📝 Additional Information

Regarding Bug 1: Since switching to "Desktop View" on the same device instantly resolves the issue, the backend database, API routing, and reverse proxy layers are verified to be fully functional. The bug is isolated to the initialization lifecycle fetching logic inside the mobile responsive view component.

Regarding Bug 2: The outbound messaging works flawlessly upon agent creation, indicating that the API credentials and network paths are intact. The failure occurs only during the session resumption state, where the front-end code silently drops the click event because it fails to establish a valid active session target for custom cloud agents.

Regarding Bug 3: This behavior confirms that the App's data-writing channel (RESTful API) works perfectly. The bug is strictly confined to the front-end UI layer of the Native App, where the view controller components fail to listen to or execute the refresh state after a successful network modification.

### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?

None

title: Incomplete file preview src URL & Knowledge base chunks disappear on refresh
body: ### 📱 Client Type Web (Desktop Browser) ### 💻 Operating System Windows ### 📦 Deployment Platform Self hosting Docker ### 📌 Version v2.2.0 ### 🌐 Browser Edge ### 🐛 What happened? I have found two consistently reproducible bugs when using the Knowledge Base / File Management features in LobeChat. These issues exist not only in my self-hosted environment but also in the official cloud deployment. Bug 1: Incomplete Preview URL (Relative Path Issue) When attempting to preview an uploaded file (e.g., .docx file), the generated preview link is incomplete: `https://view.officeapps.live.com/op/embed.aspx?src=files%2F494311%2F5d4fe402-080a-4885-bf54-eed290e1a21e.pdf` The src parameter is encoded as a relative path (decoded as files/494311/...pdf) instead of a full absolute URL containing the S3 or server public domain (e.g., https://s3.example.com/files/...). Because the domain is missing, preview plugins/services cannot fetch the actual source file, resulting in a blank screen or loading error. Bug 2: Knowledge Base Chunks State Loss After a file is uploaded and successfully vectorized, the number of chunks correctly appears next to the icon. Clicking on it successfully displays the chunk contents. However, upon refreshing the page, the chunk count badge disappears entirely, and clicking it no longer loads any chunk data. ### 📷 How to reproduce it? To reproduce Bug 1 (Incomplete src path): 1. Navigate to the Knowledge Base and upload a standard .docx file. 2. Click on the uploaded file to preview it, and observe the generated iframe address or request URL. 4. Notice that the src parameter value is only a relative path and is missing the public absolute domain. To reproduce Bug 2 (Chunks state loss): 1. Upload a document and wait for the vectorization process to complete. 2. Observe the file list and confirm that the purple chunk indicator badge (with a number inside) appears next to the file. 3. Press F5 or manually refresh the browser page. 4. After the page reloads, notice that the purple chunk indicator has disappeared, and clicking it fails to load the chunk data, just blank. ### 🚦 What it should be? 1. When generating the preview URL, the src parameter should be an accessible url. 2. After a page refresh, the frontend should successfully re-fetch and correctly display the chunk count and contents for finsihed files. ### 📝 Additional Information _No response_ ### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR? ```md
On the official LobeHub 2.2.0 Docker image, self-hosted Memory Analysis creates a `workflowRunId`, but the QStash Workflow run stops after:

```text
init STEP_SUCCESS
```

No later workflow steps are executed. `async_tasks` remains pending with `completedTopics: 0` until timeout.

The official 2.2.0 package declares:

```json
"@upstash/workflow": "^0.2.23",
"@upstash/qstash": "^2.8.4"
```

Current Upstash Workflow Cloud appears to require the 1.x-compatible protocol. A minimal REST trigger test returned:

```text
trigger rest api is only usable with sdk versions after v1.0.0 major version
```

I built a custom image based on LobeHub v2.2.0 with:

```json
"@upstash/workflow": "^1.3.0",
"@upstash/qstash": "^2.11.0"
```

and applied the minimal Workflow 1.x migration:

- removed `flowControl` from `serve(...)`
- kept flow control at trigger time
- changed `context.invoke(...)` body to `JSON.stringify(...)`
- allowed invoked workflow payloads to parse stringified JSON

With this image, Memory Analysis progressed beyond `init` into later workflow steps such as `process-topic`, and `completedTopics` started incrementing.

Expected behavior: Memory Analysis should progress beyond `init STEP_SUCCESS` and either complete or fail later with an actionable model/provider error.
