title: [Request] Bot channels forced to use server-side model providers — cannot use local/desktop providers like axonhub
body:
### 🥰 Feature Description

Bot channels should support agent execution routing through client-side/local model providers.

What's the problem?

When a WeChat (or any IM) bot is configured for an agent in LobeHub, all message processing and agent execution happens on the LobeHub server side. However, many users (especially self-hosters and power users) run local model providers on their desktop — e.g., axonhub-macos, Ollama, LM Studio, local AI gateways that aggregate multiple model providers behind a single endpoint.

Currently, if an agent uses a local/desktop-only model provider, the bot channel execution fails silently because the server cannot reach the local endpoint:

"Agent 执行失败 Operation ID: op_xxx"

This renders the bot channel feature completely unusable for anyone who:

Runs a local AI gateway/router as their primary model provider
Uses desktop-only model providers (axonhub-macos, etc.)
Has self-hosted model endpoints on their local network
Wants privacy-sensitive model calls to stay local
Expected behavior

Bot channel execution should be able to:

Route agent execution through the desktop client instead of the server when the agent uses a client-side/local model provider, OR
Allow bot platform workers to be deployed in a way that respects the client-side model provider's availability
Why this matters

LobeHub's key value proposition includes "your agents work 24/7 across IM platforms." But if the model execution is locked to server-side providers only, anyone who invested in a local infrastructure (which is common among LobeHub's tech-savvy user base) is effectively locked out of the bot channel feature.

Suggested approach

Add a mechanism for the desktop client to register itself as a capable executor for bot-triggered agent runs. When a bot message arrives:

Server checks if the target agent uses a client-only model provider
If yes, route the execution to the connected desktop client
Desktop client runs the agent with its local model provider
Desktop client sends the reply back through the server to the IM channel
Or alternatively, allow the lh bot connect CLI command to fully handle the agent execution lifecycle locally instead of proxying through the server.

Related issues

#13609 — Self-hosted bot replies silently broken by QStash signature verification
#4105 — Multiple model providers broken in client request mode on Docker

### 🧐 Proposed Solution

Core idea: Allow the desktop client (lh bot connect) to take over the full agent execution lifecycle for bot channels, instead of only acting as a message relay to the server.

Currently the architecture is:

*.txt
Plaintext
WeChat → LobeHub Server (receives message)
       → Server tries to execute agent
       → Server calls model provider
       → ❌ FAILS if provider is local/desktop-only (e.g., axonhub-macos, Ollama, LM Studio)
Proposed architecture should allow:

*.txt
Plaintext
WeChat → LobeHub Server (receives message, routes to agent)
       → Server detects agent uses client-only model provider
       → Server delegates execution to connected desktop client
       → Desktop client runs agent with local model provider
       → Desktop client sends reply → Server → WeChat
Approach A (Recommended): Add --standalone / --local-execution mode to lh bot connect
Introduce a new flag for the lh bot connect CLI command that enables the desktop client to handle the full agent execution locally:

*.bash
Shell
lh bot connect <botId> --standalone
When running in standalone mode, the desktop client:

Poll messages from the IM platform (WeChat, etc.) — already supported today
Execute the agent locally — NEW: instead of proxying to the server for execution, the client loads and runs the agent with its locally available model providers
Return the response back through the IM channel — already supported today
This approach has several advantages:

Zero additional infrastructure needed — no ngrok, no tunnels, no exposing local services to the internet
Privacy preserving — model calls stay local when the agent uses local providers
Transparent fallback — if the client is offline, the server can still execute with server-side providers
Uses existing tooling — the lh bot connect CLI already runs locally; this just extends it
Approach B (Alternative): Proxy the model provider call
Allow the desktop client to register itself as a model provider proxy to the server:

Desktop client starts a lightweight HTTP tunnel to the LobeHub server
When the bot-handled agent needs to call a model, the server routes the request through the tunnel to the client's local provider
The client forwards the response back
This is more complex to implement and has downsides (tunnel reliability, latency, security), so Approach A is preferred.

Implementation notes
The agent model provider configuration already knows whether it's a client-side or server-side provider — this information can be used to decide execution routing
Default behavior should remain unchanged (server-side execution) for backward compatibility
The --standalone flag should be opt-in, with clear documentation about the requirements
A heartbeat/health-check mechanism should be built in so the server knows when a standalone client is available

### 📝 Additional Information

_No response_

```
I tried to read https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/start, but the crawler returned an empty/too-short result, so I couldn’t extract the page content directly.

browserless returned empty or short content
```

The Browserless request itself was successful. Container logs showed:

```
Content API invoked with body: {
  gotoOptions: { waitUntil: 'load' },
  rejectRequestPattern: [
    '.*\\.(?!(html|css|js|json|xml|webmanifest|txt|md)(\\?|#|$))[\\w-]+(?:[\\?#].*)?$'
  ],
  url: 'https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/start'
}
```

Browserless returned HTTP 200 and completed the request successfully. A direct call from the LobeHub container to Browserless /content returned:
```
{
  "status": 200,
  "ok": true,
  "length": 1991516,
  "title": "Build Your Own LobeHub - Choose Your... · LobeHub",
  "hasDocs": true
}
```

  So the issue is not Docker networking, Browserless availability, DNS, token configuration, or the Browserless /content request itself.

  The actual failure happens after Browserless returns HTML, during LobeHub's markdown extraction pipeline.



### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Apply or include the Browserless timeout fix from:
https://github.com/MagicVin/lobehub/commit/72c427f2ad67509c4f35a3239c0792913873d8ae

3. Configure Browserless:
```
browserless:
  image: ghcr.io/browserless/chromium:v2.49.0
  container_name: browserless
  restart: unless-stopped
  environment:
    - 'TOKEN=${BROWSERLESS_TOKEN}'
    - 'CONCURRENT=10'
    - 'QUEUED=20'
    - 'TIMEOUT=300000'
  ports:
    - "3000:3000"
  shm_size: "2gb"
```

3. Configure LobeHub crawler:
```
BROWSERLESS_URL=http://browserless:3000
BROWSERLESS_TOKEN=***
CRAWLER_IMPLS=browserless
BROWSERLESS_WAIT_UNTIL=load
CRAWLER_TIMEOUT=60000
```

4. Ask the AI to read:
```
read https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/start
```
5. Observe that Browserless returns 200 with a large HTML payload, but the crawler may still report:
```
browserless returned empty or short content
```
6. Directly calling Browserless /content from inside the LobeHub container confirms that the returned HTML is valid, large, and contains the target docs content.

7. Optional validation:
apply the markdown extraction fix from:
https://github.com/MagicVin/lobehub/commit/d45ce7b449329696b162face4d6329def47cc072
After that patch, the same page is successfully read.


### 🚦 What it should be?

If Browserless successfully returns a valid HTML page with enough content, LobeHub should extract readable markdown content instead of reporting empty or short content.

Large modern frontend pages, such as Next.js / SPA documentation pages, should be handled reliably when Browserless is configured and returns a successful response.

### 📝 Additional Information

Root cause appears to be in the HTML-to-markdown post-processing step.

What we observed during validation:
 - Browserless request succeeds
 - Browserless logs show gotoOptions.waitUntil = 'load'
 - Browserless returns a valid large HTML payload
 - direct Browserless response contains the docs content
 - the markdown extraction layer is the failing part

The tested fix does the following:
- When trimming oversized HTML, prefer preserving <body> content instead of blindly keeping the first 1 MB of raw HTML.
- Preserve basic head metadata such as title and description for extraction.
- If Readability returns too little useful content, fall back to raw HTML-to-markdown conversion.

After applying the markdown extraction fix, the same page successfully returns:
- title
- readable content
- contentType: text
- usable markdown body


After rebuilding the Docker image with the markdown extraction fix:
```
docker build -t lobehub/lobehub:markdown-fix .
docker compose up -d --no-deps --force-recreate lobe
docker inspect lobehub --format '{{.Config.Image}}'
```
Result:
```
lobehub/lobehub:markdown-fix
```
The same page was successfully read:
```
Build Your Own LobeHub - Choose Your Deployment Platform
Explore multiple deployment platforms like Vercel, Docker, Docker Compose, and more to deploy LobeHub. Choose the platform that best suits your needs.
Number of characters 5760
Scraping mode browserless
```
Returned crawler data included:
```
{
  "crawler": "browserless",
  "originalUrl": "https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/start",
  "data": {
    "url": "https://lobehub.com/docs/self-hosting/start",
    "title": "Build Your Own LobeHub - Choose Your Deployment Platform",
    "length": 4458,
    "contentType": "text"
  }
}
```
Unit test verification:
```
cd packages/web-crawler
pnpm exec vitest run --silent='passed-only' src/utils/htmlToMarkdown.test.ts
```
Result:
```
Test Files  1 passed
Tests       6 passed
```

Yes, I am willing to submit a PR

- [x] Check that there isn't [already an issue](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues) that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate.

title: [Request] Add Xiaomi MiMo provider and configurable default model for self-hosted deployments
body:
### 🥰 Feature Description

I would like to request two related improvements for LobeHub self-hosted deployments:

1. Add **Xiaomi MiMo** as an official model provider with environment variable support.
2. Provide a clearer and more flexible way for self-hosted administrators to configure the **default model for new users**.

At the moment, Xiaomi MiMo can be used through an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint, but there does not seem to be an official MiMo provider configuration such as:

```env
MIMO_API_KEY=
MIMO_PROXY_URL=
MIMO_MODEL_LIST=
```

As a result, MiMo models have to be placed under the generic OpenAI-compatible provider. This works as a workaround, but it is not ideal for provider management, frontend display, and long-term maintenance.

In addition, self-hosted administrators often need to define which model new users should use by default. While `DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG` can currently be used, it would be helpful if this behavior were better documented and supported across officially configured providers.

## Motivation

For self-hosted LobeHub instances, administrators usually manage all API keys centrally through `.env`, so users can register and start using the service immediately without manually configuring their own provider keys.

Currently, providers like OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Qwen, and Hunyuan can be configured through environment variables. However, Xiaomi MiMo does not appear to have its own provider-specific ENV configuration.

This creates several problems:

1. MiMo models have to be mixed into `OPENAI_MODEL_LIST`.
2. The frontend cannot clearly distinguish MiMo from generic OpenAI-compatible models.
3. Self-hosted admins cannot manage MiMo API keys, proxy URLs, and model lists independently.
4. If multiple OpenAI-compatible endpoints are used at the same time, a single `OPENAI_PROXY_URL` is not enough.
5. It is harder to provide a clean default model experience for new users.
6. Admins may want the default model to be selected from MiMo, DeepSeek, Qwen, Hunyuan, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or any other configured provider.

### 🧐 Proposed Solution

### 1. Xiaomi MiMo Provider

It would be helpful if LobeHub could support Xiaomi MiMo as a first-class provider.

Example configuration:

```env
# Xiaomi MiMo Provider
MIMO_API_KEY=your-mimo-api-key
MIMO_PROXY_URL=https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1
MIMO_MODEL_LIST="-all,+mimo-v2-pro=Mimo V2 Pro,+mimo-v2.5=Mimo V2.5,+mimo-v2.5-pro=Mimo V2.5 Pro,+mimo-v2-omni=Mimo V2 Omni"
```

Expected behavior:

1. When `MIMO_API_KEY` is configured, the MiMo provider appears in LobeHub.
2. MiMo models are displayed under the MiMo provider instead of the generic OpenAI provider.
3. `MIMO_MODEL_LIST` controls which MiMo models are exposed.
4. Server-side MiMo API key configuration works for all users.
5. Users do not need to manually enter their own MiMo API key if the server has already configured one.

### 2. Configurable Default Model for New Users

It would also be helpful to provide a clear and consistent way to configure the default model used when a new user starts using LobeHub.

For example:

```env
DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG='model=mimo-v2-pro;provider=mimo'
```

or:

```env
DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG='model=deepseek-v4-pro;provider=deepseek'
```

or:

```env
DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG='model=qwen-plus;provider=qwen'
```

Expected behavior:

1. Self-hosted admins can choose the default provider and model for new users.
2. The default model should work with any officially supported provider.
3. If the configured default model or provider is unavailable, LobeHub should either fall back gracefully or show a clear warning in logs.
4. The documentation should clearly explain how to configure the default model for self-hosted deployments.

## Possible Configuration Design

A possible implementation could follow the existing provider ENV style:

```env
# Xiaomi MiMo
MIMO_API_KEY=
MIMO_PROXY_URL=https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1
MIMO_MODEL_LIST="-all,+mimo-v2-pro=Mimo V2 Pro,+mimo-v2.5=Mimo V2.5,+mimo-v2.5-pro=Mimo V2.5 Pro,+mimo-v2-omni=Mimo V2 Omni"

# Default model for new users
DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG='model=mimo-v2-pro;provider=mimo'
```

Optionally, user-side customization could also be controlled through feature flags:

```env
FEATURE_FLAGS="-mimo_api_key,-mimo_proxy_url"
```

This would be consistent with the existing approach for controlling provider-related frontend settings.

## Current Workaround

The current workaround is to route MiMo through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and add MiMo models into `OPENAI_MODEL_LIST`:

```env
OPENAI_PROXY_URL=https://custom-openai-compatible-endpoint/v1
OPENAI_MODEL_LIST="-all,+mimo-v2-pro=Mimo V2 Pro,+mimo-v2.5=Mimo V2.5,+mimo-v2.5-pro=Mimo V2.5 Pro,+mimo-v2-omni=Mimo V2 Omni"
```

However, this workaround has limitations:

1. MiMo is displayed under the OpenAI-compatible provider instead of its own provider.
2. It becomes difficult to manage multiple OpenAI-compatible providers at the same time.
3. Provider-specific model routing and frontend display are less clear.
4. The default model configuration becomes less intuitive because the provider has to be set to `openai`, even though the model is actually from Xiaomi MiMo.

Example workaround:

```env
DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG='model=mimo-v2-pro;provider=openai'
```

This works only as a compatibility workaround, but it does not provide a clean provider experience.

## Additional Context

This request is mainly for self-hosted deployments where the administrator centrally manages provider API keys through environment variables.

The goal is to make Xiaomi MiMo work like other official providers and to make the default model configuration clearer for new users.

LobeHub already has strong support for provider-specific ENV configuration. Adding Xiaomi MiMo as a first-class provider, together with clearer default model configuration support, would make the self-hosted experience more consistent and easier to maintain.

Thank you for the great work on LobeHub.


### 📝 Additional Information

_No response_

title: [Request] Allow self-hosted deployments to customize documentation and desktop app download URLs
body:
### 🥰 Feature Description

Please add support for customizing the URLs of the **"Documentation"** and **"Get Desktop App"** entries in self-hosted LobeHub deployments.

I am using LobeHub in a self-hosted environment for a small internal team. In this setup, I have configured my own API providers, model lists, default models, and deployment-specific usage rules. I also build and distribute a custom desktop application for my team members.

However, in the current web application, the links for **"Documentation"** and **"Get Desktop App"** still point to the official LobeHub website and official desktop distribution pages. This can be confusing for users in a self-hosted team environment, because the official documentation may not fully match the actual configuration, available models, provider settings, authentication method, storage setup, or desktop application build used in my deployment.

For example, my users may need to read a team-specific usage guide that explains:

1. Which models are available in this deployment.
2. Which API providers are preconfigured by the administrator.
3. How to use the custom desktop application built for this self-hosted instance.
4. Which features are enabled, disabled, or customized.
5. How to log in and use the system according to our internal workflow.

When the built-in links still point to the official LobeHub documentation or official desktop app page, users may download the wrong desktop application or follow instructions that do not apply to the self-hosted instance.

This is especially relevant because LobeHub already supports self-hosted desktop connection scenarios, and several users have discussed desktop app connection issues or custom server URLs in self-hosted deployments. For small teams, being able to guide users to the correct internal documentation and desktop app download page would make the self-hosted experience more consistent and less confusing.

### 🧐 Proposed Solution

Please provide environment variables that allow self-hosted administrators to override the default URLs for documentation and desktop app download links.

A possible configuration could be:

```env
# Custom documentation URL for self-hosted deployments
CUSTOM_DOCS_URL=https://example.com/docs/lobehub

# Custom desktop app download URL for self-hosted deployments
CUSTOM_DESKTOP_APP_URL=https://example.com/downloads/lobehub-desktop
```

Or, using a naming style aligned with existing deployment variables:

```env
LOBE_CUSTOM_DOCS_URL=https://example.com/docs/lobehub
LOBE_CUSTOM_DESKTOP_URL=https://example.com/downloads/lobehub-desktop
```

Expected behavior:

1. If `CUSTOM_DOCS_URL` is configured, all built-in documentation/help links should point to this custom URL instead of the official LobeHub documentation.
2. If `CUSTOM_DESKTOP_APP_URL` is configured, the **"Get Desktop App"** entry should point to this custom URL instead of the official desktop app page.
3. If these variables are not configured, LobeHub should keep the current default official URLs.
4. The custom URL should support both internal and public URLs.
5. These settings should work in Docker/self-hosted deployments through `.env`.
6. The feature should not require rebuilding the frontend image or modifying source code.
7. If possible, the custom links should also be reflected consistently across menus, onboarding pages, settings pages, and any other places where documentation or desktop app download links are shown.

This would allow self-hosted administrators to provide team-specific documentation and desktop app download pages while keeping the default behavior unchanged for normal users.

A more advanced but optional design could support hiding or overriding multiple official links through a structured environment variable, for example:

```env
CUSTOM_LINKS='docs=https://example.com/docs;lobe_desktop=https://example.com/downloads/desktop'
```

But the minimal solution of adding two explicit variables would already solve the main problem:

```env
CUSTOM_DOCS_URL=
CUSTOM_DESKTOP_APP_URL=
```

This would be very helpful for small teams, organizations, schools, and internal deployments where the actual usage guide and desktop app distribution are managed by the self-hosted administrator rather than the official LobeHub website.

### 📝 Additional Information

_No response_

title: Agent Group executeAgentTask isolated threads cannot access or inject saved Credentials
body:
### Summary

In Agent Group / Agent Team mode, saved credentials appear to be available in the shared group conversation path, but they are not available inside member-agent sub-tasks created via `executeAgentTask`.

A member agent invoked through `speak` can see the non-secret Credentials context (`CREDS_LIST`) and the expected credential keys. The same member agent invoked through `executeAgentTask` runs in an isolated task thread where the `lobe-creds` tool schema may be visible, but `CREDS_LIST` is empty and `injectCredsToSandbox({ keys: [...] })` fails with `unauthorized`.

This issue is not specific to any one integration or API provider. It appears to affect saved credentials in general when used from Agent Group sub-tasks / isolated threads.

No credential values, private service URLs, or secrets are included in this report.

### Expected behavior

When an Agent Group member is executed via `executeAgentTask`, the isolated task thread should preserve the authenticated user context needed by `lobe-creds` to:

1. render the same non-secret credential summary available to the shared group context;
2. expose configured credential keys in `CREDS_LIST` without revealing secret values;
3. allow `injectCredsToSandbox({ keys: [...] })` to inject authorized saved credentials into the sandbox for that task thread.

Alternatively, if isolated task threads intentionally cannot access saved Credentials, the UI and tool prompt should make that limitation explicit and prevent the model from attempting credential-dependent sandbox work inside `executeAgentTask`.

### Actual behavior

In the shared group path:

- `speak` invokes the target member agent in the group shared context.
- The Credentials rendering area is visible.
- `CREDS_LIST` is non-empty.
- Saved credential keys are visible by name only.
- `lobe-creds` is available.

In the async task path:

- `executeAgentTask` creates an isolated thread for the same member agent.
- The `lobe-creds` tool schema may still be visible.
- `CREDS_LIST` is empty.
- Saved credential keys are not visible.
- `injectCredsToSandbox({ keys: ["<credential-key>"] })` fails with `unauthorized`.

As a result, credential-dependent tasks cannot be executed reliably through `executeAgentTask`, even though the same saved credentials are available in the `speak` / shared-context path.

### Reproduction steps

1. Create or open an Agent Group.
2. Add a member agent intended to perform an API-based task that requires a saved credential.
3. Enable relevant tools / skills for the group and/or target member agent, including:
   - `lobe-creds` / Credentials
   - Cloud Sandbox
   - any skill or instruction that needs a saved credential to call an external API
4. Save a credential as a `kv-env` credential, using a placeholder key such as `test-api-credential`.
5. Ask the supervisor to invoke the target member using `speak` and inspect whether the Credentials context is visible.
   - Observed: `CREDS_LIST` is non-empty and includes the saved credential key by name only.
6. Ask the supervisor to invoke the same target member using `executeAgentTask` for the same credential-dependent task.
   - Observed: the task runs in an isolated thread; `CREDS_LIST` is empty; the saved credential key is not visible.
7. In the isolated task, attempt to call:

```ts
injectCredsToSandbox({ keys: ["test-api-credential"] })
```

8. The call fails with `unauthorized`.

### Why this appears to happen

Based on code inspection:

- The Group Supervisor uses `lobe-group-management` to orchestrate `speak`, `broadcast`, and `executeAgentTask`.
- `speak` routes to `call_agent`, which executes the selected member agent in the current group context with `subAgentId`.
- `executeAgentTask` routes through `exec_async_task`, creates a task message, calls `execSubAgentTask`, and then creates an isolated `ThreadType.Isolation` task context.
- In that isolated task context, the tool schema for `lobe-creds` can still be present, but the non-secret credentials summary rendered through `CREDS_LIST` is not preserved.
- `injectCredsToSandbox` then fails with `unauthorized`, suggesting the isolated task thread does not have the same credential authorization context as the shared group path.

Relevant code areas that may be involved:

- `packages/builtin-agents/src/agents/group-supervisor/index.ts`
- `packages/builtin-tool-group-management/src/manifest.ts`
- `packages/builtin-tool-group-management/src/executor.ts`
- `src/store/chat/agents/GroupOrchestration/createGroupOrchestrationExecutors.ts`
- `src/server/services/aiAgent/index.ts`
- `packages/builtin-tool-creds/src/manifest.ts`
- `packages/builtin-tool-creds/src/executor/index.ts`
- `src/server/modules/AgentRuntime/RuntimeExecutors.ts`

### Impact

This breaks a common Agent Group workflow:

- use a group supervisor to delegate long-running credential-dependent work to a specialist member agent;
- run that work in an isolated task thread;
- inject saved credentials into Cloud Sandbox without exposing secret values to the model.

At the moment, users may be forced to either:

- run credential-dependent API operations through `speak` in the shared group context, which is not ideal for long-running tasks; or
- bypass LobeHub Credentials by wrapping the external service as a custom MCP server that stores its own credentials.

### Suggested fix

Possible directions:

1. Ensure `executeAgentTask` / `execSubAgentTask` isolated threads inherit the same authenticated credential context needed to render `CREDS_LIST` and call `injectCredsToSandbox`.
2. Ensure `injectCredsToSandbox` works in server-side / headless / isolated task execution without relying on client-only auth state.
3. Add explicit tests comparing `speak` vs. `executeAgentTask` for `lobe-creds` visibility and injection behavior.
4. If this behavior is intentional, document that saved Credentials are unavailable in Agent Group isolated task threads and prevent models from attempting credential-dependent sandbox workflows there.

### Environment

- Deployment: self-hosted LobeHub
- Mode: Agent Group / Agent Team
- Client: web browser
- Exact version / commit: unknown

I can provide additional logs or run a specific diagnostic if needed, but I intentionally did not include any credential values or private service endpoints in this issue.

title: Add pre-execution trust verification middleware for MCP plugin calls
body:
## Problem

LobeHub supports MCP plugins, but there's no middleware layer to verify the trustworthiness of MCP servers before tool execution. When users install MCP plugins from the marketplace or configure custom servers, there's no automated way to check whether a server is safe to execute against.

This creates a gap where malicious or misconfigured MCP servers can execute arbitrary operations without any trust validation.

## Proposal

Add a configurable middleware/hook point that runs before any MCP plugin tool call:

```typescript
// Example: pluggable trust verification
interface TrustVerifier {
  verify(serverUri: string, toolName: string, params: unknown): Promise<TrustResult>;
}

// Users configure their own verification backend in settings
// or LobeHub provides a default policy engine
```

The hook should:
1. Run before any MCP tool call is dispatched
2. Receive the server URI, tool name, and parameters
3. Return allow/deny/warn with optional metadata
4. Be opt-in with zero overhead when not configured
5. Optionally surface trust info in the plugin marketplace UI

## Benefits

- **User safety:** Protects self-hosted and cloud users from untrusted MCP servers
- **Framework-agnostic:** Users choose their own verification backend
- **Opt-in:** Doesn't break existing plugin workflows
- **Marketplace enhancement:** Could show trust indicators next to plugins

## References

- [OWASP MCP Security Cheatsheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/MCP_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html)
- [OWASP MCP Top 10](https://owasp.org/www-project-mcp-top-10/) — MCP08: Unverified MCP Server Trust
- Similar proposals: Langflow (#13333), Flowise (#6433), LangChain (#37657)

title: [Bug] Chrome Browser Ctrl+V Paste of Rich Text Content to Chat Input Box Fails, Ctrl+Shift+V Works Normally
body:
### ♻ Reproduction
1. Open Chrome browser and navigate to the LobeHub chat page (e.g., https://app.lobehub.com/agent/xxx)
2. Copy some formatted text from a web page, Word, Notion, Feishu, IDE, etc.
3. Press `Ctrl + V` to paste in the chat input box

### ⏭ Expected Behavior
Content is pasted normally into the input box.

### ☹ Current Behavior
`Ctrl + V` paste has no response; content cannot be pasted into the input box.
However, using `Ctrl + Shift + V` (plain text paste) works normally.

### 💻 Additional Context
- **Browser Comparison**: The same operation works fine with `Ctrl + V` in Edge browser, but not in Chrome.
- **Permission Confirmed**: `app.lobehub.com` has been added to the "Allow to view your clipboard" list in Chrome settings, so permissions are not the issue.
- **Plain Text Works**: If the copied content is plain text (e.g., copied from Notepad), `Ctrl + V` also pastes normally. Only rich text formatted content (HTML/RTF) fails to paste.
- **Suspected Cause**: The paste event handling logic in the input box has insufficient compatibility with rich text MIME types such as `text/html` in Chrome. Edge works normally because Microsoft has added extra clipboard compatibility handling.

---
> This issue was translated by Claude.

<details>
<summary>Original Content</summary>

### ♻ Reproduction
1. 打开 Chrome 浏览器，进入 LobeHub 聊天页面（如 https://app.lobehub.com/agent/xxx）

内容正常粘贴到输入框中。

`Ctrl + V` 粘贴无反应，内容无法粘贴到输入框。
但使用 `Ctrl + Shift + V`（纯文本粘贴）可以正常粘贴。

- **推测原因**：输入框的 paste 事件处理逻辑在 Chrome 下对 `text/html` 等富文本 MIME 类型的兼容性不够，Edge 由于微软对剪贴板做了额外兼容处理所以表现正常。

Currently, the LobeHub Desktop app supports connecting to a self-hosted instance via the Wi-Fi icon, but the iOS and Android mobile apps do not have this option — they only connect to the official LobeHub cloud.

This would bring mobile experience for self-hosters on par with the desktop experience.

### 📝 Additional Information

Self-hosting setup: Docker Compose on Ubuntu 24, accessed via custom domain with SSL.
Currently using PWA on iPhone as the only mobile option.
Desktop app self-hosted connection works great — would love the same for mobile.

title: [RFC] Task Hook: pollTaskStatus API for executeAgentTask timeout recovery
body:
## 动机

`executeAgentTask` 超时后 Supervisor 无手段查询任务是否仍在运行、进度如何、能否续接结果。任务白跑。

## 核心流程

```
派发任务(初始超时 600s)
  ├─ 600s 内完成 → 正常返回结果
  └─ 超时 → 进入等待循环
       ├─ task_completed 事件到达 → 立即结束等待，返回结果
       ├─ 每 300s 轮询兜底
       │    ├─ 先查 result store → 如已完成，直接拿结果
       │    ├─ 未完成 → 返回 { status, partial_output, current_step, last_output_at, elapsed }
       │    ├─ last_output_at 距当前 > 600s → 判定 stalled → 报告用户
       │    └─ 累积等待 ≥ 60min → 报告用户（result store 额外保留 5min）
       ├─ 用户发消息 → 中断所有等待循环 → 列出各任务状态供用户决策
       └─ 进度更新为 ephemeral：不写入 messages 表，不参与上下文组装
```

## API

### `pollTaskStatus(taskId) → TaskStatus`

| 参数 | 类型 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| taskId | string | 任务 ID |

返回:
```json
{
  "status": "running | completed | failed | stalled",
  "partial_output": "最近 N 行 Agent 输出",
  "current_step": "当前子步骤描述",
  "last_output_at": "ISO8601",
  "elapsed": "已等待秒数",
  "result": "status=completed 时附带完整结果"
}
```

## Agent 侧要求

每个子步骤完成后输出进度标记: `[进度] 文件 X 已读取`
`partial_output` 截取最近 3 条进度标记。

## 策略

- 事件推送为主路径（零延迟），轮询 300s 兜底
- poll 先查 result store，消除竞态窗口
- 进度更新 ephemeral: true，不入 messages 表

## 上下文

完整规格见 LobeHub Agent Group 「AI Agent系统构建」的 `_shared/system_rules/task_hook_spec.md`

## stalled 判定

`last_output_at` 距当前 > 600s → stalled

## 硬超时

60min → result store 保留 5min

title: Web Browsing tool exposes empty parameter schema for `crawl` to Claude models, causing page fetching to fail
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Web (Desktop Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📌 Version

v2.2.1

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

When using the Claude model (claude-opus-4-6) with the Web Browsing tool, the `crawl` function's parameter schema is exposed as empty (`properties: {}, required: []`). This causes the model to be unable to properly pass the `url` parameter, resulting in empty responses when attempting to crawl web pages.

In contrast, DeepSeek models receive the correct API method `crawlSinglePage` with a properly defined parameter schema (`{"url": "..."}`), and web crawling works as expected.

Evidence:
- Claude calls: `lobe_web_browsing____crawl` with empty schema → returns empty content
- DeepSeek calls: `crawlSinglePage` with `{"url": "..."}` → returns page content successfully

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Create a conversation using a Claude model (e.g., claude-opus-4-6)
2. Enable the Web Browsing plugin
3. Ask the model to crawl any URL (e.g., "抓取 https://example.com 的内容")
4. Observe that the model calls `crawl` with an empty/malformed parameter schema
5. Response returns empty content
6. Switch to DeepSeek model in the same conversation, repeat step 3
7. DeepSeek correctly calls `crawlSinglePage` with proper `{"url": "..."}` and returns content

### 🚦 What it should be?

All models should receive the same complete tool schema for the Web Browsing plugin, including:
- The correct API method name (e.g., `crawlSinglePage`)
- Properly defined parameters with `url` as a required string field

Expected behavior: Claude models should be able to crawl web pages with the same success rate as DeepSeek models.

### 📝 Additional Information

Confirmed that switching the model provider does not resolve the issue:

- Custom provider (yunwu, New API format, same base URL) + claude-opus-4-6 → `crawl` with empty schema → empty response
- Anthropic official provider + claude-opus-4-6 → same `crawl` with empty schema → same empty response

This rules out provider compatibility issues. The root cause is on the LobeChat platform side — the tool schema injected into the prompt is determined by LobeChat's tool adapter layer, not by the upstream API provider.

Model configuration details:
- Model ID: claude-opus-4-6
- Max context: 200,000 tokens
- Extensions enabled: Context Caching (Claude), Adaptive Thinking (Opus 4.6), Thinking Effort (Opus 4.6)
- Tool use: enabled
- Vision: enabled

DeepSeek (working) receives: `crawlSinglePage` with `{"url": string}` parameter schema
Claude (broken) receives: `crawl` with `{properties: {}, required: []}` empty schema

None

title: feat: Add FunASR as self-hosted STT provider (OpenAI-compatible)
body:
## Feature Request

LobeChat currently uses `@lobehub/tts` with OpenAISTT for speech-to-text. Adding **FunASR** as a self-hosted STT option would benefit users who want fully local, privacy-first voice input.

## Why it's easy to integrate

FunASR provides an **OpenAI-compatible** `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint. If LobeChat's STT configuration allows setting a custom base URL for the OpenAI STT provider, FunASR would work immediately:

```bash
# Start FunASR server locally
pip install funasr vllm
funasr-server --device cuda
# OpenAI-compatible API at http://localhost:8000
```

## What FunASR provides

| Feature | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| Languages | 50+ (via SenseVoice, 234M params) |
| Speed | Up to 25x faster than Whisper-large (non-autoregressive) |
| Extras | Emotion detection, audio event classification |
| Privacy | Fully local, no external API calls |
| Deployment | `pip install funasr` or Docker |

## Suggested approach

In the STT settings, allow users to configure:
- Custom STT base URL (e.g., `http://localhost:8000`)
- This would make LobeChat work with any OpenAI-compatible STT server (FunASR, local Whisper servers, etc.)

**References:**
- FunASR: https://github.com/modelscope/FunASR (16K+ stars)
- SenseVoice: https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/SenseVoice (8K+ stars)

title: Langfuse ingestion fails when modelParameters contains thinking object
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Web (Desktop Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

macOS

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker / local development

### 📌 Version

`github-main` at `049c81d53b` (`@lobehub/lobehub` version `2.2.1`)

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome / Other

### 🐛 What happened?

When Langfuse tracing is enabled and a chat request includes the LobeHub `thinking` parameter, LobeHub creates the trace and generation successfully, but Langfuse rejects the ingestion payload with HTTP 207 / 400 validation errors.

As a result, the chat itself completes, but the trace does not appear in Langfuse.

Observed LobeHub server logs:

```text
[DEBUG-LANGFUSE] createTrace result { traceId: '7d276f21-e777-4965-9c94-c91c2c07fbe4' }
[DEBUG-LANGFUSE] createTraceOptions created {
  generationId: '62a399f3-6e86-4d8b-a62d-fd1a66138082',
  traceId: '7d276f21-e777-4965-9c94-c91c2c07fbe4'
}
POST /webapi/chat/newapi 200
POST http://localhost:3000/api/public/ingestion 207
```

Observed Langfuse error:

```text
Invalid request data
path: body.modelParameters.thinking
expected string, received object
expected number, received object
expected boolean, received object
expected array, received object
path: body.modelParameters.thinking.budget_tokens
expected string, received number
```

The current code in `src/server/modules/ModelRuntime/trace.ts` passes all remaining chat payload fields into `generation.modelParameters`:

```ts
const { messages, model, tools, ...parameters } = payload;

trace?.generation({
  modelParameters: parameters as any,
});
```

For requests with thinking enabled, `parameters.thinking` is an object like:

```json
{
  "type": "enabled",
  "budget_tokens": 1024
}
```

Langfuse's `modelParameters` schema does not accept object values, so the ingestion event is rejected.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Start Langfuse locally and create API keys.
2. Configure LobeHub with Langfuse enabled:

```env
ENABLE_LANGFUSE=1
LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-...
LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-...
LANGFUSE_HOST=http://localhost:3000
```

3. Make sure user telemetry is enabled.
4. Start LobeHub from `github-main`.
5. Send a chat request through a model/provider that includes LobeHub's `thinking` parameter, for example:

```json
{
  "model": "GLM-5",
  "provider": "newapi",
  "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "test" }],
  "thinking": { "type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 1024 }
}
```

6. Check LobeHub server logs and Langfuse logs.

Actual result: LobeHub sends `/api/public/ingestion`, Langfuse returns `207`, and the trace is not visible.

### 🚦 What it should be?

Langfuse traces should be ingested successfully when LobeHub chat payload contains internal structured parameters such as `thinking`.

Possible fixes:

- Exclude `thinking` from `modelParameters`, or
- Flatten/stringify structured `modelParameters` values before sending them to Langfuse, or
- Store structured values under `metadata` instead of `modelParameters`.

### 📝 Additional Information

This was reproduced on latest `github-main` commit `049c81d53b`.

A minimal SDK-only reproduction also fails with the same Langfuse validation error when `modelParameters.thinking` is an object:

```js
trace.generation({
  model: 'GLM-5',
  modelParameters: {
    stream: true,
    thinking: { type: 'enabled', budget_tokens: 1024 },
  },
});
```

Related but not identical issues found during search:

- #11967: Langfuse integration env config issue
- #6225: Langfuse trace output empty
- #6753: force-enable per-user telemetry / Langfuse

I did not find an existing issue for `modelParameters.thinking` schema rejection.

### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?

I will try to fix it

title: [Request] Add Deskbrid — Linux Desktop HAL MCP Server (9 DEs, 92 tools)
body:
## Deskbrid — Linux Desktop HAL MCP Server

**Repo:** https://github.com/coe0718/deskbrid
**License:** MIT
**Language:** Rust
**Platform:** Linux (Wayland + X11)

### What it does
Deskbrid bridges AI agents to any Linux desktop over a Unix socket and MCP protocol. 9 Wayland/X11 backends: GNOME, KDE, Hyprland, COSMIC, Sway, Niri, Wayfire, Labwc, X11.

- **92 MCP tools** across 19 categories
- Windows, keyboard/mouse input, clipboard, screenshots, OCR
- System info, battery, backlight (sysfs), CUPS printing, desktop settings (gsettings)
- Self-updating binary, web dashboard, path sandbox
- Tested on real hardware

### Why it belongs on LobeHub MCP marketplace
Unlike existing Linux desktop MCP servers (wayland-mcp — VLM-based, hyprmcp — Hyprland only), Deskbrid works across ALL major Linux desktop environments with real backend implementations.

### MCP config
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "deskbrid": {
      "command": "deskbrid",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Install: `bash <(curl -fsSL https://deskbrid.patchhive.dev/install.sh)`

title: ♻️ Replace DB-layer Drizzle type inference ($inferSelect/$inferInsert) with explicit types in @lobechat/types
body:
### Problem

Database row/insert types in `packages/database/src/schemas/*` are derived via Drizzle's `typeof table.$inferSelect` / `$inferInsert` (e.g. `RoleItem`, `ApiKeyItem`, `GenerationBatchItem`, `ChatGroupItem`, …). These inferred types are re-exported and consumed widely across models, tRPC routers, stores, and tests.

The downside surfaced in #15446: **adding a single nullable column (`workspace_id`) silently changed every affected table's inferred type**, turning `workspaceId: string | null` into a *required key*. That broke ~12 unrelated compile sites at once — model projections, store literals, and hardcoded test mocks — none of which are conceptually related to the column being added:

```
packages/database/src/models/rbac.ts(166)          — explicit .select() projection no longer matches RoleItem
src/store/session/slices/session/action.ts(256)    — hand-built ChatGroupItem literal
src/libs/trpc/lambda/context.test.ts               — apiKey mock
src/server/routers/lambda/__tests__/generationBatch.test.ts (×5)
src/server/routers/lambda/__tests__/generationTopic.test.ts (×2)
packages/database/src/models/__tests__/generation.test.ts — generation + nested asyncTask mocks
```

This is the structural issue: **inference makes the schema the single source of truth for application-facing types**, so any DDL change ripples uncontrolled into consumers and tests, and the row type can't diverge from the physical column layout (column order, nullability, projection subsets).

### Goal

Remove DB-layer type inference. Define the row/insert/domain types **explicitly in `@lobechat/types`** (`packages/types`), and have the database package import/validate against them rather than the reverse. Schema (`pgTable`) stays the runtime/migration source of truth; the *types* become hand-authored and reviewed.

### Scope

- **~157 occurrences of `$inferSelect` / `$inferInsert` across 37 schema files** in `packages/database/src/schemas/`.
- Each exported `XxxItem` / `NewXxxItem` needs a hand-written counterpart in `@lobechat/types`, then call sites migrated to the new import.
- Keep a compile-time assertion (e.g. `satisfies`/`Expect<Equal<…>>`) bridging the hand-written type to the Drizzle table during the transition so they can't silently drift.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No `$inferSelect` / `$inferInsert` re-exported as application-facing types from `packages/database`.
- [ ] Row/insert types live in `@lobechat/types` and are the imported source for models / routers / stores / tests.
- [ ] A guard test asserts each hand-written type matches its Drizzle table column set (so a future column add fails *one* explicit assertion, not N scattered consumers).
- [ ] Type-check (`tsgo --noEmit`) green.

### Notes

- Likely large; should be split per-domain (agents, sessions, messages, files, tasks, rbac, generation, …) rather than one mega-PR.
- Motivating context and the immediate (mechanical) unblock are in #15446 — that PR patches the broken sites with `workspaceId` so CI is green; this issue tracks doing it properly.

### 🐛 What happened?

When deploying LobeHub with Docker Compose, the `lobe-rustfs-init` container fails during initialization and exits with exit code 1, triggering startup errors for the entire docker-compose stack.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Start the service with `docker compose up -d` as specified in the official documentation.

_No response_

The core error logs of the `lobe-rustfs-init` container are as follows:
```text
+ mc anonymous set-json /bucket.config.json rustfs/lobe
mc: <ERROR> Unable to set-json anonymous `/bucket.config.json` for `rustfs/lobe`. parse policy failed Error("unknown field `ID`, expected one of `Id`, `Version`, `Statement`", line: 2, column: 6).
service "rustfs-init" didn't complete successfully: exit 1
```

After troubleshooting, it was found that the built-in /bucket.config.json file within the rustfs-init image has an issue with the case of JSON fields.
The file uses uppercase "ID", while the currently deployed mc client (RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z) enforces stricter validation against the AWS S3 Policy specification, which mandates the use of title-cased "Id".

title: [Bug] Infinite confirmation dialog loop — no rate limit or circuit breaker when AI triggers repeated popups
body:
### Bug Description

When the AI generates code that triggers confirmation dialogs (e.g., "Do you want to open this?", "Allow this action?", etc.), LobeHub does **not** prevent an infinite loop of popups. If the user asks the AI to write a demo program that triggers such dialogs, the popups keep appearing indefinitely, effectively locking the user out of the interface.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Open LobeHub (app.lobehub.com)
2. Ask the AI to write a demo program that triggers browser confirmation dialogs (e.g., `alert()`, `confirm()`, or file-download prompts)
3. Execute or preview the generated code
4. Observe that confirmation dialogs pop up repeatedly
5. There is no circuit breaker, rate limit, or "stop" mechanism — the popups continue until the user force-quits the browser tab

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd409dfe-240f-4682-922d-dd6b0b078a6c

### Expected Behavior

- LobeHub should detect rapid/repeated dialog triggers and **rate-limit or block** them after a threshold (e.g., 3 consecutive popups in 5 seconds).
- A **circuit breaker** should kick in: stop the execution/preview and surface a warning to the user like "This agent generated repeated confirmation dialogs and has been paused."
- The user should be able to dismiss all pending dialogs with a single action.

### Actual Behavior

- Confirmation dialogs appear in an **infinite loop** with no way to stop them from within the app.
- The user cannot interact with the underlying UI because the modal dialogs block the entire page.
- The only escape is to kill the browser tab/process.

### Environment

- **Platform:** macOS / Browser
- **App:** LobeHub Web (app.lobehub.com)
- **Theme:** Dark mode

### Suggested Fix

1. **Rate limiting:** Track dialog frequency per agent/session. If `confirm()` / `alert()` / `prompt()` are called more than *N* times within a time window, suppress subsequent calls and surface a toast/notification.
2. **Override native dialogs:** Sandbox or intercept `window.alert`, `window.confirm`, and `window.prompt` inside code preview/execution contexts so they can be throttled and non-blocking.
3. **Circuit breaker UI:** Add a "Stop agent" or "Dismiss all dialogs" button that is accessible even when modals are stacked.

### Additional Context

This is a common UX trap in any platform that lets AI generate and execute code. Without a safeguard, a single misguided prompt can render the app unusable and frustrate the user. A robust defense here would improve trust and safety significantly.

---

Thanks for the great work on LobeHub! Happy to provide more details if needed.

title: [Bug] Selecting GLM-IMAGE / CogView models in image workspace throws ZodError: prompt Required
body:
### 🐛 Bug Description

When using the `lobe-chat-database` Docker image, selecting ZhipuAI image models (GLM-IMAGE, CogView-4, CogView-3-Flash) in the image generation workspace dropdown throws a `ZodError`. Other image models (e.g., OpenAI GPT-Image) work correctly.

### 📋 Error Log

```json
{
  "name": "ZodError",
  "message": "[{\"code\":\"invalid_type\",\"expected\":\"object\",\"received\":\"undefined\",\"path\":[\"prompt\"],\"message\":\"Required\"}]"
}
```

Stack trace points to `setModelAndProviderOnSelect` → `extractDefaultValues` → `ModelParamsMetaSchema.parse()`.

### 🔍 Root Cause Analysis

The bug involves two interacting issues:

**1. Database default prevents fallback from triggering**

In `packages/database/src/schemas/aiInfra.ts`, the `parameters` column defaults to `{}`:

```typescript
parameters: jsonb('parameters').default({}),  // empty object default
```

When models are enabled via `toggleModelEnabled` / `batchToggleAiModels`, only `id`, `providerId`, `enabled`, `type`, `source` are saved — `parameters` is never populated, so it falls back to the column default `{}`.

**2. Truthy check skips fallback in `normalizeImageModel`**

In `src/store/aiInfra/slices/aiProvider/action.ts`, `normalizeImageModel` uses a truthy check:

```typescript
const fallbackParametersPromise = model.parameters
    ? Promise.resolve(model.parameters)         // {} is truthy → uses empty object!
    : getModelPropertyWithFallback(...)          // fallback never reached
```

Since `{}` is truthy in JavaScript, the fallback to `getModelPropertyWithFallback` is skipped. The empty object then fails Zod validation at `ModelParamsMetaSchema.parse({})` because `prompt` is a required field.

### 🔗 Source References

| File | Line | Issue |
|------|------|-------|
| `packages/database/src/schemas/aiInfra.ts` | `parameters` column | `default({})` causes empty objects |
| `src/store/aiInfra/slices/aiProvider/action.ts` | `normalizeImageModel` | Truthy check skips fallback for `{}` |
| `packages/model-bank/src/standard-parameters/index.ts` | `ModelParamsMetaSchema` | `prompt` is required (not optional) |

### 🛠 Suggested Fix

**Option A** (recommended): Change `normalizeImageModel` to validate parameters before using them:

```typescript
// Check if parameters has the required 'prompt' field
const hasValidParameters = model.parameters && 'prompt' in model.parameters;

const fallbackParametersPromise = hasValidParameters
    ? Promise.resolve<ModelParamsSchema | undefined>(model.parameters)
    : getModelPropertyWithFallback<ModelParamsSchema | undefined>(
        model.id,
        'parameters',
        model.providerId,
      );
```

**Option B**: Change the database default from `{}` to `NULL`:

```typescript
parameters: jsonb('parameters').default(null),  // allows fallback to work
```

### 📝 Workaround

Directly set correct parameters in the database:

```sql
UPDATE ai_models 
SET parameters = '{"prompt":{"default":""},"resolution":{"default":"hd","enum":["hd"]},"size":{"default":"1280x1280","enum":["1280x1280","1568x1056","1056x1568","1472x1088","1088x1472","1728x960","960x1728"]},"watermark":{"default":false}}'::jsonb 
WHERE id = 'glm-image';

UPDATE ai_models 
SET parameters = '{"prompt":{"default":""},"resolution":{"default":"standard","enum":["hd","standard"]},"size":{"default":"1024x1024","enum":["1024x1024","768x1344","864x1152","1344x768","1152x864","1440x720","720x1440"]},"watermark":{"default":false}}'::jsonb 
WHERE id IN ('cogview-4', 'cogview-3-flash');
```

### 🌍 Environment

- **Image**: `lobehub/lobe-chat-database:latest` (digest: `sha256:20136c08da376da970ad659d58c553effa739cb7cde8b936eb1d30716649b893`)
- **Database**: PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector
- **Affected Models**: `glm-image`, `cogview-4`, `cogview-3-flash`
- **Mode**: Logged-in (database-stored models)]

title: [Bug] Self-hosted memory extraction times out with completedTopics=0 while QStash workflowRunId is created
body:
### Bug Description

In a self-hosted LobeHub/LobeChat Docker deployment, user memory extraction consistently times out.

The task creates an Upstash QStash workflow run ID, but no topics are processed. The database shows `completedTopics: 0` until the task eventually fails with `TaskTimeout`.

This looks similar to previous reports such as #11900, #13099, and #14421, but I can still reproduce it on version 2.2.2.

### Version

LobeHub/LobeChat version: `2.2.2`

Docker image:

```text
lobehub/lobehub
```

### Deployment

Self-hosted with Docker Compose.

Services are healthy:

```text
postgresql: healthy
redis: healthy
rustfs: healthy
lobe: running
```

Relevant environment variables are configured:

```env
APP_URL=https://<redacted>.sslip.io
INTERNAL_APP_URL=http://localhost:3210
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://...
REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
REDIS_PREFIX=lobechat
QSTASH_URL=https://qstash-us-east-1.upstash.io
QSTASH_TOKEN=<redacted>
QSTASH_CURRENT_SIGNING_KEY=<redacted>
QSTASH_NEXT_SIGNING_KEY=<redacted>
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy LobeHub/LobeChat 2.2.2 with Docker Compose.
2. Configure Postgres, Redis, RustFS, and Upstash QStash.
3. Open the Memory page.
4. Click "Request memory analysis".
5. Wait for the task to run.

### Expected Behavior

Memory extraction should process chat topics and update progress, for example:

```json
{
  "progress": {
    "totalTopics": 37,
    "completedTopics": 1
  }
}
```

Eventually memories should be extracted.

### Actual Behavior

The task creates a QStash workflow run, but no topic is processed.

Database evidence from `async_tasks`:

```text
type       | user_memory_extraction:chat_topic
status     | error
error      | {"body": {"detail": "User memory extraction timed out after 185 minutes for 37 topics (estimated at 5 minutes per topic). Please retry."}, "name": "TaskTimeout"}
metadata   | {"range": {}, "source": "chat_topic", "control": {"upstash": {"workflowRunIds": ["wfr_KPgvkzjMzsPlA3YuyXevS"]}}, "progress": {"totalTopics": 37, "completedTopics": 0}}
```

Another run was manually stopped because the workflow appeared stuck:

```text
status     | error
error      | {"body": {"detail": "Force stopped stuck QStash workflow"}, "name": "ManualStop"}
metadata   | {"range": {}, "source": "chat_topic", "control": {"upstash": {"workflowRunIds": ["wfr_8nuEUnoMDIe6A3-oEv7OT"]}}, "progress": {"totalTopics": 37, "completedTopics": 0}}
```

### Additional Notes

The important part is that `workflowRunIds` are created, but `completedTopics` remains `0`.

This suggests that the QStash workflow is triggered or registered, but the actual workflow steps are not executed or callbacks are not being handled correctly.

title: [Bug] Client-side requests fail for S3/R2 images after /f redirects bypass S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN
body: ### 📱 Client Type Web (Desktop Browser) ### 💻 Operating System Windows ### 📦 Deployment Platform Self hosting Docker / Self-hosted deployment with S3-compatible storage (Cloudflare R2 observed) ### 📌 Version v2.2.2 ### 🌐 Browser Chrome ### 🐛 What happened? After upgrading to the current version, image attachments stored in S3/R2 no longer use the configured public domain in some chat flows. This is a regression from the previous version. Previously, the issue described in this discussion could be fixed by configuring: - `S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` - `S3_SET_ACL="1"` Related discussion: https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/discussions/12147 Before the upgrade, files could be accessed directly through the configured public domain, for example: ```text https://s3.example.com/files//.png ``` After the upgrade, the chat image and the Resource/file list both use a Lobe file proxy URL first: ```text https:///f/ ``` That `/f/` route then redirects to a presigned `S3_ENDPOINT` URL, for example an R2 endpoint: ```text https://..r2.cloudflarestorage.com/files//.png?X-Amz-... ``` This breaks browser/client-side model requests. The image can still be displayed from the Resource/file list via ``, but client-side `fetch()` / blob / base64 conversion fails because the redirect target is cross-origin and does not pass the same CORS/proxy rules as `S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN`. The error shown in chat is: ```json { "error": { "message": "Failed to fetch" }, "provider": "xxx" } ``` ### 📷 How to reproduce it? 1. Configure S3/R2 storage with: ```env S3_ENDPOINT= S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN= S3_SET_ACL="1" ``` 2. Enable browser/client-side requests for a provider. 3. Send a message with an image attachment. 4. Send a follow-up message that requires the model to read the previous image. 5. The request fails with `Failed to fetch`. Observed network flow: ```text GET https:///f/ 302 Location: https://..r2.cloudflarestorage.com/files/...png?X-Amz-... ``` The same file opened from the Resource/file list also uses `/f/` and redirects to the R2/S3 endpoint. The Resource/file list can display the image, because an `` tag can render a cross-origin image after following the redirect. However, client-side request mode needs the browser to read the image body and convert it to base64 before sending it to Gemini/Google, so browser CORS rules apply. ### 🚦 What it should be? When `S3_SET_ACL="1"` and `S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` are configured, file access URLs used by chat/image flows should continue to resolve through `S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN`, or `/f/` should not redirect to `S3_ENDPOINT` in a way that bypasses the configured public domain. This is especially important for browser/client-side request mode, where the model runtime may need to `fetch()` image URLs and convert them to base64. Expected behavior should match the previous version: the configured public domain should keep working for image access, avoiding direct browser access to the raw `S3_ENDPOINT` presigned URL. ### 📝 Additional Information From code inspection, current `/f/[id]` appears to call `createCachedPreSignedUrlForPreview(file.url)`, which produces a presigned URL based on `S3_ENDPOINT`. Meanwhile, `getFullFileUrl()` still respects `S3_SET_ACL` + `S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN`, but it is not used by the `/f` redirect path. The failure only appears when browser/client-side request mode is enabled. Server-side requests may not hit browser CORS restrictions. The practical difference is: ```text Resource/file list image display: follows 302 and renders the image. Client-side request mode: fetch('/f/') follows 302, then tries to read the R2/S3 response body. This requires CORS on the final redirected URL, so it fails when the configured S3_PUBLIC_DOMAIN proxy is bypassed. ``` This looks like a regression of the workaround documented in https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/discussions/12147. ### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR? No, but I am happy to help test the fix ### ✅ Validations - [x] Read the [docs](https://lobehub.com/zh/docs). - [x] Check that there isn't [already an issue](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues) that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate. - [x] Make sure this is a LobeChat issue and not a third-party library or provider issue. - [x] Check that this is a concrete bug. For Q&A, please use [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/discussions) or join our [Discord Server](https://discord.gg/rGHwKq4R).

title: [Bug] Self-hosted CAO daily scheduled tasks are not dispatched while heartbeat_interval tasks keep running
body:
### Bug Description

In a self-hosted LobeHub/LobeChat Docker deployment, CAO task scheduling behaves inconsistently:

- A daily scheduled task with `schedule_pattern = 30 18 * * *` and `schedule_timezone = Australia/Sydney` was created before the scheduled time, but it was never started.
- A task that appears in the UI as "every 10 minutes" continues to run, but the database shows this is driven by `heartbeat_interval = 600`, not by the cron `schedule_pattern`.

This suggests that `schedule_pattern` for daily cron schedules is saved correctly but is not reliably consumed by the scheduler/dispatcher in self-hosted deployments.

### Version

LobeHub/LobeChat version: `2.2.2`

Docker image:

```text
lobehub/lobehub
```

### Deployment

Self-hosted with Docker Compose.

Services are healthy:

```text
postgresql: healthy
redis: healthy
rustfs: healthy
lobe: running
```

Relevant runtime environment:

```env
APP_URL=https://<redacted>.sslip.io
INTERNAL_APP_URL=http://localhost:3210
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://...
REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
REDIS_PREFIX=lobechat
QSTASH_URL=https://qstash-us-east-1.upstash.io
QSTASH_TOKEN=<redacted>
QSTASH_CURRENT_SIGNING_KEY=<redacted>
QSTASH_NEXT_SIGNING_KEY=<redacted>
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy LobeHub/LobeChat 2.2.2 with Docker Compose.
2. Create a CAO task before the scheduled time.
3. Set it to run daily at a fixed time, for example 18:30 in `Australia/Sydney`.
4. Wait until the scheduled time passes.
5. Check the task in the UI and in the database.

### Expected Behavior

The task should be started at the configured cron time:

```text
schedule_pattern  = 30 18 * * *
schedule_timezone = Australia/Sydney
```

The database should show `started_at` and `last_heartbeat_at` updated around the scheduled time.

### Actual Behavior

The daily task is saved as `scheduled`, but it is never started.

Database evidence:

```text
id                 | task_wcPtD9GxqrnG
identifier         | T-9
schedule_pattern   | 30 18 * * *
schedule_timezone  | Australia/Sydney
heartbeat_interval |
created_at         | 2026-06-05 08:09:07.369734+00
accessed_at        | 2026-06-05 08:09:23.003+00
started_at         |
last_heartbeat_at  |
```

This task was created at `2026-06-05 08:09 UTC`, which is `2026-06-05 18:09 Australia/Sydney`, before the scheduled time `18:30 Australia/Sydney`. It should have run at `18:30`, but `started_at` and `last_heartbeat_at` remained empty.

### Comparison With A Working 10-Minute Task

Another task appears to run every 10 minutes, but its cron pattern does not explain its actual execution time:

```text
id                 | task_3dd0byRRUYfU
identifier         | T-8
schedule_pattern   | 0 9 * * *
schedule_timezone  | Australia/Sydney
heartbeat_interval | 600
created_at         | 2026-06-05 08:00:57.636174+00
accessed_at        | 2026-06-05 11:54:54.261+00
started_at         | 2026-06-05 11:54:08.126+00
last_heartbeat_at  | 2026-06-05 11:54:54.241+00
```

`schedule_pattern = 0 9 * * *` means daily at 09:00 Australia/Sydney, but this task was still being started/updated around `21:54 Australia/Sydney`. The only obvious recurring interval is:

```text
heartbeat_interval = 600
```

So the "every 10 minutes" behavior seems to be driven by heartbeat/resume logic, while daily cron schedules without `heartbeat_interval` are not dispatched.

### Additional Observation

Another scheduled task also started before its cron time:

```text
identifier         | T-5
schedule_pattern   | 0 21 * * *
schedule_timezone  | Australia/Sydney
started_at         | 2026-06-05 08:23:35.01+00
```

`0 21 * * *` should run at 21:00 Australia/Sydney, but `started_at` corresponds to around 18:23 Australia/Sydney. This suggests `started_at` may be caused by a lifecycle/heartbeat/manual path rather than the configured cron schedule.

### Hypothesis

The self-hosted CAO task runner appears to persist `schedule_pattern`, but daily cron schedules are not reliably registered or consumed by the background scheduler. Tasks with `heartbeat_interval = 600` continue to progress through a different mechanism.

title: [Bug] Memory Analysis reprocesses previously analyzed chat topics and creates duplicate memories with same sourceId/title
body:
### Bug Description

In a self-hosted LobeHub/LobeChat Docker deployment, running Memory Analysis multiple times can reprocess previously analyzed chat topics and create duplicate memories.

The duplicated memories preserve the same source topic in `user_memories.metadata.sourceId`, and in some cases the same `sourceId + title` appears more than once.

This suggests that Memory Analysis is not idempotent for already-analyzed chat topics, or that the workflow does not reliably skip/update existing memories for the same source topic/message set.

### Version

LobeHub/LobeChat version: `2.2.2`

Docker image:

```text
lobehub/lobehub
```

### Deployment

Self-hosted with Docker Compose.

Relevant services:

```text
postgresql
redis
rustfs
lobe
Upstash QStash Workflow
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy LobeHub/LobeChat 2.2.2 with Docker Compose.
2. Configure Memory Analysis and QStash Workflow.
3. Run Memory Analysis from the Memory page.
4. Wait until some memories are written to `user_memories`.
5. Run Memory Analysis again over the same chat history/topics.
6. Query `user_memories` by `metadata.sourceId`.

### Expected Behavior

If a chat topic or the same source messages were already analyzed, Memory Analysis should either:

- skip the already processed topic/message set, or
- update/merge the existing memory record,

rather than creating duplicate memories for the same source topic and same title.

### Actual Behavior

The same source topic can be analyzed again and new memories are inserted.

Example query:

```sql
select
  metadata->>'sourceId' as topic_id,
  count(*) as memory_count,
  min(created_at) as first_memory_at,
  max(created_at) as last_memory_at
from user_memories
where metadata->>'source' = 'chat_topic'
group by metadata->>'sourceId'
order by last_memory_at desc
limit 50;
```

Sample output:

```text
topic_id         | memory_count | first_memory_at              | last_memory_at
-----------------+--------------+------------------------------+------------------------------
tpc_8qaKlQcnG2Hj | 3            | 2026-06-06 14:05:14.234957+00 | 2026-06-07 01:02:07.952075+00
tpc_ikWJC1rNdryk | 11           | 2026-06-06 14:04:13.012947+00 | 2026-06-07 01:02:05.648011+00
tpc_oq54xg3HN7yK | 8            | 2026-06-06 14:03:59.730797+00 | 2026-06-07 01:02:04.539886+00
tpc_ctoM66lD0jot | 10           | 2026-06-06 14:02:56.183069+00 | 2026-06-07 01:02:03.876481+00
```

The same topic IDs have memories created in two different Memory Analysis runs.

There are also duplicate `sourceId + title` combinations:

```sql
select
  metadata->>'sourceId' as topic_id,
  title,
  count(*) as dup_count
from user_memories
where metadata->>'source' = 'chat_topic'
group by metadata->>'sourceId', title
having count(*) > 1
order by dup_count desc;
```

Sample output:

```text
topic_id         | title                                      | dup_count
-----------------+--------------------------------------------+----------
tpc_KPl57xoDYinf | 修正英语学习 Telegram 提醒任务             | 2
tpc_mVguq2WnYJqp | Telegram 英语学习进度检查提醒              | 2
tpc_MZJJ4LqAs52j | Telegram 学习提醒消息未送达问题            | 2
tpc_QCf8HFwXLExc | Telegram 英语学习进度检查提醒              | 2
tpc_RBxyTitpIhbQ | 英语学习间隔提醒任务                       | 2
tpc_3u1MBfG4bFNR | 通过 Telegram 发送英语学习进度检查提醒     | 2
```

Example `metadata` from one memory record:

```json
{
  "layer": "context",
  "labels": ["体脂率管理", "健身周期计划", "训练频率", "营养管理", "数据隐私"],
  "source": "chat_topic",
  "sourceId": "tpc_7w89bcyEQuyf",
  "messageIds": [
    "msg_fgYNwo2fykxxEW",
    "msg_uRIeiviQUNSInn"
  ]
}
```

### Impact

This can cause:

- duplicate or near-duplicate memories,
- unnecessary QStash Workflow/message consumption,
- repeated model and embedding costs,
- noisy or inconsistent memory retrieval results.

### Additional Context

The behavior was observed after multiple Memory Analysis runs. Some runs ended with errors such as embedding provider `429` or `retrieval errors`, but many memories were still inserted. Retrying Memory Analysis over the same history appears to reprocess previously analyzed topics and insert additional memories instead of reliably skipping/updating existing ones.

title: 🐛 Bug: Agent Council (Group Mode) parent_id Incorrect Concatenation Causes Foreign Key Constraint Failure
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Web (Desktop Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📌 Version

2.2

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

Bug: Agent Council group mode parent_id concatenation error causes foreign key constraint failure

**Description**

In LobeHub v2.2.2's Agent Council (group/committee mode), when multiple Agents complete a round of discussion, the system creates the next round's moderator message with the `parent_id` incorrectly concatenated as `agentCouncil-msg_X-msg_Y-msg_Z` format, causing PostgreSQL foreign key constraint validation to fail, and the message cannot be written.

**Reproduction Steps**

1. Create an Agent Council group, configure >= 3 Agents (1 supervisor + at least 2 members)
2. Send a message in the group topic to trigger multiple Agent replies
3. Wait for the first round of discussion to complete (all Agents have successfully replied)
4. The supervisor automatically initiates a new round of "moderator speech" -> triggers the error

**Expected Behavior**

`parent_id` points to a valid and unique `messages.id`, formatted as `msg_xxxxxxxxxxxxxx`.

**Actual Behavior**

`parent_id` is set to `agentCouncil-msg_AAA-msg_BBB-msg_CCC` (three message IDs concatenated with hyphens + `agentCouncil-` prefix), with no corresponding record in the `messages.id` table.

**Error Logs**

PostgreSQL:

```
ERROR:  insert or update on table "messages" violates foreign key constraint "messages_parent_id_messages_id_fk"
DETAIL:  Key (parent_id)=(agentCouncil-msg_o10lApdph0cP2y-msg_vV2kL51PJiZlcu-msg_SeYL3U7MJn4kcf) is not present in table "messages".
```

LobeHub Server (tRPC handler):

```
Error in tRPC handler (lambda) on path: aiChat.sendMessageInServer, type: mutation
Error [TRPCError]: Failed query: insert into "messages" ...
  code: 'INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR',
```

**Environment Information**

- LobeHub version: v2.2.2 (released 2026-06-04, latest version)
- Database: PostgreSQL (lobe-postgres)
- Group Agent count: 3 (1 supervisor + 2 members)
- Error code: PostgreSQL 23503 (foreign_key_violation)
- Foreign key constraint: `messages_parent_id_messages_id_fk` -> `FOREIGN KEY (parent_id) REFERENCES messages(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`

**Database Details**

The `parent_id` field is defined as `text` type (no length limit), ruling out field truncation. There are no message records in the database starting with `agentCouncil-%`, indicating the foreign key constraint successfully prevented dirty data from being written.

**Root Cause Analysis**

In the Agent Council's `aiChat.sendMessageInServer` process, when constructing the supervisor's "moderator speech" message, the code concatenates all Agent `message.id`s from the previous round (format: `agentCouncil-{id1}-{id2}-{id3}`) instead of selecting a valid `parent_id`. This appears to be a design flaw in the group message threading implementation.

**Related Context**

- The successfully completed previous round messages (15:58:14 UTC) contain three records: 1 tool message + 2 assistant messages, from the three Agents in the group
- The next round's "moderator speech" `parent_id` concatenates exactly those 3 `msg_xxx` values
- PR #15408 has classified this type of foreign key violation as `ConversationParentMissing` for error recovery, but has not fixed the root cause of `parent_id` concatenation

**Temporary Workaround**

- Avoid using multiple Agents simultaneously in a group
- Or manually @ each Agent in a regular (non-group) topic

title: [Feature Request] Diff-based agent template updates — merge upstream changes with local customizations
body:
### 🥰 Feature Description

When a user installs an agent from the LobeHub marketplace (or uses a built-in template) and then customizes its system prompt via the Agent Builder (e.g., changing the default language, adding custom instructions, or modifying the agent's persona), the agent becomes a fully independent local copy. Any subsequent updates to the original marketplace template are **completely lost** — there is no way to receive upstream improvements without manually re-applying customizations.

I'd like a mechanism that tracks which parts of an agent's system prompt were customized by the user, so that when the upstream template is updated, non-conflicting changes are **automatically merged** — similar to how Git handles branching and merging.

### 💡 Suggested Solution

**Approach: Three-way merge for agent templates**

1. **Store a base template reference** — When an agent is forked from the marketplace, store the original template identifier + version hash alongside the user's customized version.
2. **On template update detection** — When the marketplace agent's definition changes (new version published), surface an "Update Available" badge on the forked agent.
3. **Three-way merge** — Apply a merge algorithm:
   - **Base**: Original template content at fork time
   - **Theirs**: New template content from marketplace
   - **Ours**: User's customized content
4. **Auto-merge non-conflicting changes** — Sections the user didn't touch auto-update.
5. **Surface conflicts** — Sections where both sides changed are flagged in the UI for manual resolution (with a simple side-by-side diff editor).

This could start with the **system prompt only**, and expand later to cover settings, tools/plugins, model config, and other agent fields.

### 🔀 Alternatives Considered

1. **Always overwrite on template update** — Too destructive; kills all user customizations.
2. **Manual diff tool** — Users manually compare locally saved versions against updates. Better than nothing but poor UX.
3. **No sync at all (current behavior)** — Forces users to either never customize marketplace agents or accept being stuck on an old version.

### 📦 Additional Context

This is especially relevant for:

- **Customizing language preferences** — A marketplace agent in Chinese can be forked to default to English, but the user still wants SEO/content updates from the original author.
- **Adding company-specific instructions** — Forking a generic agent and adding internal compliance rules without losing the original's domain expertise.
- **Template authors who iterate** — If the original author improves the agent's capabilities over time, forked copies should be able to receive those improvements.

**LobeHub already tracks `forkedFromIdentifier`** on forked agents (visible in `packages/types/src/discover/fork.ts`), so the foundation for tracking origin is partially in place.

title: [Feature Request] MCP catalog browser inside LobeChat (via Unyly API)
body:
## Feature Request

LobeChat supports MCP servers. Today users have to find MCPs themselves (npm search, GitHub trending, etc) and manually configure JSON.

Could LobeChat integrate with **Unyly** (https://unyly.org) as an embedded MCP catalog browser?

## What Unyly provides

- **15,000+ MCP servers** indexed across all major sources (Smithery, PulseMCP, Glama, npm, Official Registry)
- **Stable REST API**:
  - `GET https://unyly.org/api/v2/mcps?search=&category=&pricing=&limit=&offset=`
  - `GET https://unyly.org/api/v2/mcps/{slug}` — per-MCP detail
  - `GET https://unyly.org/api/v2/mcps/featured?limit=8` — curated picks
  - `GET https://unyly.org/api/v2/mcps/trending?days=30&limit=20` — by install velocity
  - `GET https://unyly.org/api/v2/categories` — taxonomy
- **OpenAPI spec**: `https://unyly.org/api/openapi.json`
- **Per-MCP install command** + env var schema (so LobeChat can render the config form)
- **Security badge data** — env vars, permissions scope, repo health

## What integration would unlock for LobeChat users

- Discover MCPs from inside the client without opening browser
- One-click install (LobeChat injects the config from Unyly's response)
- Show "trending" / "featured" MCPs in onboarding
- Security audit display before user installs

## Asks

1. Would the LobeChat team consider building this integration? Happy to write the PR myself if you're open to it (~200 LOC React component pulling from `/api/v2/mcps`).
2. If the team prefers to build internally — happy to provide API access guarantees + integration support.
3. No paywall on catalog data for this use case. Free forever for client integrations like LobeChat.

## Mockup (rough)

```
┌─ MCP Library [⌘+K] ─────────────────┐
│ 🔍 Search "notion"                  │
│                                      │
│  Notion MCP        ⭐ 4.8  ⬇ 1.2k   │
│  Read & write Notion pages          │

│  ─────────────────                  │
│  Notion AI Agent   ⭐ 4.6  ⬇ 850    │
│  ...                                 │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Tech notes

- Unyly catalog is ingested daily, so listings stay fresh
- API supports CORS + has no rate limits for read endpoints
- Stable since launch — we've maintained backwards-compat on `/api/v2/*` endpoints

Looking forward to feedback!

title: [Request] Make documents prompt injection preserve context cache
body:
### 🥰 Feature Description

Currently, injecting documents list into prompt cache is like this
```
<agent_documents_index>
1 user-created docs. Use readDocument(id) for full content.
233 web-crawled docs hidden — call listDocuments(sourceType='web') to see them.

TITLE                                 ID                                    SIZE   UPDATED

</agent_documents_index>
```


This changes the context at the beginning every time:
1. a user document is created or renamed or deleted
2. every time a web crawl is started
3. a minute passes for recent documents

This massively reduces context caching across multiple tool calls and subsequent user prompts

1. make user documents behave like web documents to hide list
```
<agent_documents_index>
1 user-created docs hidden — call listDocuments(sourceType='user-created') to see them.
233 web-crawled docs hidden — call listDocuments(sourceType='web') to see them.
</agent_documents_index>

```

```
user-created docs hidden — call listDocuments(sourceType='user-created') to see them.
web-crawled docs hidden — call listDocuments(sourceType='web') to see them.
```

title: [BUG] Plugin manifest cache not invalidated on update — stale plugin versions shown
body:
## Location
`nettacker/core/fuzzer.py` — `read_from_file()` function

## Issue
The fuzzer's file reader has three problems:
1. File opened without context manager — handle never explicitly closed
2. No error handling for missing/corrupt payload files — crashes with unhandled FileNotFoundError
3. Empty lines from split() included in payload list — sends blank payloads

```python
def read_from_file(file_path):
    return open(Config.path.payloads_dir / file_path).read().split("\n")
```

## Steps
1. Configure a fuzzing module with a non-existent payload file
2. Scanner crashes at runtime with no user-friendly error

## Fix
```python
def read_from_file(file_path):
    path = Config.path.payloads_dir / file_path
    if not path.exists():
        log.warning(f"Payload file not found: {path}")
        return []
    with open(path) as f:
        return [line.strip() for line in f if line.strip()]
```
