title: Custom MCP connectors (Streamable HTTP) not injected into agent tools after upgrade to 2.2.3
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Web (Desktop Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Zeabur

### 📌 Version

2.2.3

### 🌐 Browser

Firefox

### 🐛 What happened?

After upgrading LobeHub from 2.2.2 → 2.2.3 (not a fresh install), custom MCP connectors using Streamable HTTP transport stop being injected into agent conversations:

1. Custom MCP connectors (e.g., http://10.9.16.224:9100/mcp) appeared correctly in the dashboard and in the agent's connector toggle list, but their tools only showed up in the toggle list after a ~5 minute delay.
2. Agents never received the tools — only built-in lobe-* tools appeared in conversations, even with the connector toggle enabled.
3. Clicking an existing connector showed: "This skill does not expose configurable tool permissions" — no edit button, no delete button either.
4. Deleting and re-adding the same connectors: a delete button briefly appeared but clicking it did nothing.
5. The connector was shown as installed and connected (green), but completely non-functional.

Downgrading back to 2.2.2 immediately restored all functionality — same connectors, same config, tools appear and work in agent conversations without any changes.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Start on LobeHub 2.2.2 with a working custom MCP connector (Streamable HTTP transport, e.g., http://10.9.16.224:9100/mcp) and SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IP_ADDRESS=1
2. Upgrade to 2.2.3 via Docker image tag change (Zeabur redeploy)
3. Open any agent that has the connector toggled on
4. Start a conversation — observe only lobe-* built-in tools, no custom tools
5. Go to Settings → Discover → click the custom connector → see "This skill does not expose configurable tool permissions" with no edit or delete buttons
6. Downgrade back to 2.2.2 — tools reappear immediately

### 🚦 What it should be?

Custom MCP connectors (Streamable HTTP) installed in 2.2.2 should survive the upgrade and continue injecting tools into agent conversations in 2.2.3 — same as built-in connectors (Task, Message, Documents).

### 📝 Additional Information

- Using lobehub/lobehub Docker image (not lobe-chat), self-hosted on Zeabur (K3s), Ubuntu server, internal Docker bridge network
- MCP server uses Streamable HTTP transport (Python/uv, mcp library StreamableHTTPServerTransport with stateless=True)
- SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IP_ADDRESS=1 is set
- Connector URL format: http://10.9.16.224:9100/mcp (internal IP)
- Two separate MCP connectors affected (dockpit + replicate-mcp-bridge), both Streamable HTTP
- Database is PostgreSQL (ParadeDB pg16)
- No migration errors or visible console errors
- Issue is a regression from 2.2.2, not present in a fresh 2.2.2 install

### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?

No, but I am happy to help test the fix

### 🥰 Feature Description

Please list **jobd** on the LobeHub MCP marketplace. (Filing as an issue per the guidance for marketplace addition requests.)

### 🧐 Proposed Solution

- **Repository:** https://github.com/musharna/jobd
- **Official MCP Registry entry:** `io.github.musharna/jobd` (v0.5.4, PyPI package `jobd`)
- **Publisher:** musharna (Jaret Arnold)
- **License:** MIT
- **Also listed on:** Glama (Quality A), PulseMCP, official MCP registry

**What it does:** jobd is a self-hostable, GPU-aware job broker that turns a handful of personal machines (homelab / tailnet) into a single job queue. The MCP server exposes 9 tools — `jobd_submit`, `jobd_status`, `jobd_logs`, `jobd_list`, `jobd_cancel`, `jobd_preempt`, `jobd_workers`, `jobd_job_get`, `jobd_worker_delete` — so an LLM agent can submit long-running/GPU jobs, route them by live free VRAM, babysit them across sessions, and preempt/checkpoint cleanly.

**Transport & Auth:** stdio; bearer token via env (`JOBD_URL`, `JOBD_API_TOKEN`).

**Quick start:**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "jobd": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--from", "jobd[mcp]", "jobd-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "JOBD_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:8765",
        "JOBD_API_TOKEN": "<your-token>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 📝 Additional Information

- [x] README with install + MCP config docs
- [x] Installable from PyPI (`pip install "jobd[mcp]"` / `uvx`)
- [x] 9 tools with parameter-documented JSON schemas
- [x] MIT license, SECURITY.md, CI (lint + types + tests, 3.11–3.13), CodeQL

title: Bug: Hermes Platform Agent remote runs fail with spawn hermes ENOENT
body:
# Bug: Hermes Platform Agent fails from remote LobeHub with `spawn hermes ENOENT`, and device picker filters out available devices

## Summary

I am testing the beta **Platform agents, local or remote** workflow with Hermes Agent on LobeHub Desktop. I hit two related issues:

1. The **Create Platform Agent / 接入助理** wizard sometimes shows no device in step 2 even though `lh device list` and `Settings → Devices` both show online devices.
2. After creating a Hermes Platform Agent bound to an online device, local Desktop chat can work, but sending a message from a remote LobeHub client to the same agent still crashes the bound Desktop/device process with:

```text
A JavaScript error occurred in the main process
Uncaught Exception: Error: spawn hermes ENOENT
    at ChildProcess._handle.onexit (node:internal/child_process:287:19)
    at onErrorNT (node:internal/child_process:508:16)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:90:21)
```

This looks like the remote Platform Agent execution path still relies on a bare `hermes` binary name instead of resolving the executable path from the device capability/profile detection result, a configured path, or a login shell PATH.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.3, arm64
- LobeHub Desktop: `2.2.4-canary.6`
- LobeHub CLI bundled version observed: `0.0.29`
- Device gateway: `https://device-gateway.lobehub.com`
- Hermes Agent: `Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5) · upstream 88dbf951`
- Hermes executable path on the bound device:

```bash
/Users/xnode1/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Log in with the LobeHub CLI:

```bash
npx -y @lobehub/cli login
npx -y @lobehub/cli connect --daemon
```

2. Verify devices are online:

```bash
npx -y @lobehub/cli connect status
npx -y @lobehub/cli device list
```

Observed device list includes online devices similar to:

```text
DEVICE ID                         HOSTNAME                PLATFORM  STATUS  CONNECTED
d4690eb1424653bdcbf012ee0e1bb441  XNode1deMac-mini.local  darwin    online  ...
9f3e531749b31ddf819e7f2e93eb2b69  YANBO                   darwin    online  ...
```

3. In LobeHub Desktop, enable Labs / Platform Agent.
4. Open **Create Platform Agent / 接入助理** and choose Hermes.
5. In step 2, the device selector can be empty even though `Settings → Devices` shows devices and `lh device list` shows online devices.
6. After selecting/creating a Hermes Platform Agent bound to `d4690eb1424653bdcbf012ee0e1bb441`, send a message from the local Desktop: it can work.
7. Send a message from a remote LobeHub client to the same Hermes Platform Agent.

## Expected behavior

- Create Platform Agent should show the same online devices as `Settings → Devices` and `lh device list`.
- Remote clients should be able to dispatch to the bound device without requiring the remote client machine to have Hermes installed.
- On the bound device, LobeHub should run the Hermes executable that passed capability detection, or a configurable absolute path, instead of relying on Electron/daemon PATH containing `hermes`.

## Actual behavior

- The Create Platform Agent wizard can show an empty device selector while the Settings device page and CLI show online devices.
- Remote messages fail with `spawn hermes ENOENT` in the main process.
- The error remains even after confirming the agent is bound to the expected online device.

## Investigation notes

I inspected the packaged Desktop app and the current source layout. There appear to be multiple execution paths:

### Device picker mismatch

`CreatePlatformAgent` uses `device.listDevices`, but then filters devices with:

```ts
const onlineDevices = (devices ?? []).filter((d) => d.online);
```

The Settings device list displays the full `device.listDevices` result. This can make the create wizard show no choices even when Settings shows devices.

A local hot patch that changed the wizard to show all devices sorted by `online` first, and auto-select the first device, made the device appear in the wizard.

### Hermes executable resolution

There are at least two relevant Hermes execution paths:

1. Desktop direct/tool path, using `checkPlatformCapability`, `getAgentProfile`, and `runHeteroTask` in the Desktop main process.
2. Remote gateway-driven agent run path:

```text
gateway agent_run_request
  → Desktop executeAgentRun
  → spawnLhHeteroExec
  → lh hetero exec
  → bundled resources/bin/lobe-cli.js
  → spawn('hermes', ['chat', ...])
```

The remote path appears to use `lh hetero exec` and the bundled CLI eventually spawns a bare `hermes`, which fails under Electron/daemon PATH:

```text
spawn hermes ENOENT
```

Local hot patches replacing bare `hermes` with the absolute executable path in the Desktop main bundle and bundled CLI improved parts of the flow, but the official product should probably solve this at the resolver/config level rather than via patching packaged bundles.

## Suggested fixes

1. For Platform Agent device selection:
   - Reuse the same device list semantics as Settings, or show offline/unknown devices disabled instead of hiding them entirely.
   - If filtering to online devices, surface why devices were filtered out.
   - Refetch when entering step 2, not only when opening the modal.

2. For Hermes execution:
   - Add a per-platform executable resolver, e.g. `resolvePlatformBinary('hermes')`, that uses one of:
     - an explicit configured path,
     - a path returned/stored from capability detection,
     - `command -v hermes` executed in a login shell on macOS,
     - known Hermes install paths such as `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes`.
   - Pass the resolved path into both Desktop direct execution and `lh hetero exec` / bundled CLI execution.
   - Avoid requiring the **remote client** to install Hermes; only the bound execution device should need Hermes.
   - Include the resolved command/path in debug logs when spawning Platform Agent tasks.

## Workaround tried locally

I hot patched the packaged Desktop app (`app.asar`) to:

- Show all devices in the Create Platform Agent wizard, sorted by online status.
- Auto-select the first device in step 2.
- Replace some bare `hermes` calls in Desktop main process with:

```text
/Users/xnode1/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes
```

This confirmed the device picker issue, but remote dispatch still exposed the `lh hetero exec` / bundled CLI path, which also needs binary resolution.

## Additional question

Should remote LobeHub clients need the same patched Desktop version, or should the remote client only send the request to the gateway while the bound device executes Hermes? My expectation is the latter: the bound device should be the only machine requiring Hermes installation/path resolution.

title: ContentLoading exposes raw operation i18n keys for internal operations
body:
### Problem

The message-level loading indicator can render raw i18n keys for internal operation types.

Example observed in chat while activating/calling a tool:

```text
operation.createToolMessage...
```

### Root Cause

`src/features/Conversation/Messages/components/ContentLoading.tsx` directly translates `operation.${operationType}` for every running `OperationType`.

However, `OperationType` includes many internal/bookkeeping operation types, such as `createToolMessage`, `executeToolCall`, `pluginApi`, `builtinTool*`, `searchWorkflow`, and `callLLM`. Most of those do not have `operation.*` locale keys, so react-i18next falls back to displaying the raw key.

`src/features/Conversation/ChatInput/OpStatusTray.tsx` already normalizes these internal operation types into user-facing phases such as `toolCalling`, `searching`, `generating`, and `compressing`, but `ContentLoading` does not reuse that mapping.

### Expected Behavior

Internal operation types should never be shown as raw i18n keys. They should either:

- render a localized user-facing phase label, e.g. `Calling tools...` / `Searching...`, or
- fall back to the generic loading animation when no user-facing label is appropriate.

### Suggested Fix

Extract the operation-to-activity mapping from `OpStatusTray` into a shared helper and use it from both `OpStatusTray` and `ContentLoading`.

This would allow cases like `createToolMessage`, `executeToolCall`, `pluginApi`, and `builtinTool*` to render the existing localized `opStatusTray.status.toolCalling` label instead of leaking `operation.createToolMessage`.

title: 附件类型限制过严，Agent能正常解析的文件无法上传 The attachment type restrictions are too strict, preventing the upload of files that the Agent can normally parse.
body: ### 📱 Client Type Web (Desktop Browser) ### 💻 Operating System iOS ### 📦 Deployment Platform Official Cloud ### 📌 Version v2.2.3 ### 🌐 Browser Safari ### 🐛 What happened? LobeHub聊天界面支持上传附件，然而附件上传功能会对**文件类型**进行严格限制，这将导致大量Agent有能力通过脚本或终端正常解析的文件（如HTML代码、ZIP压缩包）被**拒绝上传**，严重影响用户体验。 The LobeHub chat interface supports file uploads, but the upload feature imposes strict restrictions on **file types**. This causes many files that Agents could normally parse via scripts or terminals (such as HTML code and ZIP archives) to be **rejected during upload**, significantly impairing user experience. ### 📷 How to reproduce it? 直接在LobeHub聊天界面上传任意一个非白名单内的图片、文档类型的文件，均能复现问题，这是我当时被拒绝上传的ZIP文件，供测试（我当时希望让Agent解释这个技能，而不是安装这个Skill，请不要建议我使用添加Skill的功能）：[glmv-pdf-to-web.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28910417/glmv-pdf-to-web.zip) The issue can be reproduced by directly uploading any image or document file not on the whitelist in the LobeHub chat interface. Attached is the ZIP file that was rejected during my upload attempt, provided for testing purposes (I intended to have the Agent explain this Skill rather than install it, so please do not suggest using the "Add Skill" feature): [glmv-pdf-to-web.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28910417/glmv-pdf-to-web.zip) ### 🚦 What it should be? 我希望LobeHub能分情况处理文件上传白名单，而不是一刀切只允许特定文件，因为压缩包文件或其他文件在工作中同样极其常见，若全部禁用会严重影响LobeHub的实用性： - 当处于“对话”模式：允许上传所有文本或多媒体（图像、视频、音频，仅限多模态模型）类型的文件，因为它们不需要工具调用就能被大模型所理解。 - **最佳方案**：使用JavaScript检查文件头/MIME type，而不是只看扩展名来检验文件究竟是二进制数据还是图像或多媒体文件，而不是根据文件扩展名，防止误判造成某些配置文件被禁止上传，特别是Linux下，很多配置文件都是不带有扩展名的，例如`Dockerfile`、`Makefile`，根据文件名判断容易把支持的文件类型判定为不支持。 - **普通方案**：根据扩展名判断文件类型是否是图像或纯文本，但是支持更加宽泛的文件扩展名。 - 当处于“智能”模式（Agent模式）：移除文件类型限制，允许上传任何类型的文件，因为许多非多媒体文件均能由Agent通过工具调用来解析，无需过滤。 I hope LobeHub can handle the file upload whitelist in a more nuanced way, rather than applying a one-size-fits-all restriction that only allows specific file types. Compressed files and other formats are equally common in professional workflows, and blocking them entirely would significantly undermine LobeHub's practicality: - In "Conversation" mode: All text or multimedia (images, videos, audio, limited to multimodal models) file types are allowed to be uploaded, as they can be understood by the large model without requiring tool calls. - **Best Approach**: Use JavaScript to check the file header/MIME type rather than relying solely on the file extension to determine whether the file is binary data, an text or multimedia file. This prevents misjudgment that could lead to certain configuration files being blocked from upload, especially on Linux, where many configuration files lack extensions, such as `Dockerfile` and `Makefile`. Judging by the file name alone may incorrectly classify supported file types as unsupported. - **Standard approach**: Determine file types based on extensions, but support a broader range of file extensions for images and plain text. - In "Agent" mode: Remove file type restrictions, allowing uploads of any file type, as many non-multimedia files can be parsed by the Agent through tool calls without the need for filtering. ### 📝 Additional Information 我之所以选择了iOS作为操作系统但选择了Web Browser (Desktop)作为客户端类型是因为我使用了iPadOS Safari的“请求桌面网站功能”且在连接了实体键盘和触控板的情况下操作网站。 The reason I chose iOS as the operating system but selected "Web Browser (Desktop)" as the client type is that I use the "Request Desktop Website" feature in iPadOS Safari and operate the website with a physical keyboard and trackpad connected. ### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR? EMM relapse may present at any anatomical site with frequent CNS involvement. Biological features in- clude increased proliferation and low rate of marrow involve- ment. Prognosis remains poor despite intensive treatment. Keywords Multiple myeloma . Relapse . Extramedullary anaplastic plasmacytoma . Cytogenetics . Meningeal neoplasms . Proliferation . Ki-67 antigen Introduction Extramedullary growth of plasma cell tumors can occur as a solitary formation without bone marrow involvement (soli- tary plasmacytoma of the bone), as an extramedullary mul- tiple myeloma (eMM) with co-existing bone marrow infiltration at primary diagnosis, or as a distinct relapse pattern in multiple myeloma (MM) patients during the course of their disease. Whereas the incidence in the first two groups did not change markedly over the last years, a notably increasing number of eMM relapse could be ob- served in pretreated MM patients. In a recent longitudinal study on 1,003 MM patients, the incidence of eMM during follow-up was shown to have increased from 6.5×1,000 person years in the period 1971–1993 to as high as 48.4× 1,000 person years in the period 2000–2007 [1]. Overall, between 6% and 15% of all MM patients will develop eMM lesions during their clinical course [1–3], and incidence can be as high as 37% (10 of 27) in patients with previous allogeneic stem cell transplantation [4]. The reason for extramedullary manifestation of myeloma remains largely unclear. Usually, the cells are strongly de- pendent on the bone marrow microenvironment. Interac- tions with hemopoietic and non-hemopoietic cells are responsible for myeloma cell growth, survival, migration, and drug resistance [5]. Therefore, cultivation of primary myeloma cells without stromal cell co-cultures in vitro is barely possible, and commercially available cell lines most- ly do have their source from eMM lesions [6]. Molecular differences between MM and eMM lesions are documented in small case series. Bink and co-workers ana- lyzed 38 cases of primary extramedullary plasmacytoma by fluorescence in situ hybridization and compared the cytoge- netic findings with systemic MM. Cytogenetically, extrame- dullary plasmacytoma and multiple myeloma were closely related. Only the t(11;14)(q13;q32) translocation was absent in eMM group [7]. López-Anglada and colleagues reported on a case of relapsed eMM with a newly acquired p53 deletion in the eMM lesion but wild type p53 in the bone marrow [8]. Another group immunostained paired bone marrow and extramedullary biopsies from 12 cases of MM for p53 and Ki67 (MIB-1, proliferative index) and found an increased nuclear accumulation of p53 in the eMM sites consistent with mutated protein. The proliferation marker Ki67 was significantly increased with a proliferation rate of 40% of all cells. Ki67 in the bone marrow of patients with medullary MM stained markedly lower at less than 5% demonstrating the aggressive growth pattern of eMM [9]. Interestingly, CD56—a cell adhesion molecule positive in about 70% of all MM—was not differentially expressed in eMM. Conflicting data were shown by Dahl and col- leagues, who demonstrated that in all seven eMM cases, CD56 was completely downregulated [10]. Chan et al. reported two cases of CNS involvement due to myeloma cells which were also lacking CD56 in the cerebrospinal fluid but expressing CD56 in the bone marrow [11]. How- ever, the numbers are still too small, and further studies warranted investigating the role of CD56 in myeloma cell/ bone marrow microenvironment interactions and extrame- dullary manifestations. We therefore analyzed relapse pat- terns and individual treatment decisions of eMM cases at our institution to further elucidate this challenging clinical manifestation of multiple myeloma. Methods We screened the myeloma registry of the University Hospi- tal of Wuerzburg, Germany, for MM patients who devel- oped eMM relapse during the course of their disease. From January 2007 to June 2010, 24 eMM relapses were identified among 357 MM patients. Extramedullary relapse was defined as cytologically proven malignant effusion, as a biopsy-proven plasma cell tumor outside the bone marrow, and not originating from skeletal structures (according to Minnema et al. [12]). Statistical analysis For the statistical analysis, SPSS 12.0.1 for Windows (SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL, USA) was used. Overall survival (OS) was measured in months and defined as the time from the date of eMM relapse until the date of death or last follow- up. Progression-free survival (PFS) was measured in months defined as the time from the date of response following any therapy until the date of progression or death from any cause or last follow-up. Patients lost to follow-up were censored at date of last information. Probabilities of OS and PFS were calculated using the Kaplan–Meier method. Results Patient characteristics In all, 357 MM patients were treated at our single institution from January 2007 to June 2010, 24 (6.7%) of whom developed eMM. The median age at the time of relapse was 56 years (range, 41–79). The male/female ratio was 1.67:1. Median time from initial diagnosis to eMM relapse was 39 months and the median interval from last therapy, 5 months (range, 0–32). It is worth mentioning that six patients progressed at extramedullary sites during chemo- therapy for systemic MM. Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels were increased in 19 of 24 patients at the diagnosis of eMM with a median of 395 U/L (range, 151–2,758 U/L). Molecular cytogenetics from initial MM diagnosis was available in 19 patients. Here, 13q deletion was most fre- quent in 11 of 19 cases followed by t(4,14) and 17p. Inter- estingly, t(4;14) was found in 10 of 19 patients (52%) and deletion 17p in 4 of 19 (21%), respectively (Table 1). Those incidences, when compared to medullary myeloma, are sig- nificantly higher. For the latter, t(4;14) and del (17p) are expected to have incidences of 15% and 11%, respectively [13, 14]. Only 3 of the 24 patients had been referred to our clinic with overt extramedullary relapsed MM, which could confer slight bias. Prior to extramedullary manifestation, 22 of 24 patients had received melphalan-based high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplantation, and 6 of 24, allogeneic transplantation; novel agents had previously been used in 20 of 24 patients (Table 2a). Of the 24 patients described here, 2 had eMM relapses after their first-line 1032 Ann Hematol (2012) 91:1031–1037 therapy, 9 after second-line, and 13 after three or four lines of treatment. Type of relapse pattern Most frequently, eMM occurred at soft tissue sites (16 of 24) followed by parenchymal involvement (liver, lung, breast, larynx, kidney, parotid gland) in 6 of 24. Malignant effusion was seen in 4 of 24 patients. CNS involvement (leptome- ningeal, cerebral masses) was observed in 5 of 24 of the patients. Ten patients had more than one organ site involved. No patient with isolated secondary plasma cell leukemia as extramedullary manifestation was included. At diagnosis of eMM relapse, bone marrow infiltration was absent in 11 of 24, and in 5 of 24, infiltration was less than 20%. Thus, over two thirds had no or only minimal bone marrow infiltration at the time of occurrence of eMM disease. Due to the retrospective nature of this study, only ten biopsy specimens from eMM lesions were available for further immunohistochemistry. CD138, CD56, and Ki67 status were collected and compared to the bone marrow findings at initial diagnosis of MM. CD138 was stably expressed in bone marrow and in eMM in all ten cases. CD56 was positive in 8 of 10 bone marrow biopsies and at eMM diagnosis still in four of the initially positive eight cases. A strikingly elevated Ki67 was found within all eMM cases: the mean proliferation index in extramedullary sites was 67% (range, 20–90); Ki-67 values in bone marrow were not evaluable due to elevated Ki67 in non-malignant hema- topoietic bystander cells (Table 3). Treatment and response EM relapse was treated with radiation therapy, dose-intense chemotherapy, novel agent-based therapies, and auto- allogeneic stem cell transplantation (SCT) concepts including DLI administration. Sixteen of 24 patients underwent radia- tion therapy as local therapy. Along with dose-intense chemo- therapy (6 of 24), autologous peripheral stem cell support was given for anticipation of high hematotoxicity in this heavily pretreated cohort. Novel agents were administered in 22 of 24 with 16 of 24 bortezomib, 12 of 24 lenalidomide, and 8 of 24 thalidomide. Novel agent-based regimes had been: VDT- PACE, VRD-ICE, RAD, and VCD(T). In the setting of auto-SCT, melphalan was given additionally. Allo-SCT was performed in 13 of 24 of the patients; DLI was administered post-allo-SCT in 5 of 24 patients (Table 2b). Median progression-free survival was 2 months (95% CI 0.08–3.92). Median OS was 7 months (95% CI 3.56–10.43) (Fig. 1a and b). Eleven patients survived for longer than 6 months, 3 patients longer than 12 months. All three long-time survivors had received high-dose chemo- therapy with the two ongoing long-term survivors having received allo-SCT indicating graft versus myeloma (GvM) also affecting extramedullary sites. We further determined whether there was any difference in OS for patients who developed eMM with previous allogeneic SCT (n06) versus no allogeneic SCT (n018). However, mean OS was identical (p00.44) (Fig. 1c and d) Discussion In this retrospective study, we demonstrate features of 24 MM patients with a median age of 56 years having relapsed at extramedullary sites. To our knowledge, this is the largest case series investigating this uncommon MM manifestation. In our center, the risk for developing eMM was 6.7%, which is consistent with the estimated risk found by others [1]. Key findings were (1) an extramedullary progression without relevant bone marrow involvement in two thirds, (2) CNS involvement in a fifth, (3) a dramatically increased prolifer- ation index Ki67 within biopsied eMM lesions, and (4) an adverse prognosis (PFS and OS of 2 and 7 months, respec- tively). The eMM relapses after allogeneic transplantation did not differ significantly in manifestation and outcomes when compared to patients without prior allo-SCT. Several treatment modalities had been used on an individual basis without identifying a single convincing approach; however, long-time survival occurred only after allo-SCT. These findings add to smaller series [1, 15–17]. A novel feature in our study was the high incidence of CNS manifes- tations, an anatomical site which is not commonly involved in plasma cell dyscrasias. This fits to a large study from the Arkansas group in which 18 MM patients with CNS involve- ment were included. The authors found a strong association of CNS involvement with high-risk chromosomal abnormalities, additional extramedullary manifestations, and elevated LDH levels. Furthermore, Petersen et al., by reviewing the litera- ture, found 53 cases of meningeal myelomatosis and showed a frequent association with circulating plasma cells and an over- representation of IgD and IgA isotype [18, 19]. However, clinicians should be aware of CNS involvement as a potential manifestation of eMM disease. In contrast, Ki67 stained up to 90% of all cancer cells in our series suggesting a more aggressive behavior [21]. Cytogenetically, the patients in this study showed a high number of abnormalities being associated with adverse prognosis like 17p deletion, translocation (4;14), and 1q deletion. Overall, 11 of 19 evaluable patients (58%) displayed a high-risk profile at initial diagnosis of MM which might be linked to the short PFS and OS in this study. Clinically, presentation of eMM is often paradoxical. Whereas the bone marrow remains free of or shows only modest infiltration of MM cells or responds well to chemo- therapy, extramedullary lesions frequently progress and are refractory to further treatment lines [2, 17, 22, 23]. In our case series, about two thirds of eMM patients had no or low- grade plasma cell infiltration in the bone marrow. This might be due to selecting highly resistant clones, which can grow independent of bone marrow stroma cells [24, 25]. In a multivariate analysis by Varettoni and colleagues, the risk of extramedullary spread was neither increased by prior high-dose therapy nor treatment with bortezomib or thalid- omide/lenalidomide [1]. In addition, there are several case reports in the literature in which novel agents successfully were used to treat eMM relapse [26–29]. As of yet, it is not proven that novel agents (for instance by clonal selection) do contribute to eMM formation, but may be beneficial for several MM patients [30]. Since neither an adequate diag- nostic algorithm nor a valid therapeutic guideline is avail- able, there is a clear need for prospective trials including novel imaging techniques [31, 32]. Interestingly, CD138 was stably expressed in all our histologically examined eMM lesions, indicating CD 138 as a promising target for future antibody-based therapies. Since no targeted treatment is available so far, polyche- motherapy also used for aggressive B cell lymphomas might be an option due to the high proliferation seen in eMM. EDAP, CHOP-like, DCEP, or IEV as well as auto- and allogeneic SCT are reported in a few anecdotal publications [15, 29, 33, 34]. Although some response could be docu- mented, the number of patients is still too small and, unfor- tunately, disease control not durable. When eMM relapse occurs after allogeneic stem cell transplantation, donor lym- phocyte transfusions (DLI) with/without prior lymphode- pleting therapy can be considered. Minnema and colleagues treated three eMM patients with DLI ± bortezo- mib and observed two CR and 1 SD. Again, PFS and survival is not presented for these patients [12]. Other inves- tigators have reported an effect of DLI treatment given as monotherapy. In three out of four patients with EM relapse, a response indicated a GvM to be effective in eMM relapses [35]. However, an effective standard procedure for system- atic therapy has not been established so far. An effective therapy for local disease control is radiation therapy. There are several studies especially for classical plasmacytoma in which radiation therapy was very success- ful [36, 37]. In our opinion, radiotherapy in the setting of relapsed eMM is a reasonable palliative modality, which can reduce eMM masses locally but is often followed by new manifestations outside the irradiation field. Conclusions Extramedullary myeloma remains challenging from both a therapeutic as well as a scientific perspective. Neither a pathomechanism nor a valid clinical approach is defined in this setting. Therefore, comprehensive studies on the biolo- gy of eMM as well as prospective clinical trials are urgently needed. Longitudinal tumor sampling and gene expression profiling in MM patients may reveal accumulations in ge- nomic instability. Insight into the latter might contribute to the understanding of diagnosis and treatment for this yet rare, but increasingly encountered, and still dreaded compli- cation of multiple myeloma. title: Custom provider client request mode (fetchOnClient) does not forward X-Topic-Id to API base URL
body:
## Summary

When **Use client request mode** (`llm.fetchOnClient`) is enabled on a **custom OpenAI-compatible provider**, the browser sends `/v1/chat/completions` directly to the configured API base URL. LobeHub does **not** attach per-conversation topic identity headers (`X-Topic-Id`, `X-lobe-trace`) on that outbound request.

Stateful backends that map LangGraph / OpenAI-compatible `thread_id` from the conversation topic cannot maintain checkpoint continuity across turns.

## Expected behaviour

Each LobeHub chat topic has a stable `topicId` in LobeHub's DB. When client request mode calls a custom provider, that id should be forwarded so the upstream API can key state per conversation, e.g.:

- `X-Topic-Id: <topicId>` (or existing header convention used when proxying built-in providers)
- and/or `X-lobe-trace` (base64 JSON including `topicId`) as documented for trace metadata

## Actual behaviour

Outbound `fetchOnClient` requests to custom API base URLs include the OpenAI payload (`model`, `messages`, etc.) but **omit** topic/session headers.

**Server-side proxy path** (`/webapi/chat/…` → custom base URL) also does not forward these headers in our testing — client mode was enabled specifically to work around that, but headers are still missing on the FastAPI hop.

## Impact

- Every turn gets a new upstream `thread_id` when the API falls back to hashing message content
- Multi-turn clarify / HITL / orchestrator checkpoint state is lost between messages in the same UI conversation
- Parallel chats with the same opener can collide on turn 1

## Environment

- LobeHub self-hosted (v2.2.4 tested, 14 Jun 2026)
- Custom provider with API base URL pointing to self-hosted FastAPI OpenAI-compatible server
- **Use client request mode** enabled on the provider
- CORS configured on upstream (`OPTIONS /v1/chat/completions` → 200)

## Reproduction

1. Add custom provider with external `/v1` base URL
2. Enable **Use client request mode**
3. Open a new chat, send message, send follow-up in same topic
4. Inspect Network → request to **custom API** `/v1/chat/completions`
5. Observe: no `X-Topic-Id` / `X-lobe-trace` headers; upstream logs show different session/thread per turn

## Suggested fix

In the client request path (likely `src/services/chat/index.ts` or equivalent `fetchOnClient` implementation), merge the same `requestHeaders` / trace metadata used for built-in providers when calling custom `baseURL`, including at minimum `X-Topic-Id` from the active topic.

## References

- Consumer integration expecting these headers: [personal-ai-os lobehub.md](https://github.com/Myrz-Jay/personal-ai-os/blob/main/docs/integrations/lobehub.md) (self-hosted; not affiliated with LobeHub core team)
- Related tracking on consumer side: [Myrz-Jay/personal-ai-os#22](https://github.com/Myrz-Jay/personal-ai-os/issues/22)

title: Desktop onboarding loops back to login after successful LobeHub Cloud authorization
body:
### Environment

- App: LobeHub Desktop
- Version: 2.2.4
- OS: macOS
- Storage mode: LobeHub Cloud sync
- Account plan shown in UI: Free

### Problem

After successfully authorizing LobeHub Cloud in the browser, the desktop app shows the success state and allows clicking **Start using**. The app briefly enters the home page, but after reopening/restarting LobeHub Desktop it returns to:

```text
app://renderer/desktop-onboarding?screen=login
```

The page again shows **Authorization Successful** and the **Start using** button, creating a loop.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open LobeHub Desktop 2.2.4 on macOS.
2. Start the LobeHub Cloud login flow.
3. Complete authorization in the browser.
4. Browser shows `Authorization Successful`.
5. Desktop app shows the authorized account and the **Start using** button.
6. Click **Start using**.
7. Home page opens successfully.
8. Quit and reopen LobeHub Desktop.

### Actual behavior

The app returns to the desktop onboarding login route:

```text
app://renderer/desktop-onboarding?screen=login
```

The UI still says authorization succeeded, but the user has to click **Start using** again. After another restart, the same loop happens.

### Expected behavior

After successful authorization and clicking **Start using**, reopening LobeHub Desktop should go directly to the home page instead of returning to desktop onboarding login.

### Local diagnostics

I verified the following locally without printing token values:

- `lobehub-settings.json` still has cloud sync enabled:

```json
{
  "dataSyncConfig.active": true,
  "dataSyncConfig.storageMode": "cloud",
  "hasEncryptedTokens": true,
  "hasAccessToken": true,
  "hasRefreshToken": true
}
```

- The main process can load/decrypt the token and initially attempts to load `/`.
- Clearing the broken remote config via the app IPC and reauthorizing succeeds.
- After clicking **Start using**, the app reaches the home page.
- After a normal app restart, it goes back to `desktop-onboarding?screen=login`.
- The localStorage key `lobechat:desktop:onboarding:screen:v1` is repeatedly restored/written as `login`.

### Suspected cause

From the bundled renderer code, desktop onboarding completion uses session storage for `lobechat:desktop:onboarding:completed:v1`, while persistent storage only tracks `lobechat:desktop:onboarding:everCompleted:v1`.

In the desktop onboarding page logic:

- `resolveInitialScreen()` falls back to `Login` when `everCompleted` is true.
- The effect persists `currentScreen` into `lobechat:desktop:onboarding:screen:v1`.
- On the final **Start using** action, the code clears the saved screen and navigates to `/`, but because `currentScreen` is still `login`, the persistence effect can write `login` back again.

This seems to make a successfully authorized returning user repeatedly land on the login onboarding screen after restart.

### Notes

A local workaround that temporarily allowed entering the home page was:

1. Clear remote server config via the app IPC.
2. Reauthorize in the browser.
3. Click **Start using**.
4. Remove `lobechat:desktop:onboarding:screen:v1`.

However, after a normal restart, the app still returned to the onboarding login route, so this looks like an app-side routing/onboarding state bug rather than corrupted user data.

title: [Bug] Desktop 2.2.5 (Windows, Cloud): sign-in loop — /api/auth/get-session returns null while OIDC bearer token is valid → bounces to "Sign in to sync"
body:
### 📦 Platform

Desktop App (Electron) — official LobeHub Cloud (`app.lobehub.com`), `storageMode: cloud`

### 📌 Version

**2.2.5** (broke on auto-update 2.2.3 → 2.2.4 → 2.2.5). **Downgrading to 2.2.3 resolves it.**

### 💻 Operating System

Windows 11

### 🐛 Bug Description

After the auto-update to 2.2.5, the desktop app is stuck in a sign-in loop on a **Cloud** account. The onboarding screen shows **"Sign in to sync across devices / Authorization Successful"**; clicking **Get Started** flashes the dashboard, then immediately bounces back to the login screen. Infinite loop. Hard restart / reinstall of 2.2.5 does not help.

### 🔍 Root cause (traced via remote debugging)

The auth state is **split-brain**:

- **Main process is healthy** — `AuthCtr: Token is valid, starting auto-refresh timer` (token not expired), device-gateway connects with the correct `userId`.
- The **OIDC bearer token works** — tRPC calls to `https://app.lobehub.com/trpc/lambda/user.getUserState` return **HTTP 200 with the full account**.
- But `GET https://app.lobehub.com/api/auth/get-session` returns **HTTP 200 with body `null`**.

The renderer derives `isLogin` from **`/api/auth/get-session` (NextAuth)** rather than from the working bearer token. Because get-session is `null`, the route guard treats the user as logged out and redirects `/` → `/desktop-onboarding?screen=login` on every load — hence the loop. (`onboarding:everCompleted:v1` is already `1`, so it lands straight on the Login step.)

### 📷 Recurrence Steps

1. Sign in to a **Cloud** account on Desktop 2.2.5 (Windows).
2. Complete OAuth → screen shows "Authorization Successful".
3. Click **Get Started** → dashboard flashes → back to "Sign in to sync". Repeats indefinitely.

### 🚦 Expected Behavior

With a valid OIDC bearer token (tRPC authenticated), the desktop should treat the user as logged in and load the workspace — not gate `isLogin` on a NextAuth `get-session` that is `null` for token-based desktop auth.

### 📝 Additional Information

**Workaround:** downgrade to **2.2.3** (gates login on the bearer token) → loads straight to the dashboard, chat works.

Diagnosed by launching the app with `--remote-debugging-port` and inspecting the renderer network: `user.getUserState` (tRPC, bearer-authenticated) returns the account, while `/api/auth/get-session` returns `null`. Happy to provide more detail / HAR if useful.

Deploy and monetize agent-built apps — login, database, usage billing, and end-user-pays. The MCP server lets an agent search and invoke the full SettleMesh capability catalog (web search, LLMs, image/video generation, managed SQL, hosted agents), with a confirm step before any paid call.

### Why it benefits users
One key lets an agent both call paid capabilities and turn an app into a paid product (one-command deploy with login + DB + billing). Already live in the official MCP registry and installable in Cursor / Claude Code.

title: [Request] Add AnyAPI to the MCP marketplace
body:
### 🥰 Feature Description

We'd like to list **AnyAPI** on LobeHub's MCP marketplace (https://lobehub.com/mcp). Filing as an issue per the documented fallback path (see recent `[Request] Add … MCP Server to the MCP marketplace` issues), since the submit modal is Turnstile-gated.

AnyAPI is a **remote, hosted** MCP server (Streamable HTTP) — no install and no npm package. It gives an AI agent one API key and one USD wallet to discover, inspect, and run hundreds of scraping and data APIs (social media, search results, general web data) through a single normalized interface.

### 🧐 Proposed Solution

Index our GitHub repository and remote MCP endpoint:

- **Name**: AnyAPI
- **Repo**: https://github.com/getanyapi-com/skills
- **Homepage**: https://getanyapi.com
- **Docs**: https://getanyapi.com/docs (MCP page: https://getanyapi.com/docs/mcp-server)
- **Publisher**: AnyAPI (getanyapi.com)
- **License**: Apache-2.0
- **Logo (512×512 PNG)**: https://getanyapi.com/icon-512.png
- **Version**: 0.1.0

**What it does**

AnyAPI gives AI agents one API key and one USD wallet to call hundreds of scraping and data APIs — Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, Facebook, Google search results, general web scraping, and more — through a single normalized interface. Every API exposes a normalized input/output JSON Schema, so an agent discovers, inspects, and runs any of them with the same loop. Pricing is real-dollar pay-per-request with no subscriptions; failed calls are never charged because AnyAPI fails over across upstream providers automatically under one price reservation. The provider is always reported as AnyAPI.

**4 tools**

- `list_apis` — discover APIs; optional `query`/`category` filters; token-light (no schemas).
- `get_api` — full definition of one API incl. normalized input/output JSON Schema.
- `run_api` — execute an API by SKU with normalized input; returns output, `costUsd`, items; supports context-budget controls (`fields`, `max_items`, `summary`). Charges on success only.
- `get_balance` — remaining USD wallet balance for the key.

**Transport & auth**

- **Remote — Streamable HTTP** (hosted by AnyAPI, no install):
  `https://api.getanyapi.com/mcp`
- **Auth**: API key as `Authorization: Bearer aa_live_...`. Discovery (`list_apis`/`get_api`) works without a key; running an API requires one. Mint a key at https://getanyapi.com/dashboard/keys.

**Quick start (Claude Desktop / Cursor)**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "anyapi": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.getanyapi.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${ANYAPI_API_KEY}" }
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add anyapi --transport http https://api.getanyapi.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer ${ANYAPI_API_KEY}"`

There is also a one-step skill + MCP install: `claude plugin marketplace add getanyapi-com/skills` then `claude plugin install anyapi@anyapi`.

### 📝 Additional Information

Quality checklist (from LobeHub's submit modal):

| Check | Status |
|-------|--------|
| Has README | ✅ https://github.com/getanyapi-com/skills#readme |
| Provides ≥1 installation method | ✅ Remote Streamable HTTP URL + one-line `claude mcp add` + JSON config |
| Has ≥1 Skill (Tool) | ✅ 4 tools (`list_apis`, `get_api`, `run_api`, `get_balance`) |
| Has LICENSE | ✅ Apache-2.0 |
| Offers friendly installation | ✅ one-line `claude mcp add` + JSON for Claude Desktop / Cursor + `claude plugin install` |

This is a remote (hosted) Streamable HTTP server, so there is no npm package or stdio command — it is added by URL with a Bearer API key.

**Tags**: scraping, data, web-scraping, social-media, search, data-aggregation, api-gateway, marketplace

Thanks!

title: [Bug] Sub-topics cause silent data loss and are inaccessible after creation (regression from v2.2.4)
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Desktop App (Electron)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Official Cloud

### 📌 Version

2.2.6

### 🌐 Browser

Other

### 🐛 What happened?

Three regressions affecting sub-topics were introduced in v2.2.5 and are still present in v2.2.6:

1. [CRITICAL] Starting a sub-topic from a message partway up the main topic and sending a prompt overwrites all messages that came after the sub-topic branching point in the main topic. This causes permanent, silent data loss with no warning.

2. Sub-topics no longer appear listed under their parent topic after creation. Navigating away from the sub-topic makes it permanently inaccessible — there is no way to return to it.

3. Hovering over messages within a sub-topic no longer shows action buttons (edit, regenerate, etc.).

All three worked correctly in v2.2.4.


### 📷 How to reproduce it?

Content loss (critical):
1. Open a main topic with several messages
2. Select a message partway up the conversation and create a sub-topic from it
3. Send a prompt in the sub-topic and receive a reply
4. Return to the main topic
5. All messages that existed after the sub-topic branching point are now gone

Sub-topic disappearing:
1. Open a main topic
2. Create a sub-topic
3. Send a prompt and receive a reply (confirming the sub-topic has content and is not auto-closed)
4. Navigate away from the sub-topic
5. The sub-topic is not listed under the parent topic and cannot be returned to

Missing hover actions:
1. Open a sub-topic
2. Hover over any message
3. No edit or regenerate buttons appear


### 🚦 What it should be?

- Creating and using a sub-topic should never modify or delete messages in the parent topic
- Sub-topics should remain listed under their parent topic after creation and persist when navigating away
- Hovering over sub-topic messages should reveal action buttons (edit, regenerate, etc.), as in v2.2.4


### 📝 Additional Information

Regression introduced in v2.2.5, also present in v2.2.6.
Last known working version: v2.2.4.

Issue 1 poses a high risk of unrecoverable data loss — users have no indication that main topic content will be overwritten when starting a sub-topic.

title: PostgreSQL data import does not remap topics.agentId, causing FK failures
body:
## Bug: PostgreSQL data import does not remap `topics.agentId`, causing FK failures

### Version

- `@lobehub/lobehub`: 2.2.6
- Deployment: Docker Compose self-hosted
- Database mode: PostgreSQL

### What happened

Importing a PostgreSQL-format export through Settings -> Data Storage uploads the JSON successfully and calls `importer.importByFile`, but topic/message records fail to import.

The UI reports "Data import completed", but the import detail shows:

- `topics`: all rows failed
- `messages`: all rows failed
- `messagePlugins`: all rows failed

Server logs show the first real failure:

```text
insert or update on table "topics" violates foreign key constraint "topics_agent_id_agents_id_fk"
Key (agent_id)=(agt_RxaJn49K0Bxm) is not present in table "agents".
```

### Root cause

`packages/database/src/repositories/dataImporter/index.ts` remaps foreign keys based on `IMPORT_TABLE_CONFIG`.

`messages` already remaps `agentId` via:

```ts
{ field: 'agentId', sourceTable: 'agents' }
```

But `topics` only remaps `sessionId`:

```ts
{
  relations: [
    {
      field: 'sessionId',
      sourceTable: 'sessions',
    },
  ],
  table: 'topics',
}
```

When an exported topic contains `agentId`, the importer inserts the old exported agent ID into `topics.agent_id`. Because imported agents are assigned new DB IDs and tracked through `clientId`, this old ID does not exist in `agents.id`, so PostgreSQL rejects the topic insert.

### Expected behavior

`topics.agentId` should be remapped through `idMaps.agents` just like `messages.agentId`, so topic imports keep their agent relation without violating the FK.

### Proposed fix

Add the missing relation mapping:

```ts
{
  field: 'agentId',
  sourceTable: 'agents',
}
```

to the `topics` table config, and add a regression test that imports `agents + topics(agentId) + messages(agentId)` and asserts both topic and message point to the newly imported agent ID.

title: [Bug] SSE stream: late event:error (Premature close) after usage/speed across multiple providers
body: ### 📱 Client Type Web (Mobile Browser), Web (Desktop Browser) ### 💻 Operating System Windows ### 📦 Deployment Platform Self hosting Docker ### 📌 Version v2.2.7 ### 🌐 Browser Chrome ### 🐛 What happened? ### Summary When using an OpenAI-compatible provider, LobeHub can emit a server-side SSE `event:error` **after the model output has already completed** and after `usage` / `speed` were sent. This does not reproduce with the official DeepSeek provider in the same LobeHub deployment. It also does not reproduce in other chat apps using the same upstream/provider path. The issue appears specific to LobeHub’s OpenAI-compatible / Responses stream adapter and its handling of late stream close errors. The error was observed after upgrading from v2.2.2 to v2.2.7. ### Observed SSE order Captured raw LobeHub SSE response shows: ```text ... text / reasoning / tool_calls streamed normally event: usage event: speed event: error ``` Error payload: ```json { "body": { "message": "Premature close", "provider": "opencodecodingplan", "model": "deepseek-v4-flash", "errorType": "ProviderBizError" }, "message": "Premature close", "type": "ProviderBizError" } ``` In my capture: event: usage -> line 5866 event: speed -> line 5870 event: error -> line 5874 ### Raw upstream comparison Raw provider stream captured directly from upstream completes normally: - URL: https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions - Model: deepseek-v4-flash - HTTP 200 - Full content received - Usage chunk received - [DONE] received - No provider-side JSON error containing Premature close So this does not look like the provider returning a business error payload. ### Why this looks like a late close handling issue The LobeHub forwarded stream has already received terminal/usage information before the error appears. For Chat Completions: OpenAI SDK Stream -> convertIterableToStream -> createFirstErrorHandleTransformer -> createTokenSpeedCalculator -> createSSEProtocolTransformer -> createCallbacksTransformer For Responses API: client.responses.create(...) -> OpenAIResponsesStream -> convertIterableToStream -> createFirstErrorHandleTransformer -> createTokenSpeedCalculator -> createSSEProtocolTransformer Relevant code paths: - packages/model-runtime/src/core/openaiCompatibleFactory/index.ts - client.chat.completions.create(...) - client.responses.create(...) - packages/model-runtime/src/core/streams/protocol.ts - convertIterableToStream - catches it.next() errors and wraps them as stream error payloads - packages/model-runtime/src/core/streams/openai/openai.ts - OpenAIStream - converts FIRST_CHUNK_ERROR into LobeHub event:error - packages/model-runtime/src/core/streams/openai/responsesStream.ts - OpenAIResponsesStream - same error conversion path for Responses API - apps/server/src/modules/AgentRuntime/RuntimeExecutors.ts - onError stores streamError - after consumeStreamUntilDone(response), any streamError is thrown as fatal ### Suspected root cause The upstream OpenAI-compatible stream may close in a way that the OpenAI SDK treats as Premature close, possibly after terminal content has already been parsed. LobeHub then treats this late iterator exception as a provider business error and emits it to the client as fatal SSE event:error. This seems too strict when: - content already fully streamed - usage already emitted - speed already emitted - terminal/completed event was effectively observed ### Current impact The user sees generation interrupted / network error even though the model output and tool calls completed successfully. In agent/tool-call flows this is especially visible because the assistant step can be persisted with Premature close even when tool messages are successful. ### Conclusion This does not look like a browser/client network issue. It looks like: 1. upstream OpenAI-compatible stream close behavior triggers an SDK iterator Premature close 2. LobeHub stream adapter converts that late close into ProviderBizError 3. RuntimeExecutors / SSE pipeline treats it as fatal even though usage and speed were already sent Most suspicious area: - convertIterableToStream in packages/model-runtime/src/core/streams/protocol.ts - OpenAIStream / OpenAIResponsesStream - RuntimeExecutors.ts post-consumption streamError handling ### 📷 How to reproduce it? Start a chat, select opencodecodingplan deepseek-v4-flash, output contains multiple tool calling or websearch Similar issue also observed when using Responses API with gpt-5.5 Happens more frequently after tool/search calls Other chat apps using the same upstream path does not show this user-visible failure ### 🚦 What it should be? If a stream close/read error occurs after terminal/usage/completed state has already been reached, LobeHub should probably not surface it as a fatal user-visible event:error. Possible behavior: ignore known late close errors after terminal event log them as diagnostics/debug do not mark the assistant message as failed if content/tool calls/usage were already completed ### 📝 Additional Information ### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR? _No response_ ### ✅ Validations - [x] Read the [docs](https://lobehub.com/zh/docs). - [x] Check that there isn't [already an issue](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/issues) that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate. - [x] Make sure this is a LobeChat issue and not a third-party library or provider issue. - [x] Check that this is a concrete bug. title: [Bug] Bedrock provider: builtin model IDs invalid + models() not implemented
body:
## Description

LobeHub's Bedrock provider has two related bugs that make it largely unusable without manual workarounds.

---

## Bug 1: Builtin model IDs use cross-provider prefix not recognized by AWS

**Root cause**: Builtin Bedrock models in `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/bedrock.ts` use `global.anthropic.*` IDs (e.g., `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`), but the AWS Bedrock API requires actual foundation model IDs (e.g., `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`).

**Why it fails**:
- `LobeBedrockAI.resolveModelId()` relies on `modelIdMapping` to translate IDs
- `modelIdMapping` is always `{}` because it's never populated from `getParamsFromPayload()` or `buildPayloadFromKeyVaults()` in `apps/server/src/modules/ModelRuntime/index.ts`
- Result: `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` is sent verbatim to Bedrock → `ValidationException: The provided model identifier is invalid.`

**Relevant code**:
1. `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/bedrock.ts` — models use `global.anthropic.*` IDs
2. `packages/model-runtime/src/providers/bedrock/index.ts:116` — `resolveModelId` does `this.modelIdMapping[model] ?? model` but mapping is always empty
3. `apps/server/src/modules/ModelRuntime/index.ts:220-229` — `getParamsFromPayload` for Bedrock returns `{ accessKeyId, accessKeySecret, region, sessionToken }` without `modelIdMapping`

**Workaround**: Set `AWS_BEDROCK_MODEL_LIST` with actual Bedrock model IDs, but builtin models coexist and cause confusion.

---

## Bug 2: `models()` not implemented → JSON serialization error

**Symptom**: Clicking "Pull Models" button returns `Value is not JSON serializable`.

**Root cause**: `LobeBedrockAI` (implementing `LobeRuntimeAI`) does not implement the `models()` method. When `ModelRuntime.models()` calls `this._runtime.models?.()`, it returns `undefined`, which `NextResponse.json(undefined)` cannot serialize.

**Relevant code**:
1. `packages/model-runtime/src/providers/bedrock/index.ts` — class has `chat()`, `embeddings()`, `generateObject()` but no `models()`
2. `packages/model-runtime/src/core/ModelRuntime.ts:416` — `this._runtime.models?.()` returns `undefined` for Bedrock
3. `src/app/(backend)/webapi/models/[provider]/route.ts:60` — `NextResponse.json(undefined)` fails

**Note**: The `showModelFetcher` button defaults to `true` for Bedrock since the provider card has no `modelList` config to suppress it.

---

## Bug 3: `-all` prefix causes UI panic

Using `AWS_BEDROCK_MODEL_LIST=-all,...` to clear broken builtin models causes the Bedrock model selector to break entirely (likely null/undefined handling issue in the frontend when serverModelLists is empty).

---

## Expected Behavior

1. Builtin Bedrock models should use valid AWS model IDs, OR `modelIdMapping` should be auto-generated from the builtin list
2. `LobeBedrockAI` should implement `models()` (or the route should handle undefined gracefully)
3. Empty model list should not crash the UI

## Environment

- LobeHub version: latest (Next.js 16.2.9)
- Deployment: Docker Compose
- AWS Region: us-west-1

title: [Feature] Matrix protocol integration — IM Gateway support for Matrix homeservers
body:
## 🥰 Feature Description

Add support for Matrix (matrix.org) as an IM Gateway integration in LobeHub, allowing agents to communicate through Matrix rooms and direct messages via both the official Matrix.org homeserver and any self-hosted Matrix homeserver (Synapse, Dendrite, Conduit).

Matrix is a decentralized, open, end-to-end encrypted messaging protocol. It supports federation between servers, meaning a single integration covers the entire Matrix network — whether users are on matrix.org, a company server, or a personal homelab instance.

LobeHub's **IM Gateway** already mentions "Agents where you already chat" as a core concept. Matrix is a natural fit: it works both as a managed cloud service (matrix.org, Element Matrix Services) and as a fully self-hostable stack.

## 🧐 Proposed Solution

Implement a Matrix bot/gateway integration in LobeHub's IM Gateway layer, similar to how Telegram, Slack, or Discord bots are handled. The integration should support:

### Official / managed servers
- **matrix.org** public homeserver (free accounts)
- **Element Matrix Services** (EMS) — managed hosting by Element
- Any other public Matrix homeserver

### Self-hosted homeservers
- **Synapse** (Python, the reference implementation)
- **Dendrite** (Go, lighter footprint)
- **Conduit** (Rust, minimal resource usage, ideal for homelabs)
- Any homeserver compliant with the Matrix Client-Server API spec

### Configuration parameters
1. Homeserver URL (e.g. `https://matrix.org` or `https://matrix.example.com`)
2. Bot access token or username/password login
3. Room IDs to join/listen to, or auto-accept invites
4. Optional: E2EE support via matrix-sdk-crypto or matrix-js-sdk

A reasonable first implementation can use polling (`/sync`) rather than push rules.

## 💡 Use Cases

- **Regular users**: interact with LobeHub agents directly from Element Web, Element Desktop,  or any Matrix client, using their matrix.org or EMS account.
- **Self-hosters**: homelab users running Synapse/Conduit who want agents available on their own federated server, without depending on third-party platforms.
- **Privacy-focused users**: avoid proprietary IM platforms (Telegram, Slack, Discord) while keeping full agent functionality.
- **Organizations**: companies using Element On-Premise or a private Synapse instance for  internal communications can deploy LobeHub agents in their own federated rooms.
- **Bridge power users**: Matrix bridges (WhatsApp, Signal, IRC, XMPP via matrix-appservice) would automatically extend LobeHub agents to those networks.

## 📝 Additional Information

- Matrix spec: https://spec.matrix.org
- Reference bot library (Node.js): https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-js-sdk
- Reference bot library (Python): https://github.com/poljar/matrix-nio
- Public homeserver list: https://servers.joinmatrix.org
- This would differentiate LobeHub from competitors who only support proprietary IM platforms,
  and aligns with LobeHub's self-hosted deployment philosophy (Docker, Vercel, Alibaba Cloud).

title: LM Studio provider should expose and forward max output token setting
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Desktop App (Electron)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📌 Version

2.2.8

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

In self-hosted LobeHub, the LM Studio provider does not appear to expose a configurable maximum output token setting, and LobeHub does not forward max_tokens or max_completion_tokens in /v1/chat/completions requests.
This can cause long assistant responses to stop early even when the local model still has plenty of context available.
Observed LobeHub request payload sent to LM Studio:
```
{
  "model": "...",
  "stream": true,
  "temperature": 1,
  "top_p": 1,
  "thinking": {
    "type": "enabled",
    "budget_tokens": 8192
  },
  "messages": [...]
}
```
There is no output-token field such as:
`"max_tokens": 4096`
or:
`"max_completion_tokens": 4096`
The response stopped before completing the requested final format, while the backend model server reported no context truncation. This makes long tool-agent responses unreliable.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Configure the LM Studio provider.
2. Use an LM Studio model with a large context window.
3. Create or use an agent with tools/MCP enabled.
4. Ask for a structured response long enough to exceed roughly 1k output tokens.
5. Inspect the request LobeHub sends to LM Studio.
6. Observe that the request does not include max_tokens or max_completion_tokens.
7. Observe that the assistant response can stop before the sentinel even though the model server reports no prompt/context truncation.

### 🚦 What it should be?

LobeHub should allow configuring maximum output tokens for the LM Studio provider and should forward that value in the chat completion request.
For LM Studio’s OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions API, this should be sent as:
`"max_tokens": 4096`
If LobeHub uses a provider abstraction, it could expose this as “Max Output Tokens” / “Max Completion Tokens” and map it to the correct provider-specific field.

### 📝 Additional Information

This is not a request to change LM Studio behavior.
The issue is that LobeHub does not expose/pass the output-token parameter for the LM Studio provider.
Context size is not the limiting factor in this case.
The problem is especially visible with tool/MCP agents, because tool schemas and tool results consume context while the final response still needs enough output budget to complete reliably.

Some background tasks can also run near the same time as the main request, such as topic naming, embeddings, memory-related processing, or suggestion-related tasks.
For local model workflows, this creates several problems:

- Extra tool schemas are always sent to the model.
- Prompt size grows significantly.
- Local model VRAM/compute is used by background tasks.
- LM Studio logs become harder to debug.
- Tool agents receive a much larger and noisier tool surface than necessary.
- Safety-sensitive agents have write-capable tools visible even when the workflow does not require them.

In one local MCP/tool-agent test, the main request still included around 60 available tools even after reducing pinned/auto skills. The request contained many built-in tools unrelated to the task.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Run self-hosted LobeHub.
2. Configure a local provider such as LM Studio.
3. Configure an agent with only a small number of intended MCP tools or skills.
4. Send a simple tool-use prompt.
5. Inspect the request sent to the model provider.
6. Observe that built-in LobeHub tools and/or background systems are still present or active even if the user did not intentionally enable them for that agent.

### 🚦 What it should be?

LobeHub should allow users to disable or scope built-in tools and background agents per agent/workspace/provider.
```
Examples of useful controls:
Enable/disable lobe-agent tools
Enable/disable lobe-skills tools
Enable/disable local filesystem tools
Enable/disable web browsing tools
Enable/disable user-memory tools
Enable/disable background topic naming
Enable/disable follow-up suggestions
Enable/disable prompt rewriting
Enable/disable input suggestions
Enable/disable automatic memory processing
```
Ideally, tool exposure should be minimal by default and explicit per agent.

### 📝 Additional Information

This matters especially for local model users, where every extra tool schema consumes context and compute.
For tool/MCP agents, reducing the visible tool surface improves:

- reliability
- instruction following
- schema obedience
- safety
- latency
- debugging clarity

This is not only a performance issue. It also affects behavior because the model must reason over many unrelated tools, including tools with write capability, even during read-only workflows.

title: Memory injection is inconsistent during multi-step tool calls
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Desktop App (Electron)

### 💻 Operating System

Windows

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📌 Version

2.2.8

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

During a multi-step MCP/tool workflow, LobeHub did not inject <user_memory> into the initial model request, but did inject it into later requests after a tool call had already occurred.
This means the model’s context changes mid-turn. In a tool workflow, that can affect reasoning, tool selection, or final response behavior after the agent has already started executing the task.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Run self-hosted LobeHub.
2. Enable Memory.
3. Use an agent with MCP/tool calling enabled.
4. Send a prompt that requires at least two model turns, such as discovery followed by a read-only tool call.
5. Inspect the model provider request logs.
6. Compare the first request with later requests in the same tool loop.
7. Observe that <user_memory> may be absent initially but present after a tool result.

### 🚦 What it should be?

Memory injection should be consistent for the entire turn.
Either:

- include memory from the first model request, or
- do not inject memory until the next user turn.

It should not appear halfway through an active tool loop unless this behavior is intentional and documented.

### 📝 Additional Information

This is especially risky for compliance tests and tool agents, because memory may contain preferences or stale facts that the first tool call did not account for.

suggestion-related tasks

### 🚦 What it should be?

LobeHub should offer a setting such as:
`Defer background model tasks during active agent turns`
or:
`Queue side tasks until main response completes`
This would let local users choose reliability over convenience.

### 📝 Additional Information

This matters most for local models, where background requests may share the same GPU, same model slot, and same provider logs as the active agent.

具体场景：我们搭建了一个 Router Agent（中枢调度员(专业)），其职责是根据用户问题识别领域，然后通过 callAgent 调度对应的子 Agent（如命理大师、商业大师等）。但 callAgent 在云端始终无法完成，导致 Router Agent 被迫回退用自己的知识回答问题，完全失去了"调度"的价值。

复现步骤
步骤 1： 在工作区创建两个 Agent

Agent A（调度器）：配置 callAgent 工具（lobe-agent 插件），System Prompt 要求它调度 Agent B
Agent B（目标子 Agent）：命理大师，专门处理八字命理

*.txt
Plaintext
callAgent(agentId="agt_NTUXyRn4DyNh", instruction="介绍你的能力范围")

title: bug: searchUserMemory tool fails with "Premature close" in sandbox due to strict network/env isolation
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Desktop App (Electron)

### 💻 Operating System

Ubuntu, macOS

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker

### 📌 Version

v.2.2.8

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

The `searchUserMemory` tool fails to function within the chat sandbox, throwing an `Invalid response body... Premature close` error when trying to fetch embeddings or models from OpenAI. Detailed diagnostics show that while the main server Docker container has perfect network connectivity to `api.openai.com` and the API key is completely valid, the internal plugin sandbox runner isolates the execution context so strictly that it drops the connection stream early or blocks internal tools from reaching OpenAI embeddings endpoint.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Configure LobeHub via Docker with a valid OpenAI API key and explicitly inject embedding models via environment variables:
   `DEFAULT_FILES_CONFIG="embedding_model=openai/text-embedding-3-small,query_mode=full_text"`
2. Verify that memory operations work perfectly fine outside the chat UI using the CLI (`lh memory create` and `lh memory list` succeed flawlessly).
3. Open any chat session in the LobeHub UI and trigger a workflow that invokes the `searchUserMemory` tool.
4. The tool execution fails immediately with the following error: `Failed to fetch models: Invalid response body while trying to fetch https://api.openai.com/v1/models: Premature close`.

### 🚦 What it should be?

The plugin/tool sandbox runtime should either correctly inherit the main server process environment/proxy variables securely or correctly proxy embedding requests without prematurely closing the TCP stream. The chat-based memory search tool should be able to reach the configured embedding endpoints just as successfully as the `lh` CLI does.

### 📝 Additional Information

We performed deep technical isolation tests inside the container to rule out network or API key issues:

1. **Environment Verification:**
   Running `docker compose exec lobe env | grep DEFAULT_FILES_CONFIG` confirms the configuration is correctly present on the host container:
   `DEFAULT_FILES_CONFIG=embedding_model=openai/text-embedding-3-small,query_mode=full_text`

2. **Native Container Network Test:**
   Since `curl` is missing in the minimal production image, we ran a direct HTTPS request to OpenAI using the container's native Node.js runtime to check SSL/TLS and routing:
   ```bash
   docker compose exec lobe node -e "
   const https = require('https');
   https.get('[https://api.openai.com/v1/models](https://api.openai.com/v1/models)', (res) => {
     console.log('STATUS:', res.statusCode);
     console.log('HEADERS:', JSON.stringify(res.headers, null, 2));
   }).on('error', (e) => {
     console.error('ERROR:', e.message);
   });
   "
Response received:
STATUS: 401
HEADERS: {
  "date": "Wed, 24 Jun 2026 22:14:19 GMT",
  "content-type": "application/json",
  "connection": "keep-alive",
  "server": "cloudflare",
  "www-authenticate": "Bearer realm=\"OpenAI API\"",
  "openai-version": "2020-10-01"
  ...
}

This strictly proves that the container itself has flawless routing and handles TLS handshakes with OpenAI beautifully (getting a clean 401 response instead of a connection drop). The Premature close issue is purely an internal stream-handling bug within LobeHub's sandbox architecture (clisandbox).



### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?

None

title: Knowledge file resources pass docs_* IDs to chunk actions and semantic search
body:
### 📱 Client Type

Web (Desktop Browser)

### 💻 Operating System

macOS

### 📦 Deployment Platform

Self hosting Docker / local development

### 📌 Version

canary `d6935cd13050355efd60000d8c18bdf01ab20794`

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome

### 🐛 What happened?

File-backed knowledge resources can expose a document id (`docs_*`) as their item `id`, while chunking, embedding retry, and semantic search paths expect the real file id (`file_*`).

For example, a knowledge item can look like this:

```json
{
  "id": "docs_B2x3zYnRUttCGMvN",
  "documentId": "docs_B2x3zYnRUttCGMvN",
  "fileId": "file_TaLrbfD61pNv",
  "sourceType": "file",
  "chunkingStatus": "success",
  "embeddingStatus": "success",
  "finishEmbedding": true
}
```

The UI then sends payloads like:

```json
{"fileIds":["docs_B2x3zYnRUttCGMvN"],"query":"..."}
```

or retries embedding with:

```json
{"id":"docs_Yfov9wsQ8lvLEHlR","type":"embedding"}
```

Those requests do not target the underlying `file_*` record. The result is that retry embedding can silently do nothing, and semantic search can return no useful result even when chunking/embedding status is already successful.

Code path observed on canary:

- `packages/database/src/repositories/knowledge/index.ts` returns file resources with `COALESCE(d.id, f.id) as id`, plus `f.id as file_id` and `d.id as document_id`.
- `src/features/ResourceManager/components/Explorer/ListView/ListItem/FileListItemActions.tsx` passes `id={id}` to `ChunksBadge`.
- `src/features/ResourceManager/components/Explorer/ListView/ListItem/ChunkTag.tsx` calls `embeddingChunks([id])`, `reParseFile(id)`, `reEmbeddingChunks(id)`, and `openChunkDrawer(id)`.
- `packages/database/src/models/chunk.ts` semantic search filters by `fileChunks.fileId`, so `fileIds` must be `file_*` ids.

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Upload a file that creates both a `files` row and a linked `documents` row.
2. Open the knowledge/resource list and inspect the returned item. For file-backed documents, `id` may be `docs_*` while `fileId` is `file_*`.
3. Click retry embedding, open the chunks drawer and run semantic search, or call `chunk.semanticSearch` with the `id` from the list item.
4. Observe that the request uses `docs_*` as a file id. Retry embedding can no-op, and semantic search can return empty results.
5. Repeating the same semantic search with the real `fileId` (`file_*`) targets the chunk records correctly.

### 🚦 What it should be?

For file-backed resources, chunking, embedding retry, chunk drawer, deletion/reparse where applicable, and semantic search should consistently use the underlying `fileId` (`file_*`) when calling file/chunk APIs.

A possible fix is to pass `fileId ?? id` from the resource list action layer into chunk-related actions for `sourceType: "file"`. Server-side endpoints could also defensively resolve `docs_*` to the linked `documents.fileId` for compatibility.

### 📝 Additional Information

This does not appear to be a provider-side embedding error. It is an ID mismatch between resource list items and file/chunk APIs. I am willing to submit a PR to fix this.

### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?

Yes, I am willing to submit a PR

title: Custom skill scripts fail because relative paths are not resolved to extracted skill root
body:
### 🐛 Bug Description

Custom LobeHub Skills are installed/extracted correctly in the Desktop app, but when a skill instruction tries to execute a script via a relative path, the runner does not resolve the path relative to the extracted skill root.

In my case, the skill script exists under LobeHub Desktop's skill storage directory, but execution fails because the command is run from `/`, causing the relative path to resolve incorrectly.

### 🔄 Reproduction Steps

1. Install/import a custom skill named `dazhu-blog`.
2. The skill contains a Python script at:

   ```text
   dazhu-blog/scripts/dazhu_blog.py
   ```

3. Activate/use the skill from a conversation.
4. The skill instruction attempts to run a command like:

   ```bash
   python3 dazhu-blog/scripts/dazhu_blog.py ...
   ```

5. The command fails because the current working directory is `/`, so Python tries to open:

   ```text
   //dazhu-blog/scripts/dazhu_blog.py
   ```

6. The actual LobeHub Desktop extracted skill path is under:

   ```text
   ~/Library/Application Support/LobeHub/lobehub-storage/file-storage/skills/extracted/<hash>/dazhu-blog/scripts/dazhu_blog.py
   ```

### ✅ Expected Behavior

When a skill is activated/executed, relative paths in the skill instructions should resolve relative to the extracted skill root, or the runtime should expose a reliable variable/environment value for the skill root directory.

For example, running:

```bash
python3 dazhu-blog/scripts/dazhu_blog.py ...
```

should work if `dazhu-blog/scripts/dazhu_blog.py` exists inside the installed/extracted skill package.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The command is executed with `/` as the working directory, so the relative script path is resolved as:

```text
//dazhu-blog/scripts/dazhu_blog.py
```

and fails with:

```text
python3: can't open file '//dazhu-blog/scripts/dazhu_blog.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

However, the script does exist in LobeHub's Desktop skill storage:

```text
~/Library/Application Support/LobeHub/lobehub-storage/file-storage/skills/extracted/<hash>/dazhu-blog/scripts/dazhu_blog.py
```

### 🖥️ Environment

- LobeHub Desktop app on macOS
- Skill storage observed at:

  ```text
  ~/Library/Application Support/LobeHub/lobehub-storage/file-storage/skills/extracted/
  ```

- Custom skill: `dazhu-blog`
- Script path inside skill package: `dazhu-blog/scripts/dazhu_blog.py`

### 🔎 Related Issue

This seems related to or a macOS/Desktop variant of:

- https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/issues/12883

That issue was closed as not planned, but this appears to be a general Desktop skill runner path-resolution problem and still affects current custom skill usage.

### 💡 Suggested Fix

Possible fixes:

1. Run skill commands with the extracted skill root as the working directory.
2. Provide an environment variable such as `LOBE_SKILL_ROOT` or `SKILL_ROOT` during skill execution.
3. Rewrite/normalize skill-relative file references before passing commands to the local runner.
4. Document the required way for custom skills to reference bundled scripts if relative paths are intentionally unsupported.

### What it does

Verifly is an agent-native **email-verification API**. The MCP server lets any
MCP-capable agent (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cline, etc.) verify single
addresses in real time, verify/clean whole lists, run async bulk jobs, extract
addresses from free-form text, check sending-domain health (MX/SPF/DMARC), and
read its own credit/usage — all as first-class agent tools. It is built for
autonomous agents: a key can be self-registered programmatically and every tool
returns structured verdicts (valid / invalid / risky / unknown) with flags and a
send/reject recommendation.

### Install method — Streamable HTTP (hosted, recommended)

- **Endpoint:** `https://verifly.email/mcp`
- **Transport:** `streamable-http` (stateless)
- **Auth:** HTTP Bearer — `Authorization: Bearer vf_<your_api_key>` (get a key at https://verifly.email)
